title: Programmatically set selections fail for empty selection
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

The example in https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/data/st.dataframe titled: "Example 2: Programmatically set selections" does not work if we try with empty selections.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st
from numpy.random import default_rng as rng

df = pd.DataFrame(rng(0).standard_normal((12, 5)), columns=["a", "b", "c", "d", "e"])

if st.button("Select the first row"):
    st.session_state["data"] = {"selection": {"rows": [0], "columns": [], "cells": []}}
if st.button("Select no row"):
    st.session_state["data"] = {"selection": {"rows": [], "columns": [], "cells": []}}

event = st.dataframe(
    df,
    key="data",
    on_select="rerun",
    selection_mode=["single-row"],
)

st.code(event.selection)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the code
2. Select a row
3. Click on the button "Select the first row", it works as expected
4. Select a row again
5. Click on the button "Select no row", the dataframe selection state is empty but the table keeps the previous selection.

### Expected Behavior

The row selection should match the dataframe selection state and be empty.

### Current Behavior

The dataframe selection state is empty but the table keeps the previous selection and is not empty.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.63.0
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: WSL Docker
- Browser: Edge


### Additional Information

I remember it worked in Streamlit version 1.57.0 but I am not sure, I may be mistaken.

title: st.multiselect without key drops the user's selection when options come in a different order on rerun
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

If `st.multiselect` has no `key` and its `options` list comes back in a different order on the next run, every selection the user makes is thrown away. The widget briefly shows the new chip, then flickers back to the default. Passing `sorted(options)` makes it work, and so does setting any `key`.

The order of options is often unstable in real apps: `list(set(...))`, `df[col].unique()` after a filter, SQL queries without `ORDER BY`, dict/set unions, and "move selected to top" patterns.

Similar reports were closed as expected behavior (#5995, #8496). #11277 fixed the case where `key` is set. The keyless case still resets, even though multiselect doesn't need it to.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import random
import streamlit as st

opts = ["apple", "banana", "cherry", "date", "elderberry"]
random.shuffle(opts)  # stands in for list(set(...)), an unordered query, etc.

sel = st.multiselect("Fruits", opts)  # works with sorted(opts) or key="fruits"
st.write(sel)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app.
2. Pick any option in the multiselect.

### Expected Behavior

The option stays selected, because the set of options didn't change and only their order did.

### Current Behavior

The chip appears for a moment and then disappears. `sel` is `[]`. Measured with `AppTest` on 1.64.0:

| options | key | value after select | value after next rerun |
|---|---|---|---|
| sorted | no | `['banana']` | `['banana']` |
| sorted | yes | `['banana']` | `['banana']` |
| shuffled | no | `[]` | `[]` |
| shuffled | yes | `['banana']` | `['banana']` |

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info


Field | Value
-- | --
Streamlit version | 1.64.0
Python version | 3.12
Operating System | Linux
Browser | Chrome



### Additional Information

### Why this happens

In `lib/streamlit/elements/widgets/multiselect.py`, when there is no `key`, the widget ID is a hash of the widget parameters, including the **ordered** list of formatted options and the **indices** of the defaults:

```python
element_id = compute_and_register_element_id(
    widget_name,
    user_key=key,
    key_as_main_identity={"max_selections", "accept_new_options"},
    ...
    options=formatted_options,   # order-sensitive
    default=default_values,      # indices into options, also order-sensitive
    ...
)
```

With a new order, the ID changes on every run. When the user clicks, the frontend sends the value under the old ID. The rerun registers a widget with a new ID and no stored state, so it falls back to `default`. The frontend then mounts a new component with that ID, which is the flicker.

For multiselect, including the order isn't needed. The value travels as a list of **formatted option strings** (`string_array_value`), not indices. `MultiSelectSerde.deserialize` maps strings back with `formatted_options.index(v)`, and `validate_and_sync_multiselect_value_with_options` already handles options that change. The same selection means the same thing in any order.

### Proposed fix

Hash the options without regard to order, and hash defaults by value rather than by index:

```diff
             dg=self.dg,
             label=label,
-            options=formatted_options,
-            default=default_values,
+            # Values are stored as formatted strings rather than indices, so the
+            # order of options doesn't change their meaning. Hash options
+            # order-insensitively so reordering them doesn't reset the widget.
+            options=sorted(formatted_options),
+            default=[formatted_options[i] for i in default_values],
             help=help,
             max_selections=max_selections,
```

`proto.options` and `proto.default` are unchanged, so the display order still follows what the user passed. Only the identity hash changes. With this patch applied to 1.64.0, all four rows in the table above keep the selection, including with `default=[...]` set.

Notes:
- Existing keyless multiselects get new IDs once after upgrading. That's the same one-time reset any ID-scheme change causes.
- `selectbox`, `pills`, and `segmented_control` probably need the same change wherever they send values as strings. I haven't checked those.

title: Freshness signal: refresh cached data only when the source actually changes
body:
## Summary

Let a cached data source declare a cheap "has the source changed?" probe, so
Streamlit re-runs the expensive query (and updates dependent fragments) **only
when the underlying data actually changed** — instead of on a blind timer. This
is the event-driven counterpart to timer-based refresh.

## Why?

Timer-based refresh (`@st.fragment(run_every=…)`, or a server-side scheduled
refresh) fires on a fixed clock regardless of whether anything changed. For an
expensive query that forces a bad tradeoff:

- **Poll fast** → the heavy query re-runs every interval even when the data is
  identical, wasting warehouse/API cost.
- **Poll slow** → users stare at stale data between ticks.

Sources usually expose something *cheap* that reveals whether they changed — a
version token, an ETag, a `MAX(updated_at)`, a Snowflake stream or
change-tracking timestamp. There's no built-in way to poll that cheap signal
often and re-run the expensive work only when it moves.

## How?

Attach a cheap freshness function to a cached data source. Streamlit checks the
freshness token; when it changes, it invalidates the cache and re-runs the
fragments that read it. When it's unchanged, the cached value is served and no
expensive work runs.

Sketch (names illustrative):

```python
def orders_version():
    # Cheap probe — cache invalidates when this value changes.
    return conn.query("SELECT MAX(updated_at) FROM orders")

@st.cache_data(freshness=orders_version)
def load_orders():
    return conn.query("SELECT * FROM orders")   # expensive; runs only on change

@st.fragment(run_every="5s")
def orders_panel():
    df = load_orders()      # cheap probe each poll; heavy query only when changed
    st.line_chart(df, x="ts", y="orders")

orders_panel()
```

title: selectbox clears on rerun if format_func returns new value, even with the same options.
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Streamlit selectbox gets re-created when formatted labels change, discarding user output. 

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
import time

if "start_time" not in st.session_state:
  st.session_state["start_time"] = time.time()

start_time = st.session_state["start_time"]

option = st.selectbox(
  label="Single-select Option",
  options=["A", "B", "C"],
  format_func=lambda option: f"{option}: {int(time.time()-start_time)} seconds ago",
  key="option",
  index=None
)

st.write("Single-select Option:", option)

option2 = st.multiselect(
  label="Multi-select Options",
  options=["D", "E", "F"],
  format_func=lambda option: f"{option}: {int(time.time()-start_time)} seconds ago",
  key="option2",
)

st.write("Multi-select Options:", option2)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. In Single-select Option, Select "A"
2. In Multi-select Options, Select "D"
3. In Multi-select Options, Select "E"
4. In Multi-select Options, Select "F"
5. Wait 1 second
6. Click out of the multi select option dropdown

### Expected Behavior

It should have option A selected for 'Single-select Option', and options D, E and F selected for 'Multi-select Options'

### Current Behavior

Single-select option and multi-select options have nothing selected.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.63
- Python version: Python 3.14.7
- Operating System: Ubuntu 26.4
- Browser: Firefox 156.0.1 


### Additional Information

Proposed solution 1: Do not clear the selectbox if the selected options still exist.

Proposed solution 2: Update the selectbox and multiselect documentation with a warning about this. Currently the documentation for format_func says: "This has no impact on the return value of the command." which I would say is incorrect in this case.

This issue seems closely related to issues #11277 and #11268. They seemed to be closed for being fixed in 1.54.1.dev20260204, though I am still seeing this unexpected behavior in 1.63.

Thank you so much for your work on streamlit. It is very amazing!

title: `st.dataframe` toolbar buttons are 22.4px, below the WCAG 2.2 24px minimum target size (axe `target-size`)
body:
### Checklist
- [x] I have searched the existing issues for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary
The hover toolbar that `st.dataframe` draws (Show/hide columns, Download as CSV, Search, Fullscreen)
renders each button at 22.4 x 22.4 CSS px, and the buttons sit next to each other, so axe-core's
`target-size` rule (impact: serious, WCAG 2.2 AA, SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)) fails. Cause:
`StyledElementToolbarButton` in `frontend/lib/src/components/shared/BaseButton/styled-components.ts`
(1.64.0, line ~524) sets `padding: theme.spacing.twoXS` and `minHeight: "unset"` around a small icon.

### Reproducible Code Example
Same app as above (the `st.dataframe` line is enough).

### Steps To Reproduce
1. `streamlit run app.py`
2. Hover the dataframe so the toolbar appears.
3. Run axe-core 4.13 with the `wcag22aa` tag.

### Expected Behavior
Each toolbar button is at least 24 x 24 CSS px (or spaced so a 24px circle around each does not overlap
another target).

### Current Behavior
```
target-size (serious, wcag22aa, wcag258) — 4 nodes
<button kind="elementToolbar" data-testid="stBaseButton-elementToolbar" aria-label="Show/hide columns" class="st-emotion-cache-18ac3gt eqzt73c20">
  Target has insufficient size (22.4px by 22.4px, should be at least 24px by 24px)
<button ... aria-label="Download as CSV" ...>   (same)
<button ... aria-label="Search" ...>            (same)
<button ... aria-label="Fullscreen" ...>        (same)
```

### Suggested fix
Give `StyledElementToolbarButton` `minWidth: "1.5rem"` and `minHeight: "1.5rem"` (24px) instead of
`minHeight: "unset"`, or raise the padding one step. The toolbar is already an overlay above the element,
so the extra 1.6px per button does not move page layout. The same styled button is used by other element
toolbars (charts, `st.data_editor`), which would all pass with the one change.

In the same minimal app, axe also reports `target-size` on the `st.date_input` month/day spinbutton
segments (17.9 x 19.6px); that may deserve its own look but is secondary.

### Is this a regression?
- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.
- [x] No.

### Debug info
- Streamlit version: 1.64.0 (latest)
- Python version: 3.12
- OS: Linux (CI) and Windows 11
- Browser: Chromium (Playwright bundled)
- axe-core: 4.13.0

title: Runtime errors in Streamlit apps on HF Spaces rose 12.4% → 31.7% for the 2026 cohort while other SDKs fell
body:
Not a reproducible bug report — a signal from population data that may point at one, and I can't tell from the outside whether the cause is Streamlit or the Hugging Face runtime image.

I enumerated the complete public Hugging Face Spaces catalogue (1,458,692 Spaces) using the `runtime.stage` field HF exposes, and split permanent failures by SDK and creation year.

**`BUILD_ERROR` is falling for every SDK — that part looks healthy.** But `RUNTIME_ERROR` diverges sharply for Streamlit in the 2026 cohort:

| SDK | 2024 | 2025 | 2026 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **streamlit** | 18.1% | **12.4%** | **31.7%** |
| gradio | 47.1% | 27.0% | 20.8% |
| docker | 31.6% | 19.5% | 20.5% |

Gradio and Docker fell or stayed flat over the same period. Streamlit's rate went from 12.4% to 31.7%.

The failure mode also inverted. Among broken Streamlit Spaces created in 2025: 7,991 `BUILD_ERROR` vs 4,582 `RUNTIME_ERROR`. In 2026: **653 `BUILD_ERROR` vs 5,614 `RUNTIME_ERROR`.** Builds started succeeding and apps started crashing instead.

**Checks I ran before posting, because the obvious explanations would each invalidate this:**

- *Bulk uploaders?* No. The top-10 authors account for 2.3% of the 2026 Streamlit cohort, and excluding them entirely moves the rate from 36.6% to 37.1%. It is spread across 12,432 distinct authors.
- *Just young Spaces still settling?* Newer cohorts are consistently *less* broken across every SDK, so a worse young cohort runs against the trend rather than with it. Separately, 300 error-state Spaces re-queried individually with retries were 300/300 still broken with none recovered, so these are not transient.
- *An age artifact?* Age-standardising Streamlit to Gradio's creation-year distribution moves it 43.50% → 41.16%, so the cohort effect here isn't age composition.

**What I can't determine from outside:** whether this is a Streamlit change, a change in the Streamlit runtime image HF builds, or an interaction between the two. HF controls the Space container, so it may not be yours at all — I've filed the general Spaces census with them separately at huggingface/hub-docs#2743.

If it is useful, I can produce the list of affected Space IDs so someone can look at actual tracebacks, which is the thing this analysis can't reach.

Data (1.46M rows, one row per Space): https://huggingface.co/datasets/Ashsinha1/hf-spaces-census
Method and code: https://github.com/ashishsinha1602/dataset-integrity-audit

title: Periodic server-driven data refresh shared across sessions (vs. per-session run_every)
body:
## Summary

Provide a way to refresh a data source on a **server-side schedule** — computed
once for the whole app and pushed to every session currently viewing it —
instead of each session running its own `run_every` timer and recomputing the
same query independently. This is the shared "the dashboard refreshes every
minute and everyone sees the latest" pattern that live/ops dashboards need.

## Why?

`@st.fragment(run_every=…)` already gives time-driven updates, but the timer and
the computation are **per session**: with _N_ viewers on the same dashboard you
get _N_ timers and _N_ executions of the same query every interval. A refresh
that is cheap for one user becomes _N×_ load on the warehouse/API for a shared
internal tool.

`@st.cache_data` dedupes the *computation* across sessions, but nothing *drives*
a periodic refresh or *wakes* the sessions when a new value lands — today
`run_every` is the driver, and it's per session. The missing piece is a refresh
that runs once for the whole app and updates every session viewing it.

## How?

Mark a cached data source to refresh on a fixed interval, centrally for the
whole app. Any fragment that reads it shows the current value and re-renders when
a new one lands.

Sketch (names illustrative):

```python
# The value refreshes centrally every 60s; sessions read the current value and
# rerun when a new one lands — no per-session timer, one shared computation.
@st.cache_data(refresh_every="60s")
def latest_metrics():
    return run_warehouse_query()

@st.fragment
def kpis():
    df = latest_metrics()          # returns the current cached value immediately
    st.metric("Orders", len(df))
    st.line_chart(df, x="ts", y="orders")

kpis()
```

## Additional Context

- Split out from [#12980](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12980)
  ("real-time chart updates without rerunning the entire script"), which is being
  closed now that fragments (`run_every`), `st.rerun(scope=…)`, and element
  diffing cover the original per-session/live-update and flicker concerns.
- Related in-flight work: the non-blocking background execution spec
  ([#17067](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17067)) covers shared,
  off-thread cached computation; scheduled/recurring refresh is called out there
  as not-yet-built.
- Companion gap: a **freshness signal**
  ([#17141](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17141)) — a cheap "did
  the source change?" probe (e.g. Snowflake change-tracking / `LAST_ALTERED` /
  `MAX(updated_at)`) to drive **event-driven** invalidation instead of a blind
  timer. That's the push counterpart to this timer-based one.

title: `aria-expanded` on elements with no role: sidebar `<section>` and `st.date_input` field fail axe `aria-allowed-attr` (WCAG 4.1.2)
body:
### Checklist
- [x] I have searched the existing issues for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary
Every page of an app with a sidebar fails axe-core's `aria-allowed-attr` rule (impact: critical, WCAG 2.0 A,
SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value), and so does every `st.date_input`. In both cases `aria-expanded` is set on an
element whose role does not support it:

1. The sidebar is rendered as a plain `<section>` with no accessible name, so it has no landmark role that
   supports `aria-expanded`. `frontend/app/src/components/Sidebar/Sidebar.tsx` (1.64.0, line ~265):
   `aria-expanded={!isCollapsed}` on the `Resizable` rendered as `StyledSidebar`.
2. The date input's field is a `<div>` with no role carrying `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded`.
   `frontend/lib/src/components/widgets/DateInput/SingleDateInput.tsx` (1.64.0, line ~553); the same pattern
   is in `RangeDateInput.tsx`.

Assistive technology ignores (or mis-announces) state on an element it cannot map to a role, so the
expanded/collapsed state is not conveyed, and automated audits (axe, Lighthouse) report a critical failure
that app authors cannot fix from Python.

### Reproducible Code Example
```python
import datetime
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st

st.sidebar.write("Sidebar content")
st.date_input("Start date", datetime.date(2026, 1, 1))
st.dataframe(pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2, 3], "b": ["x", "y", "z"]}))
```

### Steps To Reproduce
1. `streamlit run app.py`
2. Run axe-core 4.13 (e.g. `@axe-core/playwright` with tags `wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa, wcag22aa`)
   against the page, at 1280px or 390px wide.

### Expected Behavior
No `aria-allowed-attr` violations.

### Current Behavior
```
aria-allowed-attr (critical, wcag2a, wcag412) — 2 nodes
<section class="stSidebar st-emotion-cache-1kss9tm e16xr0mu0" data-testid="stSidebar" aria-expanded="true" style="position: relative; ...">
  ARIA attribute is not allowed: aria-expanded="true"
<div aria-keyshortcuts="Alt+ArrowDown" aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-expanded="false" data-testid="stDateInputField" class="st-emotion-cache-11mhraf ekyilc22">
  ARIA attribute is not allowed: aria-expanded="false"
```
(At 390px the sidebar starts collapsed and the same node reports `aria-expanded="false"`.)

### Suggested fix
- **Sidebar:** put the state on the control, not the region. Remove `aria-expanded` from the `<section>`;
  set `aria-expanded` + `aria-controls="<sidebar id>"` on the collapse/expand buttons
  (`stSidebarCollapseButton` / `stExpandSidebarButton`), which already carry `aria-label`s since #14563.
  Optionally give the section an accessible name (`aria-label="Sidebar"`) so it becomes a `region` landmark.
- **Date input:** follow the React Aria DatePicker pattern the widget is now built on: the field is
  `role="group"` (labelled by the widget label) and the popup state lives on the element that opens the
  calendar. Either move `aria-haspopup` / `aria-expanded` / `aria-controls` / `aria-keyshortcuts` to a
  calendar toggle `<button>`, or, if the whole field must stay the trigger, give it a role that supports
  them. (It contains spinbuttons, so `role="button"` would nest interactive content; a separate button is
  the clean option.)

### Is this a regression?
- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.
- [x] No — sidebar has had it for several releases; the date input form arrived with the non-BaseWeb
  DateInput (#16460, 1.62).

### Debug info
- Streamlit version: 1.64.0 (latest)
- Python version: 3.12
- OS: Linux (CI, Chromium via Playwright) and Windows 11 (Chromium)
- Browser: Chromium (Playwright bundled)
- axe-core: 4.13.0

### Additional Information
Found by a WCAG 2.2 AA gate that runs axe on every page of several Streamlit apps at 390px and 1280px;
these are the only `aria-allowed-attr` findings left in those apps and none is reachable from app code.

title: Add `max_stale` parameter to `refresh_mode="background"` for configurable stale grace window
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the existing issues for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

When using `refresh_mode="background"` on `st.cache_data` / `st.cache_resource`, the stale grace window is fixed at 1×TTL (hard expiry at 2×TTL). This means an app idle overnight (longer than 2×TTL) has its cache evicted and the first morning user blocks on a cold miss.

A `max_stale` parameter would let users configure the stale grace window independently from TTL:

```python
@st.cache_data(ttl="2m", max_stale="12h", refresh_mode="background")
def load_data():
    return expensive_query()
```

This separates two concerns: **how often to refresh** (`ttl="2m"`) from **how long stale data is acceptable** (`max_stale="12h"`). Users who want frequent freshness checks but never want to block get exactly that.

### Why?

From [#11050](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11050) (comment by @itsToggle):

> Is there any way that we can influence the "2 × ttl" background cache timeout? In my use case I want a short ttl so the values are updated often, but I never want my users to have to wait for a response. I would like to set the ttl to something like 2 minutes, but the oldest background cache that's allowed to be served can be much older than four minutes.

This is also the more practical solution for the "first user of the day" problem compared to cron scheduling, since it does not require an always-on server and works on scale-to-zero deployments.

### How?

The [background refresh spec](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/specs/2026-04-08-cache-background-refresh/product-spec.md) already calls this out as future work:

> **`max_stale` parameter**: Explicitly configure the stale grace window (default: equal to `ttl`), e.g. `ttl="1h", max_stale="12h"` to serve stale data across an overnight idle gap without blocking the first morning user

### Additional Context

- Related (closed): [#5871](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/5871), [#11050](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11050)

title: st.user is empty in apps that use an external host auth token, because the token shares a subprotocol slot with XSRF
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

The frontend sends either a host auth token or the XSRF cookie in one `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` entry, and the host auth token wins when both exist. Because of that, an app that receives an external auth token from its host page cannot also send the XSRF token. The server cannot validate the token for those handshakes, so it does not read the signed user cookie and `st.user` stays empty.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

st.write(st.user)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Serve the app to a host page that sets `useExternalAuthToken: true` in `/_stcore/host-config`.
2. Configure an `[auth]` section so the app can sign a user in.
3. Leave `server.enableXsrfProtection` at its default value of `true`.
4. Sign in and let the host page pass its auth token to the app.
5. Read `st.user` in the app and see that it holds no user fields.

### Expected Behavior

An app should be able to send both the host auth token and the XSRF token on the handshake, so host-auth deployments get user identity without turning XSRF protection off.

### Current Behavior

`WebsocketConnection.getSessionTokens` builds the second subprotocol entry as `hostAuthToken ?? xsrfCookie ?? "PLACEHOLDER_AUTH_TOKEN"`. The server reads that one entry as the XSRF token (`_parse_subprotocols` in `lib/streamlit/web/server/starlette/starlette_websocket.py`). A host auth token in that slot fails `validate_xsrf_token`, so the handler skips the signed user cookie.

The handshake itself still succeeds, because an embed is same-origin and XSRF admission only applies to cross-origin handshakes. Only identity is affected.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.61.1 and `develop`
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: Any
- Browser: Any

### Additional Information

Split out of #16476, which made the XSRF token admission control for cross-origin WebSocket handshakes. That change documents this limitation in the `server.enableXsrfProtection` help text. Options worth weighing: carry both tokens in distinct subprotocol entries, or validate the host auth token on a separate path.

title: Keyed persist_state=None remount can reset the UI while st.session_state[key] still holds the previous value
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

A keyed `persist_state=None` widget that has already registered, is then hidden, then shown again can render the widget default while `st.session_state[key]` still holds the previous value on that remount run. A follow-up rerun overwrites session state with the default. Unmount should reset **both** the UI and `st.session_state[key]` in the same run (#3512).

This is a follow-up to #17106 / #17093. That PR syncs delayed first mount to a leftover pre-registration user key. This issue is the already-registered remount path: unmount cleanup has dropped widget-id state, but a leftover user-key entry can leave the two sides out of sync for one run.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

st.session_state.setdefault("input2", "input 2")
st.session_state.setdefault("input3", "input 3")

select = st.selectbox("select delayed input", ["A", "B"])
if select == "A":
    value = st.text_input("input 2", key="input2")
else:
    value = st.text_input("input 3", key="input3")

st.write("widget return:", repr(value))
st.write("session_state input2:", repr(st.session_state.get("input2")))
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Load the app. Input 2 is shown on first load with `"input 2"`.
2. Switch the selectbox to B.
3. Optionally edit input 3 and press Enter.
4. Switch back to A.
5. Compare the input 2 field with the printed `st.session_state.get("input2")` value, then press `r`.

### Expected Behavior

After the registered widget remounts, both the rendered input and `st.session_state["input2"]` are the widget default (empty) on that same run. A follow-up rerun is not required to sync them.

A user key written while the widget had **never** registered remains ordinary session state: delayed first mount (and leftover-key remount after edit/hide) should still adopt that stored value on both sides. `persist_state="session"` / `"page"` (same page) should still remount the last edit.

### Current Behavior

After switching back to A (especially after editing the sibling input 3), the input 2 **field is empty** while `st.session_state.get("input2")` still prints `"input 2"` for that run. A follow-up rerun clears the printed backend as well.

Without the sibling edit, A→B→A can keep UI and backend aligned at `"input 2"`. Either interpretation of leftover keys should keep UI and printed state in sync; the #3512 unmount rule for an already-registered `persist_state=None` widget is that both sides reset in the same run.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: current develop / #17106
- Python version: 3.13
- Operating System: macOS
- Browser: Chromium (Playwright)

### Additional Information

Found during QA of https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17106#issuecomment-5813147965.

Related:

- #3512 — unmount should reset both the widget UI and the Python value in the same run
- #17093 / #17106 — delayed first mount after a leftover pre-registration user key (out of scope here)
- #12880 — identity-by-key (out of scope)

title: GlobalHotkeys crashes on keydown/keyup events without a key
body:
### Checklist

    - [x] I searched the existing issues and pull requests for this bug.
    - [x] I reproduced this on Streamlit 1.63.0 and confirmed the same unguarded code is present on the current develop branch.

    ### Summary

    The global shortcut handler assumes every dispatched keydown/keyup event has a string key. Browser integrations, test harnesses, embedded hosts, or extensions can dispatch an Event without the KeyboardEvent key field. In that case, GlobalHotkeys calls toLowerCase on undefined and throws an uncaught TypeError.

    ### Minimal reproduction

    Run any Streamlit app, open the browser console after the app loads, and execute:

    ~~~js
    document.dispatchEvent(new Event("keydown"))
    document.dispatchEvent(new Event("keyup"))
    ~~~

    The first event reaches GlobalHotkeys.handleKeyDown and calls normalizeKey(event.key). The second reaches handleKeyUp and does the same. Because Event has no key property, normalizeKey receives undefined and key.toLowerCase() throws.

    A plain DOM Event is intentional here: event listeners can receive synthetic events from browser hosts and integrations despite the TypeScript annotation. The handler should be defensive at this external boundary.

    ### Current implementation

    In frontend/app/src/components/GlobalHotkeys/GlobalHotkeys.tsx:

    ~~~ts
    function normalizeKey(key: string): string {
    return key === "Escape" || key === "Esc" ? "esc" : key.toLowerCase()
    }

    const handleKeyDown = (event: KeyboardEvent): void => {
    const normalizedKey = normalizeKey(event.key)
    // ...
    }

    const handleKeyUp = (event: KeyboardEvent): void => {
    const normalizedKey = normalizeKey(event.key)
    // ...
    }
    ~~~

    ### Expected behavior

    Malformed or non-keyboard keydown/keyup events without a string key should be ignored without throwing. Normal keyboard shortcuts should continue to work.

    ### Suggested fix

    Guard both handlers before normalization, for example:

    ~~~ts
    if (typeof event.key !== "string") {
    return
    }
    ~~~

    Alternatively, make normalizeKey accept unknown and return undefined for invalid values, with callers returning early.

    ### Regression test

    Add cases in GlobalHotkeys.test.tsx that dispatch keydown and keyup events without key and assert that no exception is thrown and no shortcut callback runs.

    ### Environment

    - Streamlit: 1.63.0
    - Also present on the current develop branch as of 2026-09-22
    - Browser: Chromium

title: Security: Add configurable WebSocket Origin allow-list
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Our enterprise application uses Streamlit WebSockets for application communication.

During an enterprise DAST/security assessment, the scanner tested the WebSocket Origin validation by modifying the Origin header to an unauthorized domain.

The WebSocket connection was still accepted.

For example, the legitimate request contains an approved Origin:

Origin: https://<approved-application-domain>

The DAST scanner changes this to:

Origin: https://malicious-example.com

The WebSocket connection is still established.

## Security Concern

Without strict Origin validation, an authenticated WebSocket connection may potentially be initiated from an unauthorized website.

This creates a security concern for enterprise applications where access is restricted to specific trusted domains.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python

```

### Steps To Reproduce

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

Streamlit should provide a supported configuration option to define an explicit WebSocket Origin allow-list.

For example:

server.websocketAllowedOrigins = [
    "https://<approved-domain>"
]

or an equivalent configuration.

The application should reject the WebSocket upgrade when the Origin is not present in the configured allow-list.

### Current Behavior

Missing WebSocket Origin Validation

Test performed by DAST:

1. Establish normal WebSocket connection.
2. Modify the Origin header to another domain.
3. Send the WebSocket upgrade request.
4. Connection is still accepted.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit: 1.60.0
- Python: 3.12
- Deployment: Azure App Service (Linux)
- Reverse proxy: Azure Application Gateway WAF v2
- Authentication: OKTA OIDC
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

Does Streamlit currently provide a supported configuration for strict WebSocket Origin validation?

If not, could a configurable WebSocket Origin allow-list be added?

This capability is required for enterprise security/DAST compliance.

```Python
import sys

import streamlit as st
from streamlit import runtime, session_state
from streamlit.web import cli as stcli

_COUNTER_KEY_SUFFIX = "_counter_value"


@st.fragment
def _render_button_in_dialog(page_key: str) -> None:
    """Fragment: increment button rendered inside the dialog."""
    counter_key = f"{page_key}{_COUNTER_KEY_SUFFIX}"

    if st.button("➕ Increment", key=f"{page_key}_increment_btn", type="primary"):

    """Fragment: open-dialog button."""
    counter_key = f"{page_key}{_COUNTER_KEY_SUFFIX}"

    if counter_key not in session_state:

    def _open_dialog() -> None:
        _render_button_in_dialog(page_key)

    st.button("🔢 Open Counter", key=f"{page_key}_open_btn", on_click=_open_dialog)

title: Pills/ToggleButtonGroup: all options render with "selected" style on fresh page load in Safari
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

On fresh page load (before any user interaction), st.pills (multi-select mode) renders ALL options with the "selected" purple-outline style in Safari, even though no option is selected — the underlying server-side state (default=None) is correctly empty. The visual bug appears specifically in real Safari and does not reproduce in Chromium or Playwright's WebKit engine.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

selected = st.pills(
    "Filter",
    options=["Option A", "Option B", "Option C"],
    selection_mode="multi",
    default=None,
)
st.write(selected)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open the app fresh in Safari (macOS or iOS) — a new tab/window, not a warm reload.
2. Before clicking anything, observe the st.pills widget with selection_mode="multi" and default=None.
3. All options render with the "selected" purple-outline styling, even though nothing has been selected yet.
4. The underlying state is correct (st.write(selected) shows an empty list) — this is a visual-only bug.
5. Does NOT reproduce in Chromium or in Playwright's WebKit engine — only in real Safari.

### Expected Behavior

On fresh load with default=None, all pill options should render in the plain/unselected style, matching the actual empty selection state.

### Current Behavior

All pill options render in the "selected" style (purple outline/fill) on fresh page load in Safari, despite no option being selected and the server-side value correctly being an empty list.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.64.0
- Python version: (from your requirements.txt / Railway build — Claude Code can confirm the exact version)
- Browser: Safari (macOS) — reproduces on real Safari; does not reproduce in Chromium or Playwright's WebKit
- OS: macOS

### Additional Information

Extracted the relevant CSS from the live page's compiled stylesheet:
[data-selected]:not([data-disabled]) { background-color: rgba(79,70,229,0.1); border-color: rgb(79,70,229); color: rgb(79,70,229); }

This appears to be an attribute-presence selector issue: in Chromium/WebKit-via-Playwright, react-aria (the underlying ToggleButtonGroup implementation) correctly omits the data-selected attribute entirely on unselected buttons, so the selector doesn't match. It's possible real Safari's DOM/CSS engine handles react-aria's attribute timing differently on initial paint, causing data-selected to be briefly (or persistently) present on all buttons before Safari's own attribute-removal logic runs — worth investigating from the react-aria/Safari interaction side.

title: Deprecate the `persist` option of `st.cache_data` in favor of configurable cache storage
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Deprecate the [`persist` parameter of `st.cache_data`](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/caching-and-state/st.cache_data) (`persist="disk"`). It doesn't fit well with the rest of the API and is incompatible with more recent features. A better, more flexible alternative is to make the **cache storage backend configurable** (e.g. via `st.App`), so users can plug in a storage that persists to disk — or Redis/S3 — consistently across the whole app.

### Why?

`persist="disk"` is a narrow, awkward escape hatch:
- It only supports a single hardcoded mode (`"disk"`) with a non-configurable location (#3018).
- It doesn't compose cleanly with other cache features — e.g. it ignores `ttl` (#4859).
- It's a per-function flag for what is really a deployment/storage concern, so it's easy to misuse and inconsistent across an app.
- It doesn't scale to multi-instance deployments (each replica has its own local disk), where users actually want a shared/central store.

A configurable storage backend addresses all of this in one coherent mechanism, and persistence becomes just one storage implementation rather than a special-cased parameter.

### How?

- **Introduce a configurable cache storage API** (per the [custom storage API spec, PR #14902](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/14902)) — e.g. a `cache_storage_manager` parameter on `st.App` — that lets users supply a custom backend (disk, Redis, S3, …) applied consistently to `st.cache_data`.
  - A built-in/example disk-persisting storage would cover today's `persist="disk"` use case (with configurable location, and without the `ttl` incompatibility).
- **Deprecate `persist`** on `st.cache_data` with a long, clearly-communicated window and a documented migration path (it keeps working during deprecation). Follow "Graceful Evolution" — 3+ months notice, clear migration guidance.

### Additional Context

- Docs: [`st.cache_data`](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/caching-and-state/st.cache_data).
- Replacement direction: [PR #14902 — custom storage API for `st.App`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/14902) (also motivated by #5849 "bring your own Redis cache").
- Related persist limitations: #4859 (`persist='disk'` ignores `ttl`), #3018 (configurable location for persistent cache).

title: BUG: wrong value returned by backend vs frontend, when a widget is rendered after a previous page run set a default value in session state
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

If a default value is set in session state on one page run, and then subsequently a widget is rendered with a corresponding `key`, then the default value is not picked up properly and the frontend and backend show different values for that widget.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

# Sets default on first page run
st.session_state.setdefault("foo", 100.0)

if st.toggle("Show"):
    foo = st.number_input("Foo", key="foo")  # Shows 0.00
    st.write("You entered:", foo)  # Shows 100.0
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1.Turn on the  toggle
2. Compare the value in the widget vs the value printed underneath

### Expected Behavior

The value in the widget should match the number reported underneath.

### Current Behavior

The input widget displays `0.00`, but the backend reports `You entered: 100`.

If `r` is pressed to trigger a re-run, then the frontend updates to display `0.0` and the default value is lost.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.64.0
- Python version: 3.14.7
- Operating System: Ubuntu 22.04
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

This bug is problematic for more complex pages, where widgets may need to be "loaded" or "reset" programmatically, and some widgets may be conditionally hidden depending on a toggle or checkbox.

The bug does not happen if `persist_state="page"` is passed to `number_input`.

Possibly related: #15660 seems to have fixed a similar bug for when persist_state is passed, but not for when persist_state=None.

title: Scroll to st.chat_input
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Placing `st.chat_input` inside `st.bottom` causes an otherwise non-chat page to scroll to the bottom immediately on initial load, without any user interaction or chat messages. This hides the heading and initial content when using the bottom container for a persistent assistant alongside a dashboard. Replacing only `st.chat_input` with `st.text_input` prevents the unsolicited scrolling.


### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

st.title("Dashboard heading")
for number in range(30):
    st.write(f"Dashboard row {number}")

with st.bottom:
    st.chat_input("Ask about the dashboard")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Install `streamlit==1.63.0` and run the example with `streamlit run app.py`.
2. Open a fresh browser tab/context with a viewport around 1280 x 720, so the main content exceeds the viewport height.
3. Do not click, type, or scroll. Wait for rendering to settle.
4. Observe that the main page has scrolled to the bottom and the dashboard heading is offscreen.
5. As a control, replace `st.chat_input` with `st.text_input`, restart/reload in a fresh browser context, and observe that the page stays at the top.

No custom CSS, JavaScript, Snowflake connection, fragments, tabs, navigation, or third-party component is needed to reproduce this.

### Expected Behavior

An initial dashboard load should remain at the top. A bottom-docked input should not make non-chat content above it auto-scroll before any conversation exists. If automatic scrolling is intentional for chat-first apps, an opt-out for this mixed dashboard/assistant use case would be helpful.


### Current Behavior

The page scrolls to the bottom on its own. In three fresh Chrome contexts per variant, measured after rendering settled at a 1280 x 720 viewport:

| Bottom widget | Main scrollTop | Main scrollHeight | Main clientHeight |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `st.chat_input` (all 3 runs) | 843 | 1563 | 720 |
| `st.text_input` (all 3 control runs) | 0 | 1573 | 720 |

The scroll position was read from the main scrollable section (`section.stMain`), not `window.scrollY`. No Streamlit exception was displayed. Measurements used Playwright with installed Chrome in headless mode; the same symptom was first noticed in interactive Chrome in a larger app.

### Is this a regression?

### Debug info

- Python version: 3.14.3
- Operating System: macOS 26.6, ARM64
- Browser: Google Chrome 152.0.7977.83

title: Preserve coroutine-function detection for async cached functions
body:
## Summary

PR [#16168](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16168) adds async-aware `st.cache_data` and `st.cache_resource`. An async cached function remains awaitable, but the decorated object is a `CachedFunc` whose `__call__` is synchronous and returns an awaitable. As a result:

```python
import inspect

import streamlit as st


@st.cache_data
async def cached_lookup(query: str) -> str:
    return await search_service(query)


assert not inspect.iscoroutinefunction(cached_lookup)
result = cached_lookup("streamlit")
assert inspect.isawaitable(result)
value = await result
```

This issue is a searchable decision record and a place to collect demand for preserving coroutine-function detection through the cache decorators. It is not committed follow-up work and does not block #16168.

## Affected integrations

Some frameworks inspect a callback before invoking it to decide whether to use their sync or async execution path:

- LangChain `RunnableLambda`
- LlamaIndex `FunctionTool`
- MCP callback/tool registration, including decorator-based tool APIs
- Similar callback systems such as Gradio

When the decorated `CachedFunc` is classified as synchronous, a framework may invoke it on its sync path and treat the returned coroutine as the sync result instead of awaiting it.

## Supported compatibility pattern

Keep the cached implementation separate and pass a true `async def` adapter to APIs that inspect callbacks. This reusable adapter preserves coroutine-function detection while still calling through the cache:

```python
from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
from typing import ParamSpec, TypeVar

P = ParamSpec("P")
R = TypeVar("R")


def as_async_callback(
    cached_func: Callable[P, Awaitable[R]],
) -> Callable[P, Awaitable[R]]:
    async def callback(*args: P.args, **kwargs: P.kwargs) -> R:
        return await cached_func(*args, **kwargs)

    return callback


retrieve_callback = as_async_callback(cached_lookup)

runnable = RunnableLambda(retrieve_callback)
tool = FunctionTool.from_defaults(fn=retrieve_callback)
```

For decorator-based MCP registration, keep the cached function separate from the registered tool:

```python
@st.cache_data
async def cached_customer(customer_id: int) -> dict:
    return await database.fetch(customer_id)


@mcp.tool()
async def lookup_customer(customer_id: int) -> dict:
    return await cached_customer(customer_id)
```

Do not use `inspect.unwrap(cached_lookup)` as the callback. It returns the original function and therefore bypasses Streamlit caching.

## Demand collection

Please comment if the async-adapter pattern cannot satisfy your use case. Include:

- the framework and version;
- how the callback is registered and invoked; and
- why a separate `async def` adapter is insufficient.

That evidence can inform whether Streamlit should preserve coroutine-function detection directly in a future change.

## Related

- [#16168](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16168) — async-aware cache decorators
- [#8308](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8308) — general async cached-function support

title: Streamlit websockets 16.1 issue
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Streamlit's pyproject.toml pins "websockets>=12.0.0". Version 16.1 of websockets (released July 9, 2026) introduced a change that blocks non-ASCII values in HTTP headers (see [changelog](https://websockets.readthedocs.io/en/stable/project/changelog.html#id2), "Blocked non-ASCII values in Headers").

This breaks the WebSocket handshake for setups where a reverse proxy / auth layer injects headers containing UTF-8 characters before the request reaches Streamlit — for example [Authelia](https://www.authelia.com/) forward-auth, which can inject a Remote-Name header containing the user's display name (e.g. accented characters, non-Latin scripts).

Since Streamlit's dependency constraint allows websockets to resolve to 16.1+, installing/upgrading Streamlit in a fresh environment can silently pull in a version that breaks WebSocket connections for any deployment relying on non-ASCII header values, with no warning at install time

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python

```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Deploy Streamlit behind a reverse proxy (nginx/Traefik) with Authelia forward-auth, configured to forward Remote-Name, Remote-Email, etc. headers to the backend.
2. Ensure a user's Authelia display name contains a non-ASCII character (e.g. "François", "Müller", "田中").
3. Install/upgrade Streamlit in an environment where pip resolves websockets to >=16.1.
4. Log in as that user and attempt to load the app.

### Expected Behavior

The WebSocket connection (/_stcore/stream) should be established successfully, as it was with websockets<16.1.

### Current Behavior

The WebSocket handshake fails because websockets 16.1 rejects the non-ASCII header value. The app gets stuck on "Please wait..." / the frontend logs a WebSocket connection failure, similar in symptom to issues like #8799.

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.58
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: Debian
- Browser: Chrome / Mozilla


### Additional Information

Workaround: pinning websockets<16.1 restores normal behavior.

Possible fixes on Streamlit's side:

- Tighten the websockets dependency constraint (e.g. >=12.0.0,<16.1) until this is addressed, or

- Percent-encode / sanitize header values Streamlit forwards or reads internally before they reach the websockets layer.

title: [feature] Add copy="cow" option to st.cache_data
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add an opt-in `copy="cow"` mode to `st.cache_data` that uses copy-on-write semantics for cached return values. This avoids unnecessary full-object deserialization on cache hits while preserving isolation between callers, significantly reducing cache-hit latency and memory allocation for large cached objects.

### Why?

`st.cache_data` currently creates an independent copy of the cached value for each call. This provides isolation between callers, but for large objects such as Pandas DataFrames and NumPy arrays, repeatedly deserializing and copying cached values can introduce significant CPU time and memory allocation overhead.

This becomes particularly relevant for applications where large datasets are read repeatedly across multiple sessions, while mutations to returned values are relatively uncommon.

An opt-in copy-on-write mode can preserve the isolation guarantees of `st.cache_data` while avoiding unnecessary full-object duplication on cache hits. The existing behavior would remain unchanged for applications that do not opt into the new mode.

In benchmarks using Python 3.13.15, Pandas 3.0.6, and Streamlit 1.64.0, the prototype reduced observed cache-hit latency by approximately 2.7–3.2× for DataFrames ranging from 5,000 to 1,000,000 rows. In a separate allocation benchmark with 10 consecutive reads, observed allocation decreased from approximately 4.67 MB to 0.02–0.03 MB.

### How?

Introduce an optional `copy` parameter on `st.cache_data`:

```python
@st.cache_data(copy="cow")
def load_data():
    return pd.read_parquet("large_dataset.parquet")

### Additional Context

### Prototype

A working prototype is available in my fork:

https://github.com/Isllanrx/streamlit/tree/feature/cache-data-cow

The implementation is currently limited to the following areas:

- `st.cache_data` API support for `copy="cow"`
- Copy-on-write handling for supported cached return values
- Caller/session mutation isolation
- Integration with existing cache lifecycle and eviction behavior
- Unit tests for mutation isolation
- Static typing coverage for the public API

### Performance Benchmark

The prototype was benchmarked using Python 3.13.15, Pandas 3.0.6, and Streamlit 1.64.0.

| Dataset | Default copy | `copy="cow"` | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 5,000 × 12 | 0.155 ms | 0.055 ms | 2.8× |
| 50,000 × 12 | 0.158 ms | 0.049 ms | 3.2× |
| 200,000 × 12 | 0.144 ms | 0.048 ms | 3.0× |
| 1,000,000 × 12 | 0.131 ms | 0.049 ms | 2.7× |

In a separate allocation benchmark using 10 consecutive cache reads, observed allocation decreased from approximately 4.67 MB with the existing behavior to approximately 0.02–0.03 MB with `copy="cow"`.

### Stress Testing

The implementation was also tested under concurrent mutation and cache lifecycle pressure:

| Scenario | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 50 concurrent threads mutating the same 100,000-row DataFrame | Passed |
| Nested dictionaries containing DataFrames, Series, and lists | Passed |
| 200 concurrent cache entries with `max_entries=5` | Passed |
| Concurrent readers while repeatedly calling `.clear()` | Passed |
| 1,000,000-row (~100 MB) DataFrame with mutation isolation | Passed |

The concurrent mutation test completed in approximately 0.046 seconds. The cached DataFrame remained unchanged and no cross-caller mutations were observed.

The 1,000,000-row test also preserved mutation isolation, with subsequent reads completing in approximately 0.08 ms.

These tests were specifically designed to validate both the performance characteristics and the isolation guarantees of the proposed copy-on-write behavior.

title: Support stable UI placement for concurrent async tasks
body:
### Summary

When independent top-level async cached functions emit `st.*` messages concurrently, users may need their relative UI placement to stay stable and the layout to be identical on cache misses and hits.

That guarantee is not currently supported. Concurrent calls can mechanically render, but coroutine scheduling controls how their messages interleave. Each cached call owns a separate replay list, and those lists cannot reconstruct the cross-call interleaving observed during the original computations.

This does **not** mean that `asyncio.gather()`, async caching, or normal `st.*` calls from one cached function are unsupported. A single cached call continues to capture and replay its messages in order. The unsupported case is deterministic relative placement across independent concurrent cached calls.

This issue is a decision record and a place to collect demand. We are unlikely to implement a new mechanism unless real use cases show that the alternatives below are insufficient.

### Pattern without an ordering guarantee

The async cache decorators in #16168 make this pattern executable:

```python
import asyncio

import streamlit as st


@st.cache_data
async def load_customers() -> int:
    st.write("Loading customers")
    await asyncio.sleep(0.2)
    st.write("Customers loaded")
    return 120


@st.cache_data
async def load_revenue() -> str:
    st.write("Loading revenue")
    await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
    st.write("Revenue loaded")
    return "$1.2M"


async def main() -> None:
    await asyncio.gather(load_customers(), load_revenue())


asyncio.run(main())
```

The output order and the miss-versus-hit interleaving are not guaranteed. This is specifically a UI-placement limitation, not a limitation on using `asyncio.gather()`.

### Recommended: join before rendering

Return data from the cached functions, await them concurrently, and render sequentially in source order:

```python
import asyncio

import streamlit as st


@st.cache_data
async def load_customers() -> int:
    await asyncio.sleep(0.2)
    return 120


@st.cache_data
async def load_revenue() -> str:
    await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
    return "$1.2M"


async def load_all() -> tuple[int, str]:
    customers, revenue = await asyncio.gather(load_customers(), load_revenue())
    return customers, revenue


customers, revenue = asyncio.run(load_all())
st.metric("Customers", customers)
st.metric("Revenue", revenue)
```

This provides deterministic source-order layout, at the cost of waiting for all results before rendering them.

### Recommended: reserve stable progressive sections

`@st.fragment(parallel=True)` is already available on `develop` (implemented in #15173). Each fragment reserves its own container at its call site, so sections can complete progressively without moving relative to one another. Until native async cache decorators from #16168 are available, a synchronous cached wrapper can drive each async fetch:

```python
import asyncio

import streamlit as st


async def fetch_customers() -> int:
    await asyncio.sleep(0.2)
    return 120


async def fetch_revenue() -> str:
    await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
    return "$1.2M"


@st.cache_data
def load_customers() -> int:
    return asyncio.run(fetch_customers())


@st.cache_data
def load_revenue() -> str:
    return asyncio.run(fetch_revenue())


@st.fragment(parallel=True)
def customers_section() -> None:
    st.metric("Customers", load_customers())


@st.fragment(parallel=True)
def revenue_section() -> None:
    st.metric("Revenue", load_revenue())


customers_section()
revenue_section()
```

This is the best currently available alternative when progressive rendering and stable source-order placement are both required. After #16168 lands, each fragment can instead call an async cached function through `asyncio.run()`.

Async fragment bodies are not currently justified as a distinct capability for this problem: they would mostly be syntax sugar over driving async work inside a fragment unless users identify a missing lifecycle or compatibility need.

### Feedback wanted

Please comment with concrete cases where join-before-render and independent parallel fragments do not fit, especially if you need:

- progressive results rather than waiting for the full join;
- one shared event loop or loop-bound clients;
- source-order placement versus completion-order placement; or
- behavior that independent parallel fragments cannot provide.

Please also describe why the alternatives fail and what miss/hit layout users should observe.

### Related

- #16168 — async-aware `st.cache_data` and `st.cache_resource`
- #8308 — async cache decorator feature request
- #14277 — merged parallel fragments product spec
- #15173 — parallel fragments implementation

title: A config that sets server.port raises at config parse and blocks startup on a dev-mode (non-site-packages) install
body:
### Summary

Setting `server.port` raises out of config parsing and blocks startup when Streamlit considers itself a development install, and the message does not say how to proceed.

`streamlit/config.py` defines `global.developmentMode` as true whenever the package is not under a `site-packages` directory (`"site-packages" not in __file__` — so a source checkout, `pip install -e`, or a vendored/`--target` install), and `_check_conflicts()` then raises:

```
RuntimeError: server.port does not work when global.developmentMode is true.
```

The raise looks deliberate — in dev mode the Node server hard-codes 8501, which is what the comment above the check explains — so this is a question about the *failure mode* rather than a claim that the check itself is wrong. Two things make it awkward from an application author's side:

1. **A committed config value is enough.** An app that ships `[server] port = ...` in its `.streamlit/config.toml` (a normal thing to pin for a deployment) cannot start *at all* on a dev-mode install, and the author may never have intended that value for this environment.
2. **The error does not name a way forward.** It says why the port does not work, not what to do about it. The escape hatch (below) is not discoverable from the message.

### Steps to reproduce

Self-contained; `pip install --target` is just a convenient way to get a non-`site-packages` install.

```bash
WORK=/tmp/streamlit-devmode-repro
python3 -m pip install --quiet --target "$WORK/pkgs" "streamlit==1.64.0"
mkdir -p "$WORK/app/.streamlit"
printf '[server]\nport = 9999\n' > "$WORK/app/.streamlit/config.toml"
cd "$WORK/app"

# 1. Any library use that parses config
PYTHONPATH="$WORK/pkgs" python3 -c "import streamlit.config as c; c.get_config_options()"
# RuntimeError: server.port does not work when global.developmentMode is true.

# 2. The CLI
PYTHONPATH="$WORK/pkgs" python3 -m streamlit config show
# same RuntimeError

# 3. Even with no port in any config file:
PYTHONPATH="$WORK/pkgs" python3 -m streamlit config show --server.port 8502
# same RuntimeError
```

All three exit 1. With a config that sets no port, the same install parses fine (`server.port` = 8501).

### Expected behavior

One of:

- warn and ignore the configured port (nothing needs it in dev mode, and the server uses 8501 regardless), or
- raise only for the port the server would actually use, and have the message name the escape hatch, e.g. *"remove `server.port` from `.streamlit/config.toml`, or run with `--global.developmentMode false`"*.

### Actual behavior

A hard `RuntimeError` from `get_config_options()`, before any app code runs, for any source of the value: a project or machine config file, or the documented `--server.port` flag.

### Is this new?

The same on 1.63.0 and 1.64.0 (in 1.63 the check sits at the end of `streamlit/config.py`, reached via `_on_config_parsed`). I have not checked further back.

### Workarounds (both verified)

- `streamlit run app.py --global.developmentMode false` — per run.
- `[global] developmentMode = false` in a config file — persistent, but it is a hidden option and it also turns off dev-mode conveniences (e.g. `logger.level` defaulting to `debug`).

### Environment

- Streamlit 1.63.0 and 1.64.0
- Python 3.13.14
- macOS 27.0 (arm64)

title: Add a first-party Playwright-based e2e testing API (`streamlit.testing.e2e`) alongside AppTest
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add a first-party, Playwright-based **end-to-end (browser) testing API** for Streamlit apps — `streamlit.testing.e2e` — as an optional `streamlit[testing]` extra, complementing the existing browserless unit-testing API (`AppTest`). It would provide a Streamlit-aware semantic facade for finding and operating elements in a real browser, rerun/navigation-aware synchronization, useful failure artifacts, and an escape hatch to native Playwright `Page`/`Locator`. Design thoughts are in the [app testing toolkit spec (PR #16041)](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16041).

### Why?

Today users face an unhelpful choice: `AppTest` is fast and Python-native but runs no real frontend (so it can disagree with a real app, and can't cover rendering, custom components, accessibility, media, charts, or real user journeys), while browser testing can validate the real product but Streamlit provides **no supported way** to start the app, wait for reruns, select elements, collect logs, or test a deployed/embedded app — users must assemble and maintain all that infrastructure. Streamlit's own mature `e2e_playwright/` suite solves these hard problems (process lifecycle, ephemeral ports, app-idle detection, traces, iframes, uploads, dataframes/charts, etc.) but is coupled to the repo layout and private DOM test IDs, so it isn't a releasable public API.

This is especially costly for **AI coding agents**, which need a deterministic run command, semantic element identity, a compact description of the current UI, and actionable failure artifacts to validate their work — indexes, private CSS/test IDs, sleeps, and screenshots alone make brittle tests.

### How?

Ship a two-layer testing story with clear boundaries (don't build a third UI-testing engine, and don't turn AppTest into a browser emulator):

- **AppTest (browserless)** stays the fast option for logic/state/basic widget workflows — with improved runtime fidelity and typed + universal semantic queries (`get_by_key`/`get_by_label`/`get_by_text`) and a compact `snapshot()`.
- **`streamlit.testing.e2e` (browser)** — the new Playwright-based API, installed via `pip install "streamlit[testing]"`.

Proposed shape (from the spec):

```python
from playwright.sync_api import expect
from streamlit.testing.e2e import StreamlitPage, app_fixture

app = app_fixture("app.py")

def test_sign_in(app: StreamlitPage):
    app.get_element_by_label("Username", type="text_input").set_value("ada")
    app.get_element_by_label("Password", type="text_input").set_value("correct horse battery staple")
    app.get_element_by_label("Sign in", type="button").click()

    welcome = app.get_element_by_text("Welcome, ada", type="heading")
    expect(welcome.locator).to_be_visible()
```

Key capabilities:
- **App lifecycle fixture:** `app_fixture()` starts one app server per test module on an ephemeral localhost port, gives an isolated browser page per test, and waits until the initial run is idle. Also target direct/external URLs (deployed/embedded apps).
- **Semantic selection:** strict, retrying finders that understand Streamlit elements and layout containers — `get_element_by_key` / `get_element_by_label` / `get_element_by_text`, plus `get_element(type=...)` / `get_elements(type=...)`; a returned element that is a container (sidebar, form, expander, popover, dialog, tab, column, container) can scope further queries. An optional `type` discriminator maps to a generated public `ElementType` taxonomy for IDE completion.
- **Rerun/navigation-aware synchronization** so tests don't rely on sleeps.
- **Actionable failure artifacts** (text/logs/traces/screenshots) and a **semantic snapshot** (`semantic_snapshot()`) as a token-efficient interface for humans and agents.
- **Escape hatch** to native Playwright `Page`/`Locator` for anything the facade doesn't cover.
- A shared **testability vocabulary** across both layers (public element types, labels, keys, containers), explicitly optimized for AI agents.

### Additional Context

- Spec: [PR #16041 — \`[spec] Streamlit app testing toolkit\`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16041) (`specs/2026-07-16-streamlit-app-testing-toolkit/product-spec.md`).
- Related: open `feature:app-testing` issues, e.g. #9786, #13163, #9128.

title: Add a link/bookmark element that renders a rich link preview card
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add a link/bookmark element that renders a URL as a rich preview card — with properties like an icon/favicon, title, description, and optionally a preview image — similar to how a bookmark looks in Notion or a link result in Google search. It could optionally **auto-fetch** these properties (e.g. from the page's Open Graph / metadata) when they aren't provided explicitly, and it should **adapt its layout** based on which properties are present.

### Why?

Links are everywhere in apps (sources, references, related resources, docs), but a bare Markdown link is visually flat. A rich, consistent link/bookmark card makes references look polished and scannable — great for dashboards, research/agent apps that cite sources, resource lists, and "read more" sections. Today users hand-build these with columns + images + markdown or custom components, which is fiddly and inconsistent.

### How?

A new element, e.g.:

```python
st.link_preview(
    "https://streamlit.io",
    title="Streamlit • A faster way to build and share data apps",
    description="Streamlit is an open-source Python framework for data scientists and AI/ML engineers to deliver interactive data apps – in only a few lines of code.",
    icon="https://streamlit.io/favicon.png",   # icon/favicon
    image="https://.../preview.png",           # optional large preview image
)

# Minimal — auto-fetch metadata from the URL:
st.link_preview("https://streamlit.io")
```

Behavior:
- **Dynamic layout:** adapt the card to whichever properties are provided — e.g. compact (favicon + title + description) vs. a larger card with a preview image (like the two reference looks below).
- **Auto-fetch (optional):** when title/description/icon/image aren't given, fetch them from the target URL's metadata (Open Graph / `<meta>` / favicon). Should be opt-in-friendly and degrade gracefully if fetching fails or is blocked (fall back to just the URL/title). Consider caching and the SiS/Community-Cloud implications of server-side fetching (and whether fetching happens backend- or frontend-side).
- Whole card is a link to the URL; supports opening in a new tab.

**Alternative / complementary: a Markdown directive.** This could also be exposed as a Markdown directive so bookmarks can be embedded inline in any markdown text (e.g. `st.markdown`), for example:

```
:bookmark[https://python-markdown.github.io/extensions/toc/]{title="Foo" icon=":material/info:"}
```

The directive attributes (`title`, `description`, `icon`, `image`, …) map to the same properties as the element, and unspecified ones can be auto-fetched. A directive plays nicely with LLM-generated content and lets bookmarks appear inline within larger blocks of text.

**Simpler inline "mentions".** The same directive family could also cover a lighter-weight inline link — not a full card, but a link that doesn't use the default link color and instead has a more button-like hover effect, with a configurable icon and title. For example:

```
:mention[URL]{text="My link"}
:mention[URL]{text="My link" icon="🍀"}
:mention[URL]{text="My link" icon="github"}
:mention[URL]{icon="streamlit"}
```

This gives a compact, chip/mention-style link (great inline in text or chat) that sits between a plain Markdown link and the full bookmark card.

Reference looks (a compact link result vs. a larger card with a preview image):

- Compact: favicon + site + bold title (link color) + description snippet.
- Rich: title + description on the left, with a preview image on the right and favicon + URL at the bottom.

### Additional Context

- Inspired by link/bookmark cards in Notion and rich link results in Google search.
- Complements a possible OEmbed feature (embedding Streamlit content elsewhere); this is the inverse — richly embedding external links inside a Streamlit app.
- Related: #11990 (file chip element, e.g. for `st.chat_message`) — a similar compact, reference-style element that could share design/infrastructure.
