title: Frequent websocket connection drops on higher (default 30s) ping_interval
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Since the last update from Streamlit 1.45.1 (Tornado 6.4.2) to 1.47.0 (Tornado 6.5.1) my users reported very frequent (say every half a minute) grey-outs of the pages/elements. Upon further inspection it seems that the websocket connection was often considered closed.

The cause seems to lie in the `ping_timeout` saga (https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/3196, https://github.com/tornadoweb/tornado/pull/3376, https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11670).

Forcing Tornado to 6.4.2 (while still keeping streamlit on 1.47.0) solves the issue because the conditional sets the `websocket_ping_interval` to 1s again. We run Streamlit in a Docker container with Nginx, so a proxy setup applies.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
n/a
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Streamlit 1.47.0 in a Docker container with Nginx

### Expected Behavior

Stability with a higher `websocket_ping_interval` server setting (e.g. 30s).
Allowing for more recent versions of Tornado (> 6.4.2) to be used.

### Current Behavior

Streamlit instability with a higher `websocket_ping_interval` server setting

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.47.0
- Tornado version: 6.5.1
- Python version: 3.12.5
- Operating System: Linux


### Additional Information

Originally this Streamlit issue https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/3196 was reported and solved/merged with `"websocket_ping_interval": 1` on 23 jun 2021.

A recent Tornado issue on https://github.com/tornadoweb/tornado/pull/3376 came to disallow the `websocket_ping_interval` to be below the `websocket_ping_timeout` of 30s. This update was merged/released on 22 april 2025 (Tornado 6.5.1). 

The Tornado update - allowing the `websocket_ping_interval` gave trouble to some Streamlit users, reported 17 jun 2025: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11670. This Streamlit issue was eventually solved by the current code: `"websocket_ping_interval": 1 if is_tornado_version_less_than("6.5.0") else 30,`
With the update, @lukasmasuch remarked: `This could potentially bring back an old issue with dropping connections in specific proxy setups - #3196. Something we need to watch out for after this gets released.`

It seems our Streamlit setup is suffering from this regression. Forcing Tornado to 6.4.2 (while still keeping streamlit on 1.47.0) solves the issue because the conditional sets the `websocket_ping_interval` to 1s again.

title: Nested run_every fragment stays on screen with stale content after being hidden
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When a nested `run_every` fragment stops being rendered, its container can stay on screen showing frozen, stale content until the *enclosing* fragment next completes a run. Because the enclosing fragment has no timer of its own, that means it stays visible until the user next interacts with it.

The cause is on the frontend: the enclosing fragment's run finishes successfully and schedules the usual stale-node cleanup, but that cleanup executes with a *later* run's `scriptRunId`/`fragmentIdsThisRun`, so it is scoped to the wrong fragment and never prunes the evicted subtree.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
from uuid import uuid4

import streamlit as st


@st.fragment(run_every=1.0)
def standalone_auto():
    with st.container(key="standalone_auto_fragment"):
        st.write(f"uuid in fragment: {uuid4()}")


standalone_auto()


@st.fragment
def outer():
    show_nested = st.checkbox("Show nested auto fragment", value=True)
    if show_nested:

        @st.fragment
        def middle():
            @st.fragment(run_every=1.0)
            def nested_auto():
                with st.container(key="nested_auto_fragment"):
                    st.write(f"nested uuid: {uuid4()}")

            nested_auto()

        middle()


outer()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app above and wait a few seconds so both `run_every` fragments are ticking.
2. Uncheck "Show nested auto fragment".
3. Repeat, toggling at varying moments relative to the 1s tick. Under CPU load it reproduces roughly once every 4-6 attempts; on an idle machine it is rare.

It is timing sensitive: the toggle has to land while the standalone fragment's next auto-rerun is arriving. Note that `console.log`-based instrumentation slows message handling enough to hide it — use an in-page array if you need to trace.

### Expected Behavior

Unchecking the box removes the nested fragment's container, as it does on a normal rerun.

### Current Behavior

The `nested_auto_fragment` container stays in the DOM with its last-rendered content. It does not update again (its auto-rerun timer is correctly cancelled by `stop_auto_rerun`), so it reads as stale data rather than an obviously broken element. It clears on a full rerun, or when the enclosing fragment next completes a run — which for a timer-less fragment means the next user interaction with it.

Also seen in CI as a flake in `st_fragment_run_every_test.py::test_nested_fragment_run_every_can_hide_without_crash` (e.g. https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/actions/runs/33181944052), failing with `Locator expected not to be attached`.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

Not a regression of #15130. That fixed the white-screen crash in this same scenario (#15084); this leftover-element behavior is a separate defect in the same area.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.62.0 (`develop`)
- Python version: 3.11.6
- Operating System: macOS 26.6.2
- Browser: reproduced on WebKit; not browser specific

### Additional Information

**Root cause (verified by instrumenting the frontend).** `handleScriptFinished` schedules stale-node cleanup inside a `setState` updater that reads `scriptRunId` and `fragmentIdsThisRun` from `prevState` (`frontend/app/src/App.tsx:2027-2038`). Under load the next fragment run has already been committed by the time that updater flushes, so the cleanup runs for the wrong run. Captured trace, with the scheduling status paired against the state the updater actually saw:

```
delta addBlock   frag=28b54e path=0.1   run=6bd090          <- enclosing fragment writes
delta newElement frag=28b54e path=0.1.0 run=6bd090
scriptFinished ENTRY status=FINISHED_FRAGMENT_RUN_SUCCESSFULLY
                     entryRun=6bd090 entryFrags=28b54e      <- its run, finished successfully
delta ... frag=f81f56 run=af93e8                            <- next (standalone) run starts
cleanup scheduledBy=FINISHED_FRAGMENT_RUN_SUCCESSFULLY
        SEES run=af93e8 frags=f81f56                        <- executed as the standalone run
```

So the cleanup ran as `clearStaleNodes(af93e8, ["f81f56"])`. `ClearStaleNodeVisitor` therefore never descended into the enclosing fragment's subtree at `0.1` with `fragmentIdOfBlock` set, and the evicted container was never pruned.

Worth noting the run finished `FINISHED_FRAGMENT_RUN_SUCCESSFULLY`, **not** `FINISHED_EARLY_FOR_RERUN` — so this is not the deliberate cleanup skip for interrupted runs.

**Why this probably needs a server-side change.** `ForwardMsg.script_finished` is a bare enum (`proto/streamlit/proto/ForwardMsg.proto:46-57`, `:66`) and carries no run identity, so the client can only infer which run finished from React state. Both readings are unreliable, in opposite directions, and I observed each failing in the same session:

- at flush time it can see a *later* run (the failure above);
- at handler entry it can see an *earlier* run, when several messages are handled before a commit.

Carrying the run id (and `fragment_ids_this_run`) on `ScriptFinished` so cleanup can be pinned to the run that actually finished would fix it at the source.

**One constraint for whoever picks this up.** A frontend-only workaround that *removes* the evicted nodes is unsafe. Deltas address nodes by absolute path, and `AppRoot.addBlock` inherits an existing block's children rather than resetting them, so removing a node compacts its parent's `children` and every later sibling keeps the shifted index. A fragment sibling that reruns on its own then writes to the wrong slot — I reproduced a silent duplication (`["live"]` → later delta at its original path `[0, 1]` → `["live", "live v2"]`), and `SetNodeByDeltaPathVisitor` can escalate the same shift to a `Bad delta path index` throw. Substituting an index-preserving empty block avoids that, but does not address the attribution race itself. Explored in #16705, which is closed in favour of this issue.

**Related:** #15084, #15130 (the crash in this scenario), #10805 (widget-state cleanup with `run_every`).

I'm always frustrated when I hover an Altair/Vega-Lite chart, see the native download icon beside Fullscreen, click it, and can only get PNG.

For reports and papers I often need SVG (vector, scalable) as well as PNG. The old Vega-Embed ⋯ menu offered "Save as PNG" / "Save as SVG". After https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15806, that menu is gone, SVG export is gone, and `usermeta.embedOptions` can no longer restore export actions.

Workarounds (custom HTML components, extra `st.download_button`s, or DOM hacks) either leave the native toolbar unused or drift out of style as Streamlit's toolbar design changes. There is no public API to attach a format menu to the existing toolbar download button.

Related but different: #8177 is about PNG resolution, not choosing a format.

### How?

Keep the existing native download icon on Altair/Vega-Lite (and other Vega) charts, in the same toolbar row as Fullscreen.

When the pointer hovers that download icon, show a compact dropdown that matches the toolbar (same icon size, radius, colors, light/dark theme). Suggested items:

- Download PNG
- Download SVG

Clicking an item exports from the current Vega view (`toImageURL("png")` / `toImageURL("svg")`) and starts a browser download.

A click with no menu selection can keep today's PNG-only behavior as the default.

I do not need a new `st` command. Optional later: `st.altair_chart(..., download_formats=("png", "svg"))` to choose which items appear. A Python API is nice-to-have; the hover menu on the native icon is the main request.

Please do not bring back the old Vega-Embed ⋯ menu (View Source / Open in Vega Editor). This should stay a Streamlit toolbar control.

### Additional Context

- Native toolbar change that removed SVG: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15806
- Older embedOptions / actions discussion: https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/does-altairs-set-embed-options-work-with-streamlit/1675
- PNG quality (related, not this request): https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8177

I am building a Streamlit questionnaire analysis app that shows many static Altair charts. Users expect the hover toolbar download icon (same family as Fullscreen) to let them pick PNG vs SVG, without a separate download widget beside every chart.

title: fix(caching): UnserializableReturnValueError drops original exception context
body:
### Summary

When `@st.cache_data` fails to serialize a return value and raises `UnserializableReturnValueError`, the original exception (e.g., `PicklingError`) is silently dropped because the `raise` statement is missing `from ex`.

This is inconsistent with the adjacent `UnevaluatedDataFrameError` which correctly chains the original exception using `from ex` (line 409 of `cache_utils.py`).

### Impact

Users debugging `UnserializableReturnValueError` lose the root cause. For example, in issue #14593, users hit a `PicklingError` from stale class references after module reloading, but the error message gives no indication of the underlying pickle failure.

### Location

`lib/streamlit/runtime/caching/cache_utils.py`, in `_handle_cache_miss()`:

```python
# Current (line 410-412):
raise UnserializableReturnValueError(
    return_value=computed_value, func=self._info.func
)

# Should be:
raise UnserializableReturnValueError(
    return_value=computed_value, func=self._info.func
) from ex
```

### Related

Partially addresses #14593 — this is the low-effort "Option A" fix suggested there.

title: Add a `type="cards"` variant to `st.radio` for a card/bordered design
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add a `type` parameter to `st.radio` with a `"cards"` variant that renders each option as a bordered, selectable card (with the selected card highlighted) instead of the default radio-button list. Same widget behavior — only the visual style changes. See [Tremor's Radio Card Group](https://www.tremor.so/docs/inputs/radio-card-group) for the look.

### Why?

Card-style single-select is a very common, more prominent and touch-friendly pattern for choosing between a few richer options (e.g. plans, payment methods, layouts, modes). Today users approximate it with columns + bordered containers + buttons/`st.radio` and a lot of manual state/CSS work. A built-in `"cards"` variant makes this polished pattern a one-liner.

### How?

Add a `type` parameter (default preserves today's look):

```python
choice = st.radio(
    "Choose a plan",
    ["Starter", "Pro", "Enterprise"],
    captions=[
        "For individuals getting started",
        "For growing teams",
        "Advanced controls & support",
    ],
    type="cards",
)
```

- `type="default"` — current radio-button list.
- `type="cards"` — render each option as a bordered card; the selected option is visually highlighted.
- Keep existing params working (`captions`, `horizontal`, `format_func`, `index=None`, etc.). Captions map naturally to a description line inside each card.

**Alternative solution — a `border: bool` parameter:** Instead of a `type` enum, just add `st.radio(..., border=True)` that wraps each option in a bordered card. This mirrors the `border` parameter on `st.container` and keeps the API minimal. Downside: it's less extensible than a `type` enum if we later want more visual variants (e.g. `"pills"`), and it's a boolean rather than a named style.

### Additional Context

- Reference designs:
  - [Tremor — Radio Card Group](https://www.tremor.so/docs/inputs/radio-card-group)
  - [Tailwind Plus — Radio Groups (card designs)](https://tailwindcss.com/plus/ui-blocks/application-ui/forms/radio-groups)
  - [streamlit-extras — Card Selector](https://extras.streamlit.app/?extra=%F0%9F%83%8F+Card+Selector) (existing community implementation)
- Related: #2325 (`st.radio` with sections), #7184 (stretch horizontal radio), #11959 (consistent API for selectbox/pills/segmented_control/radio).

title: st.cache_data shares cache across st.Page pages for same-named functions with different source code
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

st.cache_data functions with the same name but different source code in different page files (loaded via st.navigation + st.Page) share the same cache. This is because st.Page executes all pages via exec() with
  __module__ == "__main__", and inspect.getsource() fails in that context. The fallback to func.__code__.co_code (bytecode) does not include string constants, so functions with identical structure but different inline strings (e.g., different SQL queries) produce the same cache key.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
# main.py
import streamlit as st

st.set_page_config(page_title="Cache Bug Demo", layout="wide")
pg = st.navigation(
    {
        "Page A": [st.Page("page_a.py", title="Page A")],
        "Page B": [st.Page("page_b.py", title="Page B")],
    }
)
pg.run()
# page_a.py
import streamlit as st


@st.cache_data(ttl=3600)
def load_data():
    return {"source": "page_a", "columns": ["col_a1", "col_a2"]}


data = load_data()
st.write("Page A data:", data)
st.write("Expected source: page_a, Got:", data["source"])
# page_b.py
import streamlit as st


@st.cache_data(ttl=3600)
def load_data():
    return {"source": "page_b", "columns": ["col_b1", "col_b2"]}


data = load_data()
st.write("Page B data:", data)
st.write("Expected source: page_b, Got:", data["source"])
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Create the three files above (main.py, page_a.py, page_b.py)
2. Run streamlit run main.py
3. Open Page A — displays source: page_a (correct)
4. Navigate to Page B — displays source: page_a (wrong, should be page_b)
5. Clear cache and open Page B first — displays source: page_b (correct)
6. Navigate to Page A — displays source: page_b (wrong, should be page_a)

### Expected Behavior

Each page's load_data() should have an independent cache, since they are defined in different files with different source code. Navigating between pages should return each page's own data.

### Current Behavior

Whichever page is loaded first caches its result under the function key. When the other page calls its own load_data(), the cached result from the first page is returned, because both functions produce the same cache key.

Root cause: In streamlit/navigation/page.py, st.Page.run() executes page scripts as:

module = types.ModuleType("__main__")
exec(code, module.__dict__)

This means func.__module__ is "__main__" for all pages. When inspect.getsource() fails in this exec() context, _make_function_key falls back to func.__code__.co_code, which does not include string constants — so
  structurally identical functions with different inline values produce the same key.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.55.0
- Python version: 3.14.3
- Operating System: macOS Tahoe Docker Desktop `FROM ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:python3.14-trixie-slim`
- Browser: Google Chrome 146.0.7680.178


### Additional Information

Related issue: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11157 (cache_data cannot detect difference in values of free variables). That issue covers a similar problem with closure variables, but the st.Page + exec() scenario is a distinct trigger.

Workaround: Give cached functions unique names per page (e.g., page_a_load_data, page_b_load_data).

title: Websocket Notify component to allow for Push-Notifications without polling
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Provide a component that will trigger a server-side render when it receives a message from a specified websocket server.

### Why?

Currently, streamlit requires an execution-flow, that starts in the browser. Usually, the user is interacting with a component (e.g. changing the value of input components, or pressing buttons, etc...), which triggers a render operation on the server-side. As a result of this paradigm, it is difficult to implement flows, that start with the server sending a push event to the client.

Some examples would be:

- A chatroom where the server notifies each of the participants that a new message was sent
- A live presentation where the presenter wants to push updates to all viewers, e.g. for highlighting some of the presented data, or for "changing to the next slide" by triggering a rerun that renders a new layout
- A dashboard that displays the current state of a system, which only changes sporadically and with long time-periods in between

All of these examples can be solved by polling for updates in an infinite loop, e.g. by using third-party components like [streamlit-autorefresh](https://github.com/kmcgrady/streamlit-autorefresh). The issue with this approach is that it results in a lot of wasted computation and requests where a rerun is triggered without any changes occurring. This also doesn't scale well with more and more session-threads.

This polling approach can be avoided by adding a component that only triggers a server-side rerun when it receives a websocket message on the client-side. The currently implemented execution-flow stays the same, since everything starts with a change on the client-side. 
But instead of requiring a user-interaction like a button-click, a websocket server can trigger it remotely.

### How?

On the python side, the implementation could look very similar to any of the existing input-widgets:

```python
# allow for http-header customization to enable authentication and individualized socket connections
raw_message: bytes = st.websocket_receive(url="https://some-websocket-server-address", http_headers={"Authorization": "Basic ..."})
# directly receive strings
# message: str = st.websocket_receive(url=..., encoding="utf-8")

# everytime a socket-message was received, this should trigger a redraw that shows the received message
st.write(raw_message.decode("utf-8"))
```

On the client side, the component would open a websocket using the specified URL and header fields and will update the component value as soon as it receives a message. *(I am not really familiar with js/ts... so I can't provide example code for this part of the implementation)*

## Added Bonus:

With such a component, the [multithreading section](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/concepts/design/multithreading) in the docs could also be updated with an additional example. Instead of having to join the worker-thread, it could be a deamon that starts a websocket-server and asynchronously communicates with the streamlit app via the proposed websocket component.

## Notes on Security

The proposed implementation requires the client to know both the URL and the custom header fields, and it should be highlighted in the documentation that those should only contain values that the client is allowed to know about.

### Additional Context

Issue #2927 proposes a very similar approach but also provides a [solution](https://github.com/FloWide/streamlit_callbacks/tree/main) that only uses websockets on the server-side, which doesn't really solve the polling issue. As far as I can tell, they added the socket-listener thread to the ScriptRunContext which can result in unexpected behavior and fatal errors and may not work for all streamlit commands *(according to the [multithreading documentation](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/concepts/design/multithreading))*. What I want to propose instead, is an implementation that starts at the client-side and fits more to the currently supported execution flow of streamlit apps.

title: Allow interactive resizing of `st.columns` via drag-and-drop
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add a `resizable: bool = False` parameter to `st.columns` that lets users resize columns by dragging the border between them. When enabled, a border indicator appears on hover between adjacent columns, and dragging adjusts their widths interactively. Resizing is purely client-side and does not trigger a rerun. Specced in [PR #14687](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/14687).

### Why?

Column widths in `st.columns` are static today — once set via `spec`, they can't be adjusted without changing code and rerunning. Interactive resizing helps with dashboard customization, data exploration (temporarily expand a column to see more), fine-tuning responsive layouts, and adjusting proportions live during demos/presentations. Current workarounds (layout presets via `st.selectbox`, CSS hacks in custom components, or just accepting fixed layouts) are clunky or fragile.

Related: #5003 (deactivate responsiveness of `st.columns`), #6592 (configurable column responsiveness threshold).

### How?

```python
st.columns(
    spec,
    *,
    gap="small",
    vertical_alignment="top",
    border=False,
    width="stretch",
    resizable=False,  # NEW
)
```

- `resizable=False` (default): current fixed-width behavior, no handles.
- `resizable=True`: drag the border between adjacent columns to resize.

Behavior (from the spec):
- **Hover indicator** + `col-resize` cursor over the resize area; border fades in/out (150ms).
- **Drag** resizes only the two adjacent columns; total row width is preserved (neighbor shrinks as one grows); other columns unchanged.
- **Double-click** the handle resets the adjacent pair to their original `spec` proportions.
- **Minimum width** of 64px prevents collapse; throttled updates for performance.
- **Keyboard**: Arrow Left/Right resize in 10px increments when focused.
- **Accessibility**: handles use `role="separator"`, `aria-orientation="vertical"`, `aria-valuenow/min/max`, and visible focus indicators (WCAG 2.1).
- **Touch**: drag works via touch; indicator shows on touch start.
- **Narrow viewports**: when columns stack (below `theme.breakpoints.columns`, 640px), handles are hidden and reappear when it widens.
- **State**: resized widths persist within the session (React state) and reset on refresh, a `spec`/column-count change, or stack/unstack.

### Alternatives considered (from the spec)

- `resizable: bool` (preferred) vs `resize_mode: Literal["off", "drag"]` — boolean chosen to match the existing `border=True` precedent and the binary nature of the feature; can migrate to an enum later if multiple resize modes are demanded.
- Naming: `resizable` over `adjustable` (too generic) / `flexible` (clashes with flexbox).

### Out of scope (future work)

Persist widths across sessions, snap-to-grid, per-column `min_width`/`max_width`, `on_resize` callback, and named/saveable layout presets.

### Additional Context

- Spec: [PR #14687 — \`[spec] Allow interactive resizing of st.columns\`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/14687) (`specs/2026-04-08-resizable-columns/product-spec.md`).

title: Add a `type="pills"` variant to `st.tabs` to show tabs as pills
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add a `type` parameter to `st.tabs` with a `"pills"` variant that renders the tab headers as pills (rounded, button-like segments) instead of the default underlined tab bar. Keep the same tab behavior — only the visual style of the tab headers changes.

### Why?

The underlined tab style is great for section navigation, but pill-style tabs are a very common, more compact and prominent look — especially for filters, view switchers, and dashboards. Today users approximate this with `st.pills`/`st.segmented_control` plus manual conditional rendering, which is more boilerplate and doesn't give the clean container-per-tab model that `st.tabs` provides.

### How?

Add a `type` parameter (default preserves today's look):

```python
tab1, tab2, tab3 = st.tabs(["Overview", "Details", "Settings"], type="pills")
with tab1:
    st.write("...")
```

- `type="default"` (or `"underline"`) — current tab bar.
- `type="pills"` — render the tab headers as pills.
- Everything else (content containers, active-tab state, etc.) stays identical.

### Additional Context

title: st.cache_resource does not invalidate when upstream schema changes on Streamlit Cloud
body:
## Description

When deploying a Streamlit app on Streamlit Cloud that uses `st.cache_resource` to cache a SQLAlchemy engine + SQLite database, schema changes in the seed script are not reflected until the app is manually rebooted.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Deploy an app that creates a SQLite DB on first run with `st.cache_resource`
2. Add new columns to the database schema in a code update
3. Push the update — Streamlit Cloud redeploys
4. The cached engine still points to the old database with the old schema
5. Queries referencing new columns fail with `OperationalError: no such column`

## Expected behavior

When the app code changes and Streamlit Cloud redeploys, `st.cache_resource` should detect that the underlying resource (DB schema) has changed and invalidate the cache.

## Actual behavior

The old cached engine persists across redeploys. The only workaround is:
- Manually rebooting the app from the Streamlit Cloud dashboard, or
- Adding a schema version check and calling `st.cache_resource.clear()` programmatically

## Environment

- Streamlit Cloud (managed)
- Python 3.11
- SQLAlchemy 2.0+
- SQLite (written to /tmp on Cloud due to read-only filesystem)

## Workaround

I implemented a schema version detection system that checks `PRAGMA table_info` on startup and calls `st.cache_resource.clear()` + re-seeds when columns are missing. This works but feels like it should be handled by the framework.

title: st.slider silently mis-represents dates outside the frontend number range
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

`st.slider` accepts `date`/`datetime` bounds that the frontend cannot represent exactly, and silently snaps them to a different instant instead of reporting the problem. The `int` and `float` paths already validate and raise a helpful `StreamlitAPIException`; the timelike path does not.

Timelike values are serialized as microseconds since the epoch and held in a JavaScript number on the frontend, so only about **1684-07-28 to 2255-06-05** round-trips exactly. Outside that, precision is lost.

`lib/streamlit/elements/widgets/slider.py` acknowledges the gap:

```python
elif all_timelikes:
    # No validation yet. TODO: check between 0001-01-01 to 9999-12-31
    pass
```

Worth noting the TODO's own target range is wrong — most of `0001`–`9999` is not representable, so validating to those limits would not have fixed it.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import datetime as dt
import streamlit as st

# Silently accepted, but min_value cannot be represented exactly:
st.slider("historical", min_value=dt.date(1600, 1, 1), max_value=dt.date(1700, 1, 1),
          value=dt.date(1600, 1, 1))

# Also silently accepted, both bounds unrepresentable:
st.slider("projection", min_value=dt.date(2300, 1, 1), max_value=dt.date(2400, 1, 1),
          value=dt.date(2300, 1, 1))

# Raises a bare OverflowError instead of a StreamlitAPIException:
st.slider("ancient", value=dt.date(1, 1, 1))
```

### Actual Behavior

Inspecting the serialized proto shows the bounds exceeding JavaScript's `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` with no error raised:

```
in-range 1900..2000      -> NO ERROR. min=-2208988800000000 max=946684800000000  JS-unsafe: none
historical 1600..1700    -> NO ERROR. min=-11676096000000000                      JS-unsafe: ['min']
far future 2300..2400    -> NO ERROR. min=10413792000000000 max=13569465600000000 JS-unsafe: ['min', 'max']
min date 0001..0002      -> OverflowError: date value out of range
```

Two distinct problems:

1. **Moderately out-of-range values are accepted and lose precision.** Years like 1600 or 2300 are ordinary in historical datasets and long-range projections, so this is not just an exotic edge case.
2. **Extreme values raise a bare `OverflowError`.** It comes from `prepared_value[0] - timedelta(days=14)`, which computes the *default* `min_value`/`max_value` even when the caller supplied both explicitly, and overflows next to `date.min`/`date.max`. This is not a `StreamlitAPIException`, so it surfaces as an unhandled Python error rather than actionable guidance.

### Expected Behavior

Out-of-range timelike bounds should raise a `StreamlitAPIException` naming the representable range, matching how the int and float paths already behave. Extreme values should produce that same message rather than an `OverflowError`.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: `develop` (reproduced at `f2648d7237`)
- Python version: 3.14.5
- OS: macOS 15.5

### Additional Information

Contrast with the existing int path, which is what the timelike path should mirror:

```
`max_value` (9007199254740992) must be <= (1 << 53) - 1
```

title: bug: @st.cache_data hash collision via fixed sampling seed and PIL P-mode palette omission
body:
## Summary

Two distinct cache-key collision bugs exist in `lib/streamlit/runtime/caching/hashing.py` that can cause `@st.cache_data` and `@st.cache_resource` to return stale or wrong data without any error.

---

## Bug 1 — Deterministic sampling seed enables adversarial hash collisions

**Affected code:** `_to_bytes()` in `hashing.py`, large-object sampling branches for Pandas Series/DataFrame, Polars Series/DataFrame, and NumPy arrays.

**Root cause:** When a data structure exceeds the sampling threshold (`_PANDAS_ROWS_LARGE = 50_000` rows or `_NP_SIZE_LARGE = 500_000` elements), the code samples a smaller subset before hashing. The sampling seed is hardcoded:

```python
# Pandas
series_obj.sample(n=_PANDAS_SAMPLE_SIZE, random_state=0)
df_obj.sample(n=_PANDAS_SAMPLE_SIZE, random_state=0)

# Polars
obj.sample(n=_PANDAS_SAMPLE_SIZE, seed=0)

# NumPy
state = np.random.RandomState(0)
np_obj = state.choice(flat, size=_NP_SAMPLE_SIZE)
```

Because the seed is always `0`, the sampled row indices are globally fixed and known in advance. An adversary who knows which indices will be sampled can craft two structurally different inputs that produce the same hash by only modifying non-sampled positions.

**Minimal reproduction (NumPy):**

```python
import numpy as np, hashlib
from streamlit.runtime.caching.hashing import update_hash
from streamlit.runtime.caching.cache_type import CacheType

_NP_SIZE_LARGE  = 500_000
_NP_SAMPLE_SIZE = 100_000

def get_hash(obj):
    h = hashlib.md5(usedforsecurity=False)
    update_hash(obj, h, CacheType.DATA)
    return h.hexdigest()

total = _NP_SIZE_LARGE + 10_000
arr_a = np.zeros(total, dtype=np.float64)
arr_b = arr_a.copy()

# Compute which indices are NOT sampled (fixed because seed=0)
sampled = np.random.RandomState(0).choice(np.arange(total), size=_NP_SAMPLE_SIZE)
mask = np.ones(total, dtype=bool)
mask[sampled] = False
arr_b[mask] = 255.0  # modify only non-sampled positions

print(get_hash(arr_a))  # same hash
print(get_hash(arr_b))  # same hash — COLLISION
```

**Minimal reproduction (Pandas):**

```python
import pandas as pd, numpy as np, hashlib
from streamlit.runtime.caching.hashing import update_hash
from streamlit.runtime.caching.cache_type import CacheType

_PANDAS_ROWS_LARGE  = 50_000
_PANDAS_SAMPLE_SIZE = 10_000

def get_hash(obj):
    h = hashlib.md5(usedforsecurity=False)
    update_hash(obj, h, CacheType.DATA)
    return h.hexdigest()

n = _PANDAS_ROWS_LARGE + 5_000
df_a = pd.DataFrame({"val": np.zeros(n)})
df_b = df_a.copy()

sampled = df_a.sample(n=_PANDAS_SAMPLE_SIZE, random_state=0).index
all_idx = pd.Index(range(n))
non_sampled = all_idx.difference(sampled)
df_b.loc[non_sampled, "val"] = 99.0

print(get_hash(df_a))  # same hash
print(get_hash(df_b))  # same hash — COLLISION
```

**Impact:** `@st.cache_resource` is shared across all user sessions. An adversary who can send a request to the app can pre-compute a colliding payload and silently poison the cache, causing all subsequent users to receive the adversary's data instead of the real result — with no error raised.

---

## Bug 2 — PIL P-mode images: palette bytes omitted from hash

**Affected code:** PIL `Image.Image` branch in `_to_bytes()`.

**Root cause:** For palette-indexed (`mode="P"`) PIL images, `tobytes()` returns only the palette index per pixel, not the actual color table. Two images with identical pixel indices but different color palettes produce identical hashes despite being visually distinct.

```python
# current code
np_array = np.frombuffer(pil_obj.tobytes(), dtype="uint8")
return self.to_bytes(np_array)
```

**Minimal reproduction:**

```python
from PIL import Image
import hashlib, numpy as np
from streamlit.runtime.caching.hashing import update_hash
from streamlit.runtime.caching.cache_type import CacheType

def get_hash(obj):
    h = hashlib.md5(usedforsecurity=False)
    update_hash(obj, h, CacheType.DATA)
    return h.hexdigest()

img_a = Image.new("P", (100, 100), 0)
img_b = Image.new("P", (100, 100), 0)

palette_a = [0] * 768
palette_b = [0] * 768
palette_a[0:3] = [0, 0, 0]    # index 0 → black
palette_b[0:3] = [255, 0, 0]  # index 0 → red

img_a.putpalette(palette_a)
img_b.putpalette(palette_b)

print(get_hash(img_a))  # same hash
print(get_hash(img_b))  # same hash — COLLISION, despite different colors
```

**Impact:** Two visually different images (e.g., a legitimate chart vs. a manipulated one) share the same cache key. The first cached result is returned for all subsequent inputs regardless of actual image content.

---

## Proposed Fix

A fix has been submitted as PR #14610. The approach:

1. **Sampling seed**: Derive the seed from the data (hash of first row / first 64 elements) so that sampled indices are content-dependent. Falls back to `seed=0` for unhashable payloads to preserve the existing pickle fallback path.
2. **PIL P-mode**: Prepend `getpalette()` bytes to `tobytes()` output before hashing.

---

## Environment

- Streamlit version: all versions with large-object sampling (introduced with the sampling optimization)
- Python: 3.10+
- OS: Linux / macOS / Windows (platform-independent)

title: A custom component cannot own the `r` or `c` keys: the app-level shortcuts fire regardless
body:
### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary Streamlit's `r` (rerun) and `c` (clear cache) shortcuts fire whenever focus is on anything other than a small set of native form elements. A custom component that binds those keys cannot keep them: even a capture-phase listener calling `preventDefault()`, `stopPropagation()` and `stopImmediatePropagation()` sees the key and the app still acts on it. This makes single-letter keyboard interfaces — the norm in accessible visualization libraries, where a blind user drives a chart from the keyboard — impossible to build on Streamlit's non-iframe component path. ### Reproducible Code Example ```Python # app.py import streamlit as st st.session_state["runs"] = st.session_state.get("runs", 0) + 1 st.write(f"RUNS={st.session_state['runs']}") st.text_input("a text input") st.button("a button") st.markdown( '
' "a custom widget
", unsafe_allow_html=True, ) ``` ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Save the snippet above as `app.py` and run `streamlit run app.py`. 2. Click the bordered div to focus it, press r, and watch `RUNS` increment. 3. To confirm a component cannot defend the key, run this in the browser console and press r again with the div focused: ```js document.addEventListener('keydown', e => { if (e.key === 'r') { e.preventDefault(); e.stopPropagation(); e.stopImmediatePropagation(); } }, true); // capture phase — the earliest a listener can run ``` ### Expected Behavior A component should be able to opt out of app-level key handling for the region it owns, or the exemption should extend to focus inside a registered custom component. ### Current Behavior The capture-phase listener above receives the event, and the app reruns anyway. title: st.cache_data on class methods intermittently raises UnserializableReturnValueError
body: ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary When `@st.cache_data` decorates a method that returns a custom class instance, `pickle.dumps()` intermittently fails with `PicklingError: Can't pickle : it's not the same object as X`. This happens because Streamlit's `LocalSourcesWatcher` deletes watched modules from `sys.modules` on file changes, creating a class identity mismatch between the instance being pickled and the class found by pickle's resolution mechanism. ### Reproducible Code Example ```Python ### `repro_model.py` """Local module — simulates any user-defined class in a local .py file.""" class MyResult: def __init__(self, output: str = "", value: int = 0): self.output = output self.value = value ### `repro_agent.py` """ Helper module imported once by repro.py. Simulates agents/__init__.py — only loaded once, holds a stale class reference after sys.modules is invalidated by the file watcher. """ import streamlit as st from repro_model import MyResult # bound once at import time @st.cache_data(show_spinner=False) def get_result(key: str) -> MyResult: import time time.sleep(0.1) return MyResult(output=f"result for {key}", value=42) ### `repro.py` — run with `streamlit run repro.py` import streamlit as st import sys import importlib import repro_agent # imported once — simulates agents/__init__.py st.title("cache_data pickle race condition repro") if st.button("1) Normal call (works)"): try: result = repro_agent.get_result("test") st.success(f"Got: {result.output}") except Exception as e: st.error(f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}") if st.button("2) Simulate file-watcher then call (fails, and keeps failing)"): # This is exactly what LocalSourcesWatcher.on_path_changed does: # for wm in self._watched_modules.values(): # del sys.modules[wm.module_name] if "repro_model" in sys.modules: del sys.modules["repro_model"] # Re-import creates a NEW class object in sys.modules importlib.import_module("repro_model") # Clear cache so pickle.dumps is attempted again repro_agent.get_result.clear() try: # repro_agent still uses the OLD MyResult class. # pickle resolves sys.modules["repro_model"].MyResult → NEW class. # OLD is not NEW → PicklingError → UnserializableReturnValueError result = repro_agent.get_result("test") st.success(f"Got: {result.output}") except Exception as e: st.error(f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}") ``` ### Steps To Reproduce **Steps:** 1. `streamlit run repro.py` 2. Click **"1) Normal call"** — succeeds. 3. Click **"2) Simulate file-watcher"** — fails with `UnserializableReturnValueError`. 4. Click **"1) Normal call"** again — **also fails**, until Streamlit is restarted. ### Expected Behavior Step 4 demonstrates persistence: `repro_agent` is never re-imported, so it keeps using the old class, while `sys.modules` keeps the new one. Neither step 3 not step 4 should throw the `UnserializableReturnValueError`. Expected behavior : ### Current Behavior `UnserializableReturnValueError` is thrown ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. ### Debug info - **Streamlit**: 1.55.0 - **Python**: 3.13.7 - **OS**: Windows 11 / Linux (Kubernetes) - Occurs more frequently in local dev (active filesystem) than in deployed containers ### Additional Information > **Disclosure**: This bug report was written by an LLM (Claude) after a deep investigation into a production issue. The root cause analysis, reproduction script, and identified problematic code path are all LLM-generated ## Suggested Fixes ### Option A: Chain the original exception (low-effort, improves DX) In `_handle_cache_miss`, chain the original exception so users can see the real error: ```python raise UnserializableReturnValueError( return_value=computed_value, func=self._info.func ) from ex # <-- add "from ex" ``` ### Option B: Guard `write_result` against stale class references Before calling `pickle.dumps()` in `DataCache.write_result`, re-import the module and verify class identity: ```python import importlib cls = type(value) mod = sys.modules.get(cls.__module__) if mod is not None: current_cls = getattr(mod, cls.__qualname__, None) if current_cls is not None and current_cls is not cls: # Module was reloaded — update the instance's class to the current one value.__class__ = current_cls ``` ### Option C: Don't delete modules from `sys.modules` preemptively Instead of deleting all watched modules on every file change, only invalidate the module that actually changed. Or defer the deletion to the start of the next script run rather than doing it immediately from the watcher thread. ## Workaround Return only pickle-safe primitives (dicts, strings, numbers) from `@st.cache_data` functions, and reconstruct custom objects outside the cache boundary: ```python @st.cache_data(show_spinner=False) def _cached_call(key: str) -> dict: result = do_expensive_work(key) return result.__dict__ # dict is always pickle-safe def get_result(key: str) -> MyResult: return MyResult(**_cached_call(key)) ```

title: WebSocket protocol error path ignores client.showErrorDetails and leaks stack traces
body:
## Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

## Summary

When a malformed WebSocket `BackMsg` frame fails protobuf deserialization, Streamlit uses a path that bypasses uncaught app exception redaction. Because of this, `client.showErrorDetails` does not apply. Stack traces with file paths and line numbers can reach the client. I reproduced this on 1.61.1.

## Reproducible Code Example

```python
# app.py
import streamlit as st

st.write("hello")

# send_malformed_frame.py
import asyncio
import websockets


async def main():
    async with websockets.connect(
        "ws://localhost:8501/_stcore/stream",
        subprotocols=["streamlit"],
    ) as ws:
        # b"\\xff" is not a valid BackMsg protobuf frame.
        await ws.send(b"\\xff")


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Run `app.py` on Streamlit 1.61.1.
2. Set `client.showErrorDetails = "none"`.
3. In a second terminal, run `send_malformed_frame.py`.
4. The script connects to `ws://localhost:8501/_stcore/stream` with subprotocol `streamlit` and sends `b"\xff"`.
5. Observe that the script receives a `ForwardMsg` Exception payload.
6. Observe that the Exception payload contains `DecodeError` and a stack trace entry with an absolute file path.

## Expected Behavior

Protocol-level WebSocket errors should return a generic client error or close the connection. They should not expose stack traces, file paths, or line numbers to the client. `client.showErrorDetails` should not be bypassed.

## Current Behavior

The deserialization exception goes through `AppSession._create_exception_message()`. That method calls `exception_utils.marshall(...)` without `is_uncaught_app_exception=True`. The redaction logic does not run. On the event-loop thread there is no script run context, so traceback filtering does not remove internal frames. In my local repro, the returned Exception payload had message `Error parsing message with type 'BackMsg'`, type `DecodeError`, and a stack trace entry that exposed `lib/streamlit/web/server/starlette/starlette_websocket.py`.

## Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

## Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.61.1
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: Any
- Browser: N/A

## Additional Information

Split from [issue #16386](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16386). This also affects the generic `AppSession.handle_backmsg()` exception path, not only protobuf deserialization failures.

title: Axios 1.14.1 and 0.30.4 supply chain attack
body:
axios@1.14.1 and axios@0.30.4 are compromised

frontend/lib/package-lock.json uses axios^1.13.6 currently, making new builds potentially vulnerable. Axios 1.14.1 has since been removed from npm, but vulnerable versions could exist in npm caches and other registries.

> On March 30, 2026, StepSecurity identified two malicious versions of the widely used axios HTTP client library published to npm: axios@1.14.1 and axios@0.30.4. Both versions were published using the compromised npm credentials of a lead axios maintainer, bypassing the project's normal GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline. The attacker changed the maintainer's account email to an anonymous ProtonMail address and manually published the poisoned packages via the npm CLI.

Source: https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/axios-compromised-on-npm-malicious-versions-drop-remote-access-trojan
Axios Github Issue: https://github.com/axios/axios/issues/10604

title: st.metric sparkline (chart_data) fails to render after a no-data -> data transition
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When an `st.metric` (that has previously been rendered with a sparkline and then again with no data) is re-rendered with `chart_data` going from empty/None (no sparkline) to a populated list (sparkline expected), the sparkline frequently fails to mount. The metric value and delta update correctly; only the embedded chart is missing. It reproduces reliably on the first
"no data -> data" transition and is unaffected by the data itself.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import time

import streamlit as st

st.set_page_config(page_title="Metric Chart Issue Demo", layout="wide")

# Realistic-looking weekly data (~52 weeks)
# fmt: off
CHART_DATA_WITH = [
    5, 8, 12, 7, 9, 15, 11, 13, 8, 10, 14, 6, 9, 11, 13, 7,
    10, 12, 8, 14, 9, 11, 7, 13, 10, 8, 12, 9, 11, 14, 7, 10,
    13, 8, 11, 9, 12, 7, 14, 10, 8, 13, 11, 9, 12, 7, 10, 14,
    8, 11, 13, 9,
]  # 52 values
# fmt: on

CHART_DATA_WITHOUT = []

st.title("Metric Chart Rendering Issue")

use_workaround = st.toggle("Enable Container Workaround", value=False)
st.caption("Toggle ON to see the mitigation that reduces (but doesn't eliminate) the issue")

# Dropdown (default to "With Data")
dataset = st.selectbox("Select Dataset", ["With Data", "Without Data"], index=0)

# Determine data based on selection
if dataset == "With Data":
    chart_1 = CHART_DATA_WITH
    chart_2 = [x * 2 for x in CHART_DATA_WITH]
    chart_3 = [x * 0.5 for x in CHART_DATA_WITH]
    chart_4 = [x * 1.5 for x in CHART_DATA_WITH]
    metric_val = 42
    delta_val = 5
else:
    chart_1 = CHART_DATA_WITHOUT
    chart_2 = CHART_DATA_WITHOUT
    chart_3 = CHART_DATA_WITHOUT
    chart_4 = CHART_DATA_WITHOUT
    metric_val = 0
    delta_val = 0

# Generate timestamp for workaround keys
if use_workaround:
    base_timestamp = int(time.time() * 1000)

# Four metric cards - conditional rendering based on workaround toggle
if not use_workaround:
    # Path A: No workaround (default)
    col1, col2, col3, col4 = st.columns(4)

    with col1:
        st.metric(
            label="Metric 1",
            value=metric_val,
            delta=delta_val,
            delta_color="normal",
            chart_data=chart_1 if chart_1 else None,
            chart_type="bar",
            border=True,
        )

    with col2:
        st.metric(
            label="Metric 2",
            value=int(metric_val * 2),
            delta=int(delta_val * 2),
            delta_color="normal",
            chart_data=chart_2 if chart_2 else None,
            chart_type="bar",
            border=True,
        )

    with col3:
        st.metric(
            label="Metric 3",
            value=metric_val,
            delta=delta_val,
            delta_color="normal",
            chart_data=chart_3 if chart_3 else None,
            chart_type="bar",
            border=True,
        )

    with col4:
        st.metric(
            label="Metric 4",
            value=int(metric_val * 1.5),
            delta=round(delta_val * 1.5, 1),
            delta_color="normal",
            chart_data=chart_4 if chart_4 else None,
            chart_type="bar",
            border=True,
        )
else:
    # Path B: With single-container workaround
    col1, col2, col3, col4 = st.columns(4)

    with col1, st.container(key=f"col1_{dataset}_{base_timestamp}"):
        st.metric(
            label="Metric 1",
            value=metric_val,
            delta=delta_val,
            delta_color="normal",
            chart_data=chart_1 if chart_1 else None,
            chart_type="bar",
            border=True,
        )

    with col2, st.container(key=f"col2_{dataset}_{base_timestamp}"):
        st.metric(
            label="Metric 2",
            value=int(metric_val * 2),
            delta=int(delta_val * 2),
            delta_color="normal",
            chart_data=chart_2 if chart_2 else None,
            chart_type="bar",
            border=True,
        )

    with col3, st.container(key=f"col3_{dataset}_{base_timestamp}"):
        st.metric(
            label="Metric 3",
            value=metric_val,
            delta=delta_val,
            delta_color="normal",
            chart_data=chart_3 if chart_3 else None,
            chart_type="bar",
            border=True,
        )

    with col4, st.container(key=f"col4_{dataset}_{base_timestamp}"):
        st.metric(
            label="Metric 4",
            value=int(metric_val * 1.5),
            delta=round(delta_val * 1.5, 1),
            delta_color="normal",
            chart_data=chart_4 if chart_4 else None,
            chart_type="bar",
            border=True,
        )

st.markdown("---")
st.markdown("""
### How to Reproduce

**Without Workaround (Toggle OFF - default):**
1. Start with "With Data" selected (default)
2. Switch to "Without Data" - charts should disappear
3. Switch back to "With Data" - **charts are expected to fail to appear**

**With Workaround (Toggle ON):**
1. Enable the "Container Workaround" toggle above
2. Repeat steps 1-3 - charts should appear more reliably (but may still occasionally fail)

---

**Expected**: Charts appear when switching to "With Data"  
**Actual (no workaround)**: Charts consistently fail to render after first transition  
**Actual (with workaround)**: Charts usually render, but may still occasionally fail

**Workaround**: Wrap each metric in a keyed container with a timestamp-based unique key. 
This forces Streamlit to create fresh component instances on each render, which appears 
to reduce (but not eliminate) the rendering issue.

---

**Environment**: Streamlit 1.57.0, 1.60.0, and 1.61.1 (reproduces on all)

**Other Mitigation Strategies Attempted:**
- Double-container wrapping (nested containers with unique keys) - slightly better than 
  single container
- Using `st.empty()` placeholders before containers - no improvement
- Session state counters for key generation - worse performance
- Explicit data validation (converting empty lists to None) - no improvement

The single-container workaround shown in this demo provides the best balance of simplicity 
and reliability improvement.
""")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Instructions also included inline in code example to view while executing.

Steps (with the "Container Workaround" toggle OFF):

1. Load the page with "With Data" selected. All four metric cards show sparklines.
2. Select "Without Data". Charts clear; values go to 0. (expected)
3. Select "With Data" again. Values return, but the sparklines do NOT render.

Additional browser console check:

The sparkline renders as `[data-testid="stMetricChart"]` containing an `<svg>`.
Run in the browser console after step 3:

```
    (() => {
      const m = [...document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid="stMetric"]')];
      return {
        cards: m.length,
        withChart: m.filter(c => c.querySelector('[data-testid="stMetricChart"] svg')).length,
      };
    })()
```

Healthy: `withChart === cards`. Bug: `withChart < cards` (typically 0) after
the transition, even though the metric values are correct.



### Expected Behavior

- Expected: selecting "With Data" repopulates both the values and the sparklines. Continually going between data/no data should update the chart correctly each time
- Actual: values repopulate; sparklines are sometimes absent after the transition. Somewhat better with extra container hacks, but never 100% correct

### Current Behavior

All covered in the code, but in general:
* I display a few metric cards with data to start.
* Then I change to the card not being backed by any data by setting `chart_data` to None or an empty list (this is an approximation of what my app is doing, but gets the point across...I have data sometimes and then users can switch to selections that have no data for whatever reason). Everything works to here
* Then another selection adds data back to the the card. 
* Everything on the cards functions as expected except the sparkline chart. The chart may or may not re-render. In my experience, without any mitigation the chart will not re-render the vast majority of the time. With shenanigans like additional container indirection, it might re-render more often but never have I seen it work every time.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit: reproduced on 1.57.0, 1.60.0, and 1.61.1 (not fixed by the upgrades)
- Python: 3.13
- Browser: Chromium 149.0.7827.200 and Firefox 140.12.0esr (also observed in normal app use across browsers and operating systems including MacOS and Windows of various versions. I cannot tell you what browsers were involved there tho)
- OS: Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.8 (Plow)


### Additional Information

- Direction-specific: "no data -> data" fails; "data -> no data" is fine.
- Wrapping each metric in a keyed `st.container` with a per-run unique key reduces the failure rate but does not eliminate it. A second nested keyed container helps marginally more.
- Using a monotonic session-state counter for the keys made it worse, and converting empty lists to None had no effect - suggesting the issue is a frontend component-lifecycle timing race, not key collision or data handling.
- In case it's useful, in my case the dropdown selection would map to a DB query that is returned in a pandas dataframe. Once the query has been fetched once, it's cached for 24 hrs

title: st.cache_data / st.cache_resource provide no way to inspect cache size or memory usage
body:
## Description

In production Streamlit apps that cache large datasets, developers have no programmatic way to answer:
- How much memory is my cache consuming?
- Which cached function is using the most memory?
- How many entries are currently cached?
- Which entries are closest to TTL expiration?

The only option is `st.cache_data.clear()` — a nuclear option that evicts everything.

## Use Case

Streamlit apps deployed on memory-constrained containers (512MB on Community Cloud, small Docker/K8s pods) can hit OOM kills with no advance warning. Developers set `max_entries` and `ttl` through trial and error because there is no way to observe the cache at runtime.

## Proposed API

```python
info = st.cache_data.info()
# Returns:
# {
#     "load_data": {"entries": 12, "approx_bytes": 52428800, "oldest_entry_age": timedelta(minutes=45)},
#     "fetch_users": {"entries": 3, "approx_bytes": 1048576, "oldest_entry_age": timedelta(minutes=12)},
# }
```

This would enable:
1. Monitoring dashboards for cache health
2. Informed decisions about TTL and max_entries tuning
3. Debugging memory issues without restarting the app
4. Conditional clearing of specific function caches when approaching limits

## Context

Related but distinct from #14357 (cache_resource validate args) and #3018 (configurable cache location). Neither addresses runtime introspection of cache state.

title: Deduplicate identical `st.cache_data` return values to save memory
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

`st.cache_data` stores one serialized (pickled) blob per cache key, where the key is derived only from the function + input arguments. If a function returns the *same* value (e.g. the same dataframe) for many different inputs, each of those cache entries stores a full, redundant copy. We could recognize identical serialized return values (e.g. by hashing the serialized value bytes) and store the payload only once, with each cache key referencing it — saving memory (and disk when persisted).

### Why?

- **Memory savings:** Functions that frequently return the same object under different arguments currently blow up memory with duplicate copies. Content-addressed storage would keep a single shared copy.
- Could also help mitigate memory issues when replaying widgets in cached functions (a common source of memory crashes), since the shared thing would be the stored bytes.
- Complements existing cache memory work like #2911 (limit cache size by memory footprint) and #14558 (inspect cache memory usage).

### How?

Introduce a content-addressed layer for cached values:

- On write, hash the serialized **value payload** and store it once in a blob store keyed by that digest; the per-argument cache key stores a lightweight reference (digest + metadata) plus a reference count.
- On read, resolve the reference to the shared blob and deserialize as usual.
- Evict a blob only when no cache key references it anymore.

Key implementation note: today the pickled entry is a `CachedResult` that bundles the value **and** per-call metadata (replayed `messages`, `main_id`/`sidebar_id`, `stored_at`). Because that metadata differs per key, hashing the whole `CachedResult` blob wouldn't dedup much — the design should **separate the value payload (content-addressable, shared) from the per-key metadata** so identical values actually collide.

Notes:
- Copy semantics are preserved: `st.cache_data` still returns independent copies on each read (values are deserialized per call); only the *stored bytes* are shared.
- Likely only worth it above a size threshold, given the hashing/bookkeeping overhead.

### Additional Context

Current behavior (from a code investigation): storage keys are built from input args only (`_make_value_key`), the return value is `pickle.dumps(CachedResult(...))` and written via `storage.set(value_key, bytes)`, and the in-memory layer is a `TTLCache[str, bytes]` with one independent blob per key. There is no hashing of the return-value bytes and no cross-key dedup today (the only "dedup" in the caching code is background-refresh scheduling).

- Related: #2911 (limit cache by memory footprint), #14558 (inspect cache memory usage), #13992 (cache observability).

title: Overlap between cache spinner and progress bar text
body: Currently, the cache spinner overlaps with the text of the progress bar. This is a minor cosmetic issue that doesn't affect functionality, but it slightly impacts the UI's readability. It could be easily fixed by adding a st.space. ```python import time import streamlit as st @st.cache_data(show_spinner=True, show_time=True) def foo(): # Add a space to prevent overlapping # st.space("medium") pbar = st.progress(0.0, text="Loading...") for i in range(1, 101): pbar.progress(i / 100, f"({i} / 100) Computing...") time.sleep(1) foo() ````

title: Deleting a widget's session_state key leaves the frontend showing the stale value (backend/frontend divergence for one rerun)
body: ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary Deleting a keyed widget's entry from `st.session_state` (e.g. `del st.session_state["foo"]` inside a callback) does not reset the widget, but can lead to an inconsistency between frontend and backend. The Python side returns the widget's *default* value for that run, but the frontend keeps displaying the old value, so backend and frontend disagree. On the **next** rerun the backend silently re-adopts the stale frontend value, so the deletion is effectively undone. ### Reproducible Code Example ```Python import streamlit as st text = st.text_input("Foo", value="default", key="foo") st.write("widget returned:", repr(text)) def populate(): st.session_state["foo"] = "hello" def delete(): del st.session_state["foo"] st.button("Populate", on_click=populate) st.button("Delete", on_click=delete) st.button("Noop") ``` ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Run the app. 2. Click **Populate** (callback sets `st.session_state["foo"] = "hello"`). The text input now shows `hello` and `widget returned: 'hello'`. 3. Click **Delete** (callback runs `del st.session_state["foo"]`). 4. Observe the text input on screen vs. the `widget returned:` line. 5. Click **Noop** (any interaction that triggers a plain rerun) and observe again. ### Expected Behavior The widget value in the frontent and backend should be consistent. After deleting a widget's key in session state, it should presumably fall back to its default value. ### Current Behavior - After clicking Delete, the backend returns `widget returned: "default''` , but the frontend widget still displays `"hello"`. - After the next rerun (step 5), the backend re-adopts the stale frontend value, and both show `"hello"`. ### Screenshot ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. ### Debug info - Streamlit version: 1.59.2 - Python version: 3.14.6 - Operating System: Ubuntu 22.04 - Browser: Chromium ### Additional Information Likely related: #5442

title: Revamp `streamlit hello` to showcase the latest features, advanced dashboards, and agentic UIs
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Revamp the built-in `streamlit hello` demo app to reflect what modern Streamlit can do. The current demos (animation, plotting, mapping, dataframe) are dated and don't represent today's feature set. Refocus it on advanced dashboards and agentic/chat UIs, using the latest layout, theming, and data elements.

### Why?

`streamlit hello` is one of the first things new users run, so it shapes their first impression and sense of what's possible. Today it undersells Streamlit — it predates chat elements, the newer layout primitives, updated theming, richer widgets, and dashboard-oriented components. A refreshed showcase would be a much stronger onboarding and marketing surface and double as living example code for current best practices.

### How?

Rebuild the demos around modern, high-impact use cases, for example:

- **Advanced dashboard** — multi-column/flex layout, metrics, cards, tabs, and rich charts, with theming that looks polished out of the box.
- **Agentic / chat UI** — `st.chat_message` / `st.chat_input`, streaming responses (`st.write_stream`), status/progress, and tool-call style interactions.
- **Data exploration** — modern `st.dataframe` features (column config, selections, editing) and interactive filtering.

Additional considerations:
- Use current layout, theming, and widget features throughout (retire deprecated patterns).
- Keep it dependency-light and fast to launch.
- Structure it as clean, idiomatic example code users can learn from and copy.

### Additional Context

- `streamlit hello` lives in `lib/streamlit/hello/`.

title: BUG: Stale widgets from previous page runs are not removed when a spinner is later invoked
body:

### Summary

In certain circumstances, UI elements from previous page executions unexpectedly remain on the screen.

This is possibly related to #14249 , which was apparently caused by a recent change #13849 and fixed by #14251. However, this bug occurs in a slightly context, without use of tabs or cached functions, so I think it's a distinct issue.

I've boiled down a minimal reproducible example below. The bug seems to occur if a call to `st.spinner` is made after a selection widget, and the precise behaviour varies depending on whether Expander containers are used and whether other objects are rendered before the spinner.

I noticed two slight variants of this bug, depending on whether some markdown is rendered before the call to st.spinner. In each cases a different stale widget is left:

### Variant 1: without markdown call

As per the code example below: the "Button 1" widget (and Expander box) remains visible, but the "Button 2" widget is cleared.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6e22f030-7a8a-4cfd-9c7a-95f966c704e4

### Variant 2: with markdown call

As above but uncommenting the call to `st.markdown`: now the "Button 1" widget is indeed cleaned up properly, but the "Button 2" widget is now erroneously left.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5a6b9243-dd68-4154-8eab-6db307caa2c5

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

st.write("Streamlit version:", st.__version__)

choice = st.radio("Radio", options=["A", "B"])
if choice == "B":
    with st.expander("Inner", expanded=True):
        st.button("Button 1")
    st.button("Button 2")

# Uncommenting this line changes the behaviour of the bug:
# st.markdown("Some text")

with st.spinner():
    pass
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Click "B"
2. Click "A"

### Expected Behavior

When "A" is selected, the Expander and Button widgets should be hidden.

### Current Behavior

When "A" is selected, the Expander box and "Button 1" Button remain visible.

title: Allow linking (and embedding) any individual element in a Streamlit app
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Allow users to create a link that points directly to a specific element in a Streamlit app — similar to how you can link to a block in Notion. Opening such a link would scroll to (and optionally highlight) that element, and it could also be used to embed just that single element elsewhere.

### Why?

Two main use cases:

1. **Point someone to a specific element** — e.g. share a link that jumps straight to a particular chart, table, or section instead of "scroll down to the third chart".
2. **Embed a specific element** — embed just one chart or part of a page into Notion, Medium, blog posts, etc. This pairs with OEmbed support (to embed Streamlit apps/elements in other services).

### How?

- Give elements a stable, addressable anchor/ID (auto-generated, and/or user-settable, e.g. via the existing `key`).
- Support a URL fragment (e.g. `?...#element-id` or a query param) that, on load, scrolls to and briefly highlights the target element.
- Provide a UI affordance to copy an element's link (similar to the anchor icon on Markdown headers, but for any element).
- For embedding, allow rendering a single addressed element standalone (tie in with OEmbed / embed mode) so it can be embedded in other services.

### Additional Context

- Inspired by linking to a block in Notion.
- Related: #636 (scrolling to an element), and OEmbed support for embedding Streamlit apps/elements in other services (Notion, Medium, etc.).

title: Validation function of `st.cache_resource()` to receive the same arguments that are passed to the cached function.
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

As seen [here](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/caching-and-state/st.cache_resource#:~:text=receives%20the%20cached%20value%20as%20its%20only%20parameter%20and%20it%20must%20return%20a%20boolean.) in the documentation of `st.cache_resource()`, `validate`
> receives the cached value as its only parameter and it must return a boolean.

I'd like the validation function to receive the same arguments that are passed to the cached function.

### Why?

As seen [here](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/caching-and-state/st.cache_resource#:~:text=is%20useful%20e.g.%20to%20check%20the%20health%20of%20database%20connections.) in the documentation, `validate`
> is useful e.g. to check the health of database connections.

The cached function could be responsible for caching multiple database connections, based on an argument it receives. The validation function would then need to receive the same argument(s) to check the health of the corresponding database connection.

As a simpler, more concrete example, I'd like to cache the content of big files and invalidate the cache if the files change. Note the addition of the `path` argument in `validate`:
```py
@st.cache_resource(validate=lambda cached, path: cached[0] == path.stat().st_mtime)
def get_big_file(path: Path):
    return path.stat().st_mtime, load_big_file_with_expensive_compute(path)
```

Side note: depending on the situation, `st.cache_data()` might be more appropriate than `@st.cache_resource()`, so the `validate` argument could also be added to `st.cache_data()`.

### How?

I can think of two ways to avoid a breaking change to the current `validate` function:
1. We could inspect if `validate` expects arguments, something like
   ```py
   validate(*args, *kwargs) if inspect.signature(validate).parameters else validate()
   ```
1. We could introduce a new function like `validate_with_args`. The two functions would be mutually exclusive.

### Additional Context

As a workaround, I can create one cached function for every file:
```py
# File 1
@st.cache_resource(validate=lambda cached: cached[0] == path1.stat().st_mtime)
def get_big_file1():
    return path1.stat().st_mtime, load_big_file_with_expensive_compute(path)

# File 2
@st.cache_resource(validate=lambda cached: cached[0] == path2.stat().st_mtime)
def get_big_file2():
    return path2.stat().st_mtime, load_big_file_with_expensive_compute(path)
```
But if I my paths are dynamic, that gets complicated. I implemented a decorator that dynamically creates a cached function (with a unique `__qualname__`) as well as the corresponding validation function for each path. See `cache_file` below.

Without the `__qualname__`, the first file would work, but not any subsequent file, as the first `validate` function would be used for all the files. That's feels hacky/fragile.

```py
from collections.abc import Callable
from pathlib import Path
from typing import TypeVar
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

import streamlit as st
from streamlit.testing.v1 import AppTest

T = TypeVar("T")


def cache_file(f: Callable[[Path], T]) -> Callable[[Path], T]:
    def decorated(path: Path, **kwargs):
        def validate(cached):
            return cached[0] == path.stat().st_mtime

        def cached(path: Path, **kwargs):
            return path.stat().st_mtime, f(path, **kwargs)

        cached.__qualname__ = str(path)

        return st.cache_resource(cached, validate=validate)(path, **kwargs)[1]

    return decorated


def _test_app(path0, path1):
    from pathlib import Path

    import streamlit as st

    from apps.utils import cache_file

    @cache_file
    def get_text(path: Path):
        return path.read_text()

    st.text(get_text(path0))

    st.text(get_text(path1))


@patch.object(Path, "read_text", autospec=True, wraps=Path.read_text)
def test_cache_file(mock_read_text: MagicMock, tmp_path: Path):
    paths = (tmp_path / "0.txt", tmp_path / "1.txt")
    paths[0].write_text("0A")
    paths[1].write_text("1A")

    at = AppTest.from_function(_test_app, args=paths)

    for _ in range(2):
        at.run()
        assert not at.exception
        assert at.text[0].value == "0A"
        assert at.text[1].value == "1A"
        assert mock_read_text.call_count == 2

    paths[0].write_text("0B")

    for _ in range(2):
        at.run()
        assert not at.exception
        assert at.text[0].value == "0B"
        assert at.text[1].value == "1A"
        assert mock_read_text.call_count == 3

    paths[0].touch()

    for _ in range(2):
        at.run()
        assert not at.exception
        assert at.text[0].value == "0B"
        assert at.text[1].value == "1A"
        assert mock_read_text.call_count == 4

    paths[1].write_text("1B")

    for _ in range(2):
        at.run()
        assert not at.exception
        assert at.text[0].value == "0B"
        assert at.text[1].value == "1B"
        assert mock_read_text.call_count == 5
```
