title: Send dataframe (Arrow) data via HTTP instead of the WebSocket
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Send dataframe (Arrow) data over HTTP rather than through the WebSocket, similar to how we already serve images, video, and audio. HTTP appears to be faster than the WebSocket *and* gets parallelized by the browser, which should speed up BI-style apps with many charts/tables containing thousands of datapoints each.

### Why?

- Browsers make HTTP requests in parallel, so the rest of the app can keep loading *while* the dataframe data downloads (instead of serializing everything through a single WebSocket).
- Anecdotally, the WebSocket seems a bit slower than plain HTTP requests for large payloads.
- If it works well for dataframes, it could be extended to charts (which carry large datasets too).

### How?

An MVP could extend the existing **forward message cache** mechanism to support a *reference message* that carries a URL instead of a hash. If the URL is set, the frontend downloads the message body over HTTP. This would let us put the Arrow data in media file storage and send only a lightweight reference over the WebSocket.

Considerations:
- Likely only beneficial above a certain size threshold, since there's overhead to uploading to storage, exchanging metadata, and cleaning up.
- `st.dataframe` lazy data loading could keep the initial payload small and might pair well with this (e.g. auto-enable for large dataframes).
- **SiS caveat:** new HTTP endpoints have historically been very painful there (file uploader, custom components, download button, forward message cache, static file serving). Prefer reusing existing media-file-storage plumbing rather than introducing a new endpoint, and validate end-to-end upload efficiency in that environment.

### Additional Context

- Could later be extended to charts / other elements that transfer large datasets.
- Related mechanisms: media file storage (used for images/video/audio) and the forward message cache.

title: @st.cache_data crashes with NameError on Python 3.14 when annotations use TYPE_CHECKING imports (PEP 649)
body:
## Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

## Summary

On Python 3.14, `@st.cache_data` (and likely `@st.cache_resource`) crashes with a `NameError` when a decorated function uses type annotations that reference types imported under `if TYPE_CHECKING:`. This is caused by Python 3.14's PEP 649 (deferred evaluation of annotations), which changes how `inspect.signature()` resolves annotations. Streamlit's caching internals call `inspect.signature()` to determine parameter names, and on Python 3.14 this now triggers lazy annotation evaluation, which fails when the referenced types are not available at runtime.

## Reproducible Code Example

```python
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

import streamlit as st

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from collections.abc import Sequence

@st.cache_data
def my_func(items: "Sequence[str]" = None) -> None:
    return None

# Calling the function triggers the crash
my_func(["a", "b"])
```

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Install Python 3.14.x (e.g., 3.14.2)
2. Install Streamlit (`pip install streamlit`)
3. Create a file with the code above
4. Run `streamlit run app.py`
5. Observe the crash

## Expected Behavior

`@st.cache_data` should work correctly with functions whose annotations reference types imported under `if TYPE_CHECKING:`, just as it does on Python <= 3.13. The decorator only needs parameter *names* (not types) for cache key computation, so annotation resolution should not be required.

## Current Behavior

The app crashes immediately with:

```
NameError: ("name 'Sequence' is not defined", '')
```

Full traceback (abbreviated):

```
File ".../streamlit/runtime/caching/cache_utils.py", line 440, in _make_value_key
    arg_name = _get_positional_arg_name(func, arg_idx)
File ".../streamlit/runtime/caching/cache_utils.py", line 535, in _get_positional_arg_name
    params: list[inspect.Parameter] = list(inspect.signature(func).parameters.values())
File ".../lib/python3.14/inspect.py", line 3321, in signature
    return Signature.from_callable(obj, follow_wrapped=follow_wrapped, ...)
...
File ".../lib/python3.14/annotationlib.py", line 1137, in _get_dunder_annotations
    ann = getattr(obj, "__annotations__", None)
NameError: ("name 'Sequence' is not defined", '')
```

### Root cause

In `cache_utils.py`, the function `_get_positional_arg_name` calls `inspect.signature(func)`. On Python <= 3.13, this did not eagerly evaluate annotations. On Python 3.14 (PEP 649), annotations are evaluated lazily via `__annotate__`, and `inspect.signature()` now triggers that evaluation — causing a `NameError` for any type that is only imported under `TYPE_CHECKING`.

### Suggested fix

Since `_get_positional_arg_name` only accesses `.name` and `.kind` on the parameters (never `.annotation`), the fix could be to call `inspect.signature(func, eval_str=False)` or to use `inspect.get_annotations(func, format=inspect.Format.FORWARDREF)` (Python 3.14+) to avoid triggering annotation evaluation. Alternatively, wrapping the `inspect.signature()` call to catch `NameError` and falling back to a non-evaluating approach would also work.

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

## Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.52.2 (likely affects all versions including 1.55.0)
- Python version: 3.14.2
- Operating System: Windows 11
- Browser: N/A (crashes before rendering)

## Additional Information

- PEP 649: https://peps.python.org/pep-0649/
- The `if TYPE_CHECKING:` pattern is the standard Python practice (recommended by ruff's TC rules) for avoiding circular imports and keeping runtime import overhead minimal. It is widely used across the Python ecosystem.
- Streamlit's own codebase uses `from __future__ import annotations` in `cache_utils.py` and `hashing.py`, which currently shields its internal code from this issue — but user code that follows the `TYPE_CHECKING` pattern (without `from __future__ import annotations`) is affected.
- **Workaround**: Move the affected imports out of the `TYPE_CHECKING` block so they are available at runtime. This requires adding `noqa` comments for ruff's TC rules.

body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Return `None` when accessing an uninitialized `st.session_state` value instead of raising an exception. This would remove common initialization boilerplate and make nested event data easier to consume.

### Why?

Today, initialization requires:

```python
if "foo" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.foo = 123
```

With a `None` default, this could become:

```python
if not st.session_state.foo:
    st.session_state.foo = 123
```

It could also simplify truly empty selection results for charts and dataframes while still allowing checks such as `if event_data.selection.points`.

### How?

Have missing session-state attributes resolve to `None`. The existing `AttributeDict` may already be close to this behavior; [`addict`](https://github.com/mewwts/addict) could also be useful as an implementation reference or dependency.

### Additional Context

This could be breaking for code that intentionally relies on missing values raising an exception, so compatibility and migration behavior would need careful consideration.

title: Add a button group widget with trigger (click) mode
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Provide a button group that supports **trigger (click) mode** instead of selection mode — i.e. a horizontal group of buttons that returns the clicked value once (like `st.button`) and clears after the rerun, rather than persisting a selection. This can either be a new `st.button_group` command or an extension of the existing `st.pills` / `st.segmented_control`.

### Why?

It's currently a bit complicated to build things like quick selections / quick replies for chat UIs (a major need for LLM-powered apps), button toolbars, dialog action rows (Confirm / Cancel / Clear), or clickable example grids. Today you have to combine many individual `st.button`s across `st.columns`, which is a lot of boilerplate and looks messy because wrapping depends on each button's label length.

### How?

Two main options:

**Option 1 — Extend `st.pills` / `st.segmented_control` with a trigger mode:**

```python
st.pills(..., selection_mode="single" | "multi" | "trigger")
```

In `trigger` mode the widget doesn't keep state: it returns the clicked value and clears it after the rerun (like a button), returning `None` otherwise. `default` wouldn't be allowed in this mode.

**Option 2 — Add a dedicated `st.button_group` command (preferred):**

```python
st.button_group(
    options,
    *,
    format_func=None,
    key=None,
    on_click=None,
    args=None,
    kwargs=None,
    disabled=False,
    type="default" | "rounded",
    wrap=True,
)
```

Behaves like `st.pills` but tailored for triggers: no top label/help (not needed for quick selections), `on_click` instead of `on_change` (aligns with `st.button`), a `type` option for a rounded pill-like look, and a `wrap` option. Keeping triggers in a separate command avoids overloading the selection API (e.g. `selection_mode="trigger"` reads oddly, `default` becomes incompatible, and typing gets awkward).

### Additional Context

- Related: #8318 (quick replies/suggestions for chat responses) — one of the primary motivating use cases.
- Other use cases: button toolbars, dialog action rows, and clickable example grids.

body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

I am noticing behaviour very similar to the behaviour described in [this issue](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9036#issuecomment-2594452089) when using v1.41.1. In particular, I'm noticing that if I cause a rerun by pressing "R" and there is a cache miss, then sometimes the page reloads, element status is lost (e.g. active element, but not state like selected items) and scroll position is lost (the page is scrolled to the very top).

I first noticed this on a large page with many elements and several cached_data references. I was able to narrow it down to a single simple page show in the reproducible code.

The problem seems to come up when there are multiple cached_data functions that all expire together and all need to be run again as part of the same app rerun.

The attached video shows the reload happening consistently on the cache miss, i.e. every 3 seconds. I've found that if I reduce the number of cached_data functions, then this is less likely to happen.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
def get_table(table_name: str) -> list:
```

title: Server-side validation of client-side widget constraints
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Widget constraints like `options` allow-lists, `disabled`, `num_rows`, `max_chars`, and DataFrame column `validate` are enforced only in the browser, so a forged `WidgetState`/`BackMsg` can submit out-of-constraint values that flow into `st.session_state`, callbacks, and return values. We could add a way to have Streamlit re-check these constraints server-side.


### Why?

Many developers reasonably assume `st.selectbox(options=[...])` can only return one of its options, or that `disabled=True` blocks a value/callback — but that only holds client-side. Relying on it today means hand-rolling server-side validation for every widget, which is easy to forget.

### How?

Enforce declared widget constraints server-side by default in the widget deserialize path — validating the incoming value against `options` allow-lists, `min_value`/`max_value`, `max_chars`, `disabled=True`, and `st.data_editor` `disabled`/`num_rows`/column `validate`. On a violation, coerce to a valid value (reset to default / clamp), consistent with how Streamlit already handles stale `options` today, so normal frontend/backend sync races don't break.

title: Implement browser session API
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Browser sessions allow developers to track browser status in streamlit, so that they can implement features like authentication, persistent draft or shopping cart, which require the ability to keep user state after refreshing or reopen browsers.

### Why?

The current streamlit session will lost state if users refresh or reopen their browser. And the effort of providing a API to write cookies has been pending for years. I think provide a dedicated API to track browser session would be cleaner and easier to implement.  
With this API developers don't need to know how it works, it can be based on cookie or local storage or anything else. And developers can use it with singleton pattern to keep state for browser to persist whatever they want in streamlit.

### How?

This feature will introduce several new APIs:
* `st.get_browser_session(gdpr_consent=False)`, which will set a unique session id in browser if it doesn't exist, and return it.
If `gdpr_consent` is set to True, a window will pop up to ask for user's consent before setting the session id.
* `st.clean_browser_session()`, which will remove the session id from browser.

The below is a POC of how `get_browser_session` can be used to implement a simple authentication solution:

```python
from streamlit.web.server.websocket_headers import _get_websocket_headers
from streamlit.components.v1 import html
import streamlit as st

from http.cookies import SimpleCookie
from uuid import uuid4
from time import sleep

def get_cookie():
    try:
        headers = st.context.headers
    except AttributeError:
        headers = _get_websocket_headers()
    if headers is not None:
        cookie_str = headers.get("Cookie")
        if cookie_str:
            return SimpleCookie(cookie_str)


def get_cookie_value(key):
    cookie = get_cookie()
    if cookie is not None:
        cookie_value = cookie.get(key)
        if cookie_value is not None:
            return cookie_value.value
    return None


def get_browser_session():
    """
    use cookie to track browser session
    this id is unique to each browser session
    it won't change even if the page is refreshed or reopened
    """
    if 'st_session_id' not in st.session_state:
        session_id = get_cookie_value('ST_SESSION_ID')
        if session_id is None:
            session_id = uuid4().hex
            st.session_state['st_session_id'] = session_id
            html(f'<script>document.cookie = "ST_SESSION_ID={session_id}";</script>')
            sleep(0.1)  # FIXME: work around bug: Tried to use SessionInfo before it was initialized
            st.rerun()  # FIXME: rerun immediately so that html won't be shown in the final page
        st.session_state['st_session_id'] = session_id
    return st.session_state['st_session_id']


@st.cache_resource
def get_auth_state():
    """
    A singleton to store authentication state
    """
    return {}


st.set_page_config(page_title='Browser Session Demo')
session_id = get_browser_session()

auth_state = get_auth_state()
if session_id not in auth_state:
    auth_state[session_id] = False

st.write(f'Your browser session ID: {session_id}')

if not auth_state[session_id]:
    st.title('Input Password')
    token = st.text_input('Token', type='password')
    if st.button('Submit'):
        if token == 'passw0rd!':
            auth_state[session_id] = True
            st.rerun()
        else:
            st.error('Invalid token')
else:
    st.success('Authentication success')
    if st.button('Logout'):
        auth_state[session_id] = False
        st.rerun()
    st.write('You are free to refresh or reopen this page without re-authentication')
```

A more complicated example of using this method to work with oauth2 can be tried here: https://ai4ec.ikkem.com/apps/op-elyte-emulator/ 

### Additional Context

Related issues:
* https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/861
* https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8518

title: st.table() / st.dataframe() / st.data_editor() causes fatal SIGSEGV (exit code 139) in PyArrow convert_column - process killed silently, no Python exception raised
body:
### Summary

Calling st.table(), st.dataframe(), or st.data_editor() with a pandas DataFrame causes a fatal segmentation fault (SIGSEGV, exit code 139) that kills the entire Streamlit process. The crash originates inside PyArrow's convert_column C extension, called during Streamlit's internal DataFrame-to-Arrow serialization. No Python exception is raised. The process dies silently with no user-visible error. In containerized environments (Kubernetes/OpenShift) this triggers a pod restart.


### Steps To Reproduce

We were unable to produce a minimal example that reliably crashes in all environments. The crash is non-deterministic and appears to depend on the process memory state at the time of rendering. It reproduces consistently in our containerized Linux environment (OpenShift, Python 3.11) but not on a local Windows developer machine.

The code that triggers it in the enviroments:

```
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

# This DataFrame is rendered on every page rerun
df = pd.DataFrame({"Group": st.session_state.get("usergroup", [])})
st.table(df)  
```

or

```
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

# DataFrame built from backend JSON response
rows = [{"col_a": "value", "col_b": None}, {"col_a": "other", "col_b": 3}]
df = pd.DataFrame(rows)  # object-dtype columns with None values
st.dataframe(df)  #
```


Steps To Reproduce

1. Deploy a Streamlit 1.55.0 app to a Linux container (e.g. OpenShift/Kubernetes)
2. Navigate to a page that renders st.table() or st.dataframe() with a DataFrame that has object-dtype columns (e.g. built from pd.DataFrame(list_of_dicts) where some cells are None)
3. Trigger a Streamlit script rerun via a button click that loads new data into session state before the render
4. Observed: process dies with exit code 139, container restarts
5. Repeat the exact same steps - it works on the second attempt

### Expected Behavior

The DataFrame renders normally. If an internal serialization error occurs, Streamlit catches it and displays an error in the UI without killing the process.

### Current Behavior

The Python process is killed with SIGSEGV (exit code 139). Nothing appears in logs unless faulthandler is explicitly enabled at startup. With import faulthandler; faulthandler.enable() added, the crash trace is:

```
Fatal Python error: Segmentation fault

Current thread (most recent call first):
  File ".../pyarrow/pandas_compat.py", line 638 in convert_column
  File ".../pyarrow/pandas_compat.py", line 656 in dataframe_to_arrays
  File ".../streamlit/dataframe_util.py", line 839 in convert_pandas_df_to_arrow_bytes
  File ".../streamlit/dataframe_util.py", line 919 in convert_anything_to_arrow_bytes
  File ".../streamlit/elements/table.py", line 78 in marshall_table
  File ".../streamlit/elements/table.py", line 234 in table
```

The crash is non-deterministic: it only occurs on some reruns, always the first one after the pod/process starts, and does not occur on subsequent reruns with identical data and code. We have no confirmed explanation for the non-determinism beyond it appearing to depend on process memory state.

**Workaround**: converting object-dtype columns to pd.StringDtype() before rendering prevents the crash:

- For st.table(): replace with st.write() / st.markdown() to avoid PyArrow entirely

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- **Streamlit version:** 1.55.0
- **Python version:** 3.11
- **OS:** Linux (OpenShift container, py311ora base image)
- **PyArrow version:** (bundled with Streamlit 1.55.0)
- **pandas version:** (default installed with Streamlit 1.55.0)
- **Browser**: Microsoft Edge

### Additional Information

- The crash is in PyArrow's C extension code, not in Streamlit's Python layer - Streamlit could potentially guard against it by catching signals or pre-validating column types before passing to PyArrow
- After the SIGSEGV the container restarts automatically (Kubernetes/OpenShift restart policy). On the very next attempt, with the process freshly started and identical code, data, and user actions, the crash does not occur and the app works normally. This "works after restart" behavior is what made the bug difficult to diagnose initially, as it appeared to be a transient infrastructure issue rather than a code defect.

```python
choice = st.command_menu(

)
if choice == "Export data":
    ...
```

title: SnowflakeConnection.query() cache key ignores params argument
body:
## Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

## Summary

`SnowflakeConnection.query()` (and likely `SQLConnection.query()`) does not include the `params` argument when generating the cache key. This causes incorrect cached results when the same query string is called with different parameter values.

## Steps to reproduce

```python
import streamlit as st

conn = st.connection("mydb", "snowflake")
query = "SELECT * FROM my_table WHERE status = ?"

# First call - returns correct data for status 'active'
result1 = conn.query(query, params=["active"])

# Second call - SHOULD return data for status 'inactive'
# ACTUALLY returns cached data for status 'active'
result2 = conn.query(query, params=["inactive"])

# Workaround: disable caching, but loses the benefit of caching
result3 = conn.query(query, params=["inactive"], ttl=0)
```

## Expected behavior

The cache key should include both the query string AND the params argument. Different parameter values should result in separate cache entries.

## Actual behavior

The cache key only includes the query string. The `params` argument is ignored, so `conn.query(q, params=["a"])` and `conn.query(q, params=["b"])` return the same cached result.

## Workaround

Wrap the query in a custom cached function that includes params in the signature:

```python
@st.cache_data(ttl=600)
def query_with_params(query: str, params: tuple):
    conn = st.connection("mydb", "snowflake")
    return conn.query(query, params=list(params), ttl=0)

# Usage - params as tuple for hashability
query_with_params(query, ("active",))
query_with_params(query, ("inactive",))  # Now correctly cached separately
```

## Is this a regression?

Unknown - this may have been the behavior since `st.connection` was introduced.

## Debug info

- Streamlit version: (current)
- Python version: 3.11+
- OS: macOS / Linux

## Additional context

This also likely affects `SQLConnection.query()` and potentially other connection types that support parameterized queries with internal caching.

Using parameterized queries is a security best practice to prevent SQL injection, so it's important that the caching mechanism supports this pattern correctly.

### Summary

When the options given to selectbox are instances of arbitrary classes **and** a format function is used, the selected option always revert to the first option if another option is selected.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import NamedTuple

import streamlit as st


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class MyDataClass:
    id: int
    name: str


class MyNamedTuple(NamedTuple):
    id: int
    name: str


class MyPlainClass:
    def __init__(self, id_: int, name: str) -> None:
        self.id = id_
        self.name = name

TypeToTest = MyDataClass
a = TypeToTest(1, "one")
b = TypeToTest(2, "two")
x = {a: "I", b: "II"}


def format_function(s: MyDataClass | MyNamedTuple | MyPlainClass) -> str:
    print(x[s])
    return s.name


s = st.selectbox("selectbox", [a, b], format_func=format_function)
st.write(s.name)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Run the code above and try to select the second option.

### Expected Behavior

The second option is selected.

### Current Behavior

selectbox always reverts the selection to the first option.

title: `st.status` created on a container outside a fragment corrupts the element tree and crashes the app with "Cannot set a node at a delta path"
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When a fragment calls `.status()` on a container that was declared outside the fragment, and then opens that status block a second time with a separate `with` statement, the app crashes to a blank page with `Uncaught Error: Cannot set a node at a delta path`. The status container re-emits its own block at the wrong delta path, which destroys an intermediate container in the frontend element tree, so the next element written inside it has no parent. This is a regression: it works in 1.58.0 and fails in every version from 1.59.0 onward.

### Reproducible Code Example

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-16281)

```Python
import streamlit as st


@st.fragment
def frag(outside):
    block = outside.status("query")
    with block:
        st.code("first")
    with block:  # second, separate `with` on the same status block
        st.text("second")


st.title("Repro")
frag(st.container())
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Save the example above and run it with `streamlit run app.py`.
2. Open the app in a browser and open the developer console.
3. No interaction is needed. The crash happens during the initial page load.

### Expected Behavior

The app renders the title and a `query` status container holding both writes. Opening a status block twice with two separate `with` statements should behave the same whether the status was created on a container inside or outside the fragment.

### Current Behavior

The app area goes blank and the "running" indicator returns to a rerun control. The console logs this error, thrown at `frontend/lib/src/render-tree/visitors/SetNodeByDeltaPathVisitor.ts:125` (bundle paths shortened to `index.js`):

```
Uncaught Error: Cannot set a node at a delta path
    at e.visitBlockNode (index.js:14:6488)
    at bu.accept (index.js:14:2717)
    at e.visitBlockNode (index.js:14:6366)
    at bu.accept (index.js:14:2717)
    at e.visitBlockNode (index.js:14:6366)
    at bu.accept (index.js:14:2717)
    at e.visitBlockNode (index.js:14:6366)
    at bu.accept (index.js:14:2717)
    at e.setNodeAtPath (index.js:14:6730)
    at e.addElement (index.js:14:9426)
```

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.60.0
- Python version: 3.11.13
- Operating System: Linux
- Browser: Chromium

### Additional Information

#### Affected versions

Same repro, one browser check per version, each version serving its own frontend:

| Streamlit version | Crashes on initial load |
| --- | --- |
| 1.58.0 | no |
| 1.59.0 | yes |
| 1.59.1 | yes |
| 1.59.2 | yes |
| 1.60.0 | yes |
| `1.60.1.dev20260729` (nightly) | yes |

The regression enters in 1.59.0. No released version fixes it, and the nightly above still fails.

#### The delta stream

These are the deltas the backend emits for the example above on the first script run. The defect is the sixth delta:

```
[0, 1]           block=flex_container   fragment=-      <- the outside container
[0, 2]           block=flex_container   fragment=X      <- the fragment's own container
[0, 1, 0]        block=transparent      fragment=X      <- outside-write wrapper
[0, 1, 0, 0]     block=expandable       fragment=X      <- the status, inside the wrapper
[0, 1, 0, 0, 0]  element=code           fragment=X      <- first `with` write
[0, 1, 0]        block=expandable       fragment=X      <- BUG: re-emitted at the wrapper's path
[0, 1, 0, 0, 1]  element=text           fragment=X      <- crashes here
```

The sixth delta replaces the `transparent` wrapper at `[0, 1, 0]` with an `expandable` block. `AppRoot.addBlock` only inherits the existing children when the block type matches (`frontend/lib/src/render-tree/AppRoot.ts:469`), and `transparent` is not `expandable`, so the frontend drops the whole subtree. The next delta targets `[0, 1, 0, 0, 1]`, its parent at `[0, 1, 0, 0]` no longer exists, and the visitor throws.

#### Root cause

`StatusContainer._create` captures the delta path for later re-emits from the **parent's** cursor **before** the block is created (`lib/streamlit/elements/lib/mutable_status_container.py:81-91`):

```python
delta_path: list[int] = (
    parent._active_dg._cursor.delta_path if parent._active_dg._cursor else []
)

status_container = cast(
    "StatusContainer",
    parent._block(block_proto=block_proto, dg_type=StatusContainer),
)

# Apply initial configuration
status_container._delta_path = delta_path
```

Normally the parent cursor points at exactly the index where the new block lands, so the captured path identifies the status block correctly.

Since 1.59.0, a write from a fragment into a container declared outside that fragment is redirected into a per-fragment layout-transparent wrapper block. The status block therefore lands one level deeper than the captured path predicted, so `_delta_path` points at the wrapper instead of the status.

`update()` does not use the cursor. It builds a message and sets that stale path directly (`mutable_status_container.py:151`):

```python
msg.metadata.delta_path[:] = self._delta_path
msg.delta.add_block.CopyFrom(self._current_proto)
```

`__exit__` calls `update(state="complete")` whenever the state is still `running` (`mutable_status_container.py:185-204`), so an explicit `update()` call is not required to trigger this.

#### Scope of the trigger

Each row was checked in a browser against 1.59.1:

| Variant | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Same code without the fragment | works |
| Fragment, status, one `with` block | works |
| Fragment, status, one `with` block plus a later `update()` | works |
| Fragment, status, **two separate `with` blocks** | **crash** |
| Outside container is `st.container`, `st.popover`, or `st.expander` | crash in all three |
| Inner block is `outside.container()` instead of `outside.status()` | works |

`st.status` is the element that matters, because it is the one that re-emits its own block from a stored path. The type of the outside container does not matter.

The one-`with` case still emits the misdirected delta and still replaces the wrapper, but nothing is written inside the block afterwards, so no delta is left without a parent and no crash is visible. The element tree is already wrong in that case, which means this defect can also corrupt a page silently.

#### Related work

The 1.59.0 change that introduces the redirection is the outside-container-writes work: #15541, #15545, #15598, #15620, and #15623.

This looks close to #12514 (fragments inside a shared container), but it is a different defect. #16171 is the fix for #12514 and it is present in the nightly listed above, which still reproduces this crash.

#### Possible fix

Capture `_delta_path` after the block is created, from the path `_block()` actually wrote to, rather than predicting it from the parent cursor beforehand. It may be worth auditing any other element that stores a delta path and later enqueues a message with it directly.

#### Workarounds

Both verified on 1.59.1:

- Write everything to the status inside a single `with` block.
- Create the status on a container declared inside the fragment, or use `st.expander` or `st.container` instead of `st.status`.

title: Disable chat_input submit button if uploaded files exceed size limit or uploads fail or file format mismatch
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

When st.chat_input (and st.file_uploader) accept files, a file that exceeds max_upload_size or otherwise fails to upload is flagged with an error chip in the UI, but the submit button stays enabled — so the user can still send the message with a failed or missing attachment. Please provide a way to automatically disable the submit button while any attached file is over the limit, errored, or still uploading, so an incomplete/invalid set of files can't be submitted. Ideally also expose the per-file upload status so developers can gate submission themselves.

### Why?

There's currently no way to stop a chat submission when an upload fails. max_upload_size (from #12692) rejects oversized files before upload, which is great, but the rejected file is then silently dropped — it never appears in the returned ChatInputValue.files / st.file_uploader value, and st.chat_input returns None until submit, so no upload status is available to Python before the user hits send. As a result the app can't detect the failure or set disabled= off it.

The practical impact:
- The user attaches 3 files, 1 is over the limit → only 2 upload, the failed one is invisible to the app, and the user can still submits mistakenly believing all 3 went. The app then runs on a partial/incorrect set — wrong results, wasted compute/tokens (very common in LLM apps), and confusion.
- Submitting while a file is still uploading can send an incomplete set.
- submit_mode only governs behavior after submit (disable/stop during the run), so it doesn't help gate submission on upload state.

### How?

Two complementary options:

1. A built-in guard — a parameter that auto-disables the submit button until every attached file has uploaded successfully. For example:

st.chat_input(
       "Type a message…",
       accept_file="multiple",
       max_upload_size=1,
       block_submit_on_upload_error=True,  # submit stays disabled while any file errors/uploads
   )

2. Expose the upload status so developers can implement their own logic — e.g. a list of {name, size, status} (uploading / success / error) available on rerun before submit, so we can do disabled=any(f.status != "success" for f in files).

Desired behavior (matching the natural mental model): submit is enabled only when all attached files have status success. If the user deletes an errored file, it drops out of the status list, and since the remaining files are already success, submit re-enables. In short: track upload status per file before submit, and let it drive the submit button.

### Additional Context

title: [Request for feedback] Starlette/ASGI Support in Streamlit
body:
Starting with **Streamlit 1.53**, we're introducing experimental support for running Streamlit with [Starlette](https://www.starlette.io/) as the underlying web framework. This is the first step toward our long-term goal of **fully migrating from Tornado to Starlette/ASGI**, and we need your help to identify any issues or gaps before the full transition. ## What's New > **Note:** To use the experimental Starlette features, you need to install the optional dependencies: > > ```bash > pip install streamlit[starlette] > ``` ### 1. Starlette Server Mode (Experimental) You can now run Streamlit using Starlette instead of Tornado by setting a config option: ```toml # .streamlit/config.toml [server] useStarlette = true ``` Or via command line: ```bash streamlit run app.py --server.useStarlette=true ``` ### 2. ASGI App Entry Point (Experimental) For advanced use cases, you can now create an ASGI-compatible Streamlit application using the new `App` class: ```python from streamlit.starlette import App app = App("main.py") ``` Run it with `streamlit run` (preferred): ```bash streamlit run myapp.py ``` Streamlit will automatically detect the `App` instance and run it in Starlette mode. Alternatively, you can use any ASGI server directly: ```bash uvicorn myapp:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8501 ``` The `App` class supports advanced configuration including: - **Custom HTTP routes** — Add REST API endpoints alongside your Streamlit app - **Middleware** — Add security headers, authentication, logging, etc. - **Lifespan hooks** — Run code on startup/shutdown (e.g., pre-warm caches, initialize resources) - **Framework integration** — Mount Streamlit inside FastAPI, Django, or other ASGI frameworks > 📖 For more details on the `App` interface and its full capabilities, see the [specification in PR #13449](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/13449).
Example: Adding custom routes ```python from streamlit.starlette import App from starlette.routing import Route from starlette.responses import JSONResponse async def health_check(request): return JSONResponse({"status": "healthy", "service": "streamlit-app"}) async def get_data(request): return JSONResponse({"items": ["apple", "banana", "cherry"], "count": 3}) app = App( "main.py", routes=[ Route("/api/health", health_check), Route("/api/data", get_data), ], ) ```
Example: Adding custom middleware ```python from streamlit.starlette import App from starlette.middleware import Middleware from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware class SecurityHeadersMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware): async def dispatch(self, request, call_next): response = await call_next(request) response.headers["X-Content-Type-Options"] = "nosniff" response.headers["X-Frame-Options"] = "SAMEORIGIN" return response app = App( "main.py", middleware=[Middleware(SecurityHeadersMiddleware)], ) ```
Example: Mounting FastAPI in Streamlit ```python from fastapi import FastAPI from starlette.routing import Mount from streamlit.starlette import App # Create FastAPI sub-application api = FastAPI() @api.get("/health") async def health(): return {"status": "healthy"} @api.post("/predict") async def predict(data: dict): return {"prediction": data.get("value", 0) * 2} # Mount FastAPI into Streamlit app # - Streamlit UI at / # - FastAPI endpoints at /api/* # - FastAPI docs at /api/docs app = App( "dashboard.py", routes=[Mount("/api", app=api)], ) ```
Example: Mounting Streamlit in FastAPI ```python from fastapi import FastAPI from streamlit.starlette import App # Create the Streamlit sub-application streamlit_app = App("dashboard.py") # Create FastAPI with Streamlit's lifespan to manage the runtime lifecycle api = FastAPI(lifespan=streamlit_app.lifespan()) @api.get("/api/data") async def get_data(): return {"data": [1, 2, 3]} # Mount Streamlit under /dashboard api.mount("/dashboard", streamlit_app) # Run with: uvicorn myapp:api ```
Example: Lifespan hooks for startup/shutdown ```python from contextlib import asynccontextmanager from streamlit.starlette import App @asynccontextmanager async def lifespan(app): # Startup: runs before accepting connections print("🚀 Starting up...") model = load_ml_model() # Pre-warm caches db = init_db_connection() # Yield state accessible via app.state yield {"model": model, "db": db} # Shutdown: cleanup resources print("👋 Shutting down...") db.close() app = App("main.py", lifespan=lifespan) ```

title: Multiple custom Streamlit components fail to load in deployed environments

### Summary

Several custom Streamlit components, including `streamlit_shadcn_ui`, `st_bridge`, `st_aggrid`, `streamlit_image_select`, and `st-theme`, fail to load in deployed environments (except Streamlit Community Cloud), though they work correctly in local development. The issue seems related to network latency or proxy settings affecting frontend asset access in the deployment environment.

Examples were people -including me- have such problems:

* https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/button-in-your-app-is-having-trouble-loading-the-streamlit-shadcn-ui/75962
* https://discuss.huggingface.co/t/need-help-with-streamlit-bridge-on-hf-space/105889
* https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/trouble-loading-the-st-aggrid-aggrid-component/75480
* https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/streamlit-image-select-image-select-component-issue/74615
* and lastly it happens to my deployment in Google Cloud Run with st-theme component

### Reproducible Code Example

I haven't been able to reproduce the issue locally; it only occurs when I deploy it to Google Cloud Run. Could this be due to the serverless nature of the platform, where multiple container instances are spun up to serve the streamlit app? I've read that using **session affinity** (https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/session-affinity) in Google Cloud Run deployments is recommended to ensure requests are routed to the same instance, especially since Streamlit relies on WebSockets. Could this be causing the problem? Does Streamlit really needs such a feature to work correct?

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Deploy the app on a cloud platform (e.g., Google Cloud Run).
2. Include any of the mentioned custom components (streamlit_shadcn_ui, st_bridge, st_aggrid, etc.).
3. Run the app and observe the error when trying to load the components.
4. See the error message indicating trouble loading the frontend assets for the components.

### Expected Behavior

The app should load the custom components without any issues, just as it works in local development. The frontend assets should be accessible in the deployment environment.

### Current Behavior

When deploying the app, the custom components fail to load. The error message indicates that the app is having trouble accessing the component frontend assets, which may be due to network latency or proxy issues. The components work fine locally but fail when deployed.

Your app is having trouble loading the `[component_name]` component.

If this is an installed component that works locally, the app may be having trouble accessing the component frontend assets due to network latency or proxy settings in your app deployment.

title: Allow hashing of plain Python classes by handling standard library functions
body:
# Feature Request: Allow hashing of plain Python classes by handling standard library functions

## Summary

Streamlit's caching mechanism currently rejects plain Python classes because it cannot hash the `copyreg._reconstructor` function that appears in their default `__reduce__()` output. This can be fixed by adding support for hashing standard library functions by their fully qualified names, allowing common Python classes to work with `st.cache_resource` and `st.cache_data` without requiring the verbose `hash_funcs` workaround.

## Why?

**Current Problem:**

When users try to cache functions with plain Python class instances as arguments, they get a confusing error:

```python
import streamlit as st

class Data:
    def __init__(self, payload: bytes):
        self.payload = payload

@st.cache_resource
def transform(data: Data) -> Data:
    return Data(payload=b'new')

data = Data(payload=b'old')
transform(data)  # ❌ UnhashableParamError: Cannot hash argument 'data'
```

**Error:** `TypeError: cannot pickle 'function' object` → `UnhashableParamError`

This is confusing because:

- The `Data` class IS pickle-serializable (`pickle.dumps(data)` works fine)
- The documentation says "arguments must be hashable" but plain classes fail
- Users must add `hash_funcs` to every decorator, which is verbose

**Root Cause:**

Streamlit uses `__reduce__()` (from the pickle protocol) to generate cache keys. Python's default `__reduce__()` for plain classes returns `copyreg._reconstructor` as the first element. Streamlit can hash builtins but not regular standard library functions, so it tries to call `__reduce__()` on the function itself, which fails.

**Impact:**

This affects all plain Python classes without custom `__reduce__()` methods - a very common use case. Users must use the `hash_funcs` workaround for every cached function:

```python
@st.cache_resource(hash_funcs={Data: lambda d: d.payload})
def transform(data: Data):
    return Data(payload=b'new')
```

## How?

Add handling for standard library functions in `lib/streamlit/runtime/caching/hashing.py`.

## Additional Context

**Related Issues:**

- **#13480** - Original bug report (this enhancement solves it)
- **#10348** - Feature request for custom `__streamlit_hash__()` (complementary - handles advanced cases)
- **#7966** - Broader request to improve custom class hashing
- **#6703** - Request for non-serializable objects (different problem)
- **#1399** (docs repo) - Documentation clarity improvement

---

**Note:** This enhancement provides automatic support for the common case (plain classes). Issue #10348 proposes adding `__streamlit_hash__()` for advanced customization. Together, these would provide both automatic support (this enhancement) and user control (#10348).

title: Add `allowed_dates` parameter to st.date_input to restrict selectable dates to a specific list
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Currently, st.date_input only supports continuous date ranges via min_value and max_value. 
There is no way to restrict selectable dates to a specific list of valid dates, such as 
dates available in a dataframe. Adding an allowed_dates parameter would fill this gap.

### Why?

I'm always frustrated when I need to show a date picker that only allows the user to select 
dates that exist in a dataset. For example, when a dataframe contains sales data only for 
specific dates, the current widget allows the user to select any date in the range, even 
dates with no data. This forces developers to use workarounds like st.selectbox, which 
lacks the calendar UI and date-picking experience that st.date_input provides.

### How?

Introduce a new parameter called `allowed_dates` in `st.date_input` with the following behavior:

- Accepts a list of datetime.date objects
- Disables all dates not present in the list in the calendar UI
- Example usage:

import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"date": ["2025-01-01", "2025-01-15", "2025-02-10"]})
df["date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["date"]).dt.date

selected = st.date_input(
    "Select a date",
    allowed_dates=df["date"].tolist()
)

### Additional Context

This feature request was inspired by a common use case discussed while using st.date_input  with dataframes. The current workaround is to use st.selectbox with the list of available dates, but this sacrifices the calendar UI   experience.

Related issue: st.date_input currently supports min_value and max_value for continuous 
ranges, but has no support for non-continuous date lists.

### Summary

Similar to the issues linked, if the network connection is intermittent/flaky the existing session is lost and a new one created, causing unpleasant/unexpected user experience.

See:

https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/1386
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/1628
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6442

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
import time

if "counter" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.counter = 0

st.write(f"Run count = {st.session_state.counter}")

st.session_state.counter += 1

time.sleep(3)

st.rerun()
```


### Steps To Reproduce

title: WebSocket header HTTP_SEC_WEBSOCKET_PROTOCOL value changed to 'streamlit, PLACEHOLDER_AUTH_TOKEN' which gives connection error
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

After this change https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/commit/fd1037ba61 in the file https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blame/1.29.0/frontend/app/src/connection/WebsocketConnection.tsx#L435 the request header `Sec-Websocket-Protocol` from the webpage client has no longer the value `'streamlit'` but from Streamlit version **1.29.0** the value is `'streamlit, PLACEHOLDER_AUTH_TOKEN'`.

I use a Streamlit app where the server side of the app is in a docker and the communication between the webpage client and the server goes through a proxy based on Flask and uwsgi.

That changed header prevented the webpage client from connecting to the server ( URL `/_stcore/stream failed`).

My fix was to replace the value `'streamlit, PLACEHOLDER_AUTH_TOKEN'` with `'streamlit'` in my proxy layer before establishing the websocket handshake, so I did a patch for that.

Maybe it's a good idea for you guys that you rethink the solution? Maybe it can be more robust?

title: Widgets in an st.popover opened inside an st.dialog are occluded by the dialog and unusable
body:
### Checklist
- [x] I have searched the existing issues for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When an `st.popover` is used inside an `st.dialog`, the popover opens but its body
is rendered underneath the dialog's interaction layer. Widgets inside the popover
(e.g. a `selectbox`) cannot be interacted with, and clicking them lands on the
dialog's dismissable overlay — which can close the dialog. This is a regression
from the migration of `st.dialog` to React Aria (#15327); it worked in 1.58.0.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st


@st.dialog("My dialog")
def show_dialog():
    st.write("dialog content")
    with st.popover("Open popover"):
        fruit = st.selectbox("Fruit", ["Apple", "Banana", "Cherry"])
        st.write(f"picked: {fruit}")


if st.button("Open dialog"):
    show_dialog()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app and click **Open dialog**.
2. Inside the dialog, click **Open popover** (the popover body appears).
3. Try to open the popover's `selectbox` dropdown and pick an option.
4. The dropdown does not open; clicking in the popover body instead hits the
   dialog overlay (and can dismiss the dialog).

### Expected Behavior

The popover body renders above the dialog and its widgets are fully interactive:
opening the `selectbox`, picking an option, and having the value commit —
dismissing neither the popover nor the dialog. (This is how it behaved in 1.58.0.)

### Current Behavior

The popover body is occluded by the dialog. The in-popover widget is not
interactable, and interacting with it can close the dialog.

Objective evidence (Playwright, both Chromium and WebKit): hit-testing the
in-popover selectbox at its own center with `document.elementFromPoint` returns
the dialog rather than the widget, and the dropdown cannot be opened even with a
forced click:

```
selectbox_hit = { topTestId: "stDialog", inBody: false, inDialog: true }
dropdown_opened = false
```

Root cause: the popover body is portalled to `document.body` (outside the dialog's
DOM subtree), while `st.dialog` is now a React Aria (`data-rac`) overlay that
establishes its own stacking/overlay layer that paints and hit-tests above the
portalled popover body. Control: a BaseWeb overlay opened from a widget placed
**directly** in the dialog (e.g. a `multiselect` in the dialog) renders correctly
above the dialog, so the dialog does not occlude all portalled overlays — only the
popover body at the `popup` z-tier.

### Is this a regression?
- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

Confirmed via `git bisect` (probe: is the in-popover selectbox usable above the
dialog?):

| Commit | Description | Result |
|--------|-------------|--------|
| tag `1.58.0` (`209ad55c`) | 1.58.0 release (does not contain #15327) | PASS |
| `590deca9` | parent of #15327 | PASS |
| **`a7200715` (#15327)** | **Remove `BaseWeb` for `Dialog` (React Aria migration)** | **FAIL (first bad commit)** |
| `d65a3aae` (#15339) | Remove BaseWeb for Popover (floating-ui) | FAIL (not the cause) |
| current `develop` | — | FAIL |

#15327 shipped in 1.59.0 and is not in 1.58.0, which is why 1.58.0 works and
1.59.0+ is broken. This is independent of the `st.popover` floating-ui migration
(#15339). There is a prior related fix, #15876 "Fix React Aria dialog overlay
stacking", which does not cover this popover-in-dialog case.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: `develop` (reproduces on 1.59.0 and later; first broken in #15327)
- Python version: 3.12.3
- Operating System: Linux
- Browser: Chromium and WebKit (both affected)

### Additional Information

- Scope: only the combination **popover inside a dialog** is affected. Standalone
  popovers, and widgets placed directly in a dialog, work correctly.
- Suggested direction for a fix: render/portal the popover body into the dialog's
  overlay/stacking context when it is opened inside a dialog, or raise the popover
  body to a tier that clears the React Aria dialog overlay (mirroring how direct
  BaseWeb overlays clear it via the `basewebOverlay` tier).
- Found during QA of PR #15961 (which fixes the separate #15959 popover-overlay
  stacking/dismissal issues). This popover-in-dialog gap is not caused by, and is
  out of scope for, that PR.

title: streamlit does not produce WebSocket ping frames
body: ### Checklist - [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary streamlit is supposed to generate WebSocket ping to ensure that the connection to the end-user is not terminated by any proxy sitting between the user and streamlit ### Reproducible Code Example _No response_ ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Build Dockerfile with streamlit==1.34.0 requirements.txt 2. Use `ENTRYPOINT ["streamlit", "hello"]` 3. Run container, e.g. podman run --rm -p 8501:8501 streamlit 4. Oper browser to localhost:8501, open Network inspector and select WebSocket connection messages 5. Note missing ping messages after initial data transfer over WebSocket ### Expected Behavior In `server.py`, there is TORNADO_SETTINGS (https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/406b1e617a4d7c147d199073063c20d6d45cfa3e/lib/streamlit/web/server/server.py#L61-L74) that states that WebSocket ping messages should be sent every second. This does not occur, and causes the WebSocket connection to be dropped when a component between the end-user and streamlit determines that the TCP connection is idle / not active. Since this function does not currently work (tested in 1.34.0 of streamlit), deploying streamlit in any environment can cause connectivity issues, unless the developer writes their own ping logic into streamlit. ### Current Behavior No WebSocket ping messages is sent, code suggests it should be sent. ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. ### Debug info - Streamlit version: streamlit, version 1.34.0 - Python version: Python 3.12.3 - Operating System: (python:3 container image, Linux cdf8d47bc708 6.8.4-200.fc39.aarch64 #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Thu Apr 4 21:00:27 UTC 2024 aarch64 GNU/Linux - Browser: N/A, but Version 124.0.6367.201 (Official Build) (arm64) ### Additional Information I'm assuming this is a regression or upstream bug as a result of library update. I've found similar issues and code changes related to this: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/3464 https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/websocketconnection-websocket-onerror/46298/10

title: st.selectbox fuzzy search only matches contiguous substrings since 1.59.0 (BaseWeb → react-aria migration)
body:
### Checklist
- [x] I have searched the existing issues for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Since 1.59.0 (the `BaseWeb` → react-aria `ComboBox` migration, #15438), typing in
`st.selectbox` only matches options where the query is a **contiguous substring**
of the label. In 1.58.0 the search was truly fuzzy (non-contiguous subsequence),
so e.g. typing `ape` matched both `Grape` and `Apple`. Now it only matches
`Grape`, and queries like `aple` / `rp` that used to match return "No results".

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

FRUITS = ["Apple", "Apricot", "Banana", "Cherry", "Grape", "Mango", "Peach", "Pear"]
v = st.selectbox("Fruit", FRUITS, index=2)  # Banana pre-selected
st.write("value:", v)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app above.
2. Click the selectbox and type `ape`.
3. Observe the dropdown.
4. Repeat with `aple` and `rp`.

### Expected Behavior

Fuzzy (non-contiguous, case-insensitive, label-only, score-ordered) matching, as
in 1.58.0:

| Type | Dropdown |
|------|----------|
| `ape`  | `Grape`, `Apple` |
| `aple` | `Apple` |
| `rp`   | `Grape` |

### Current Behavior

Only contiguous-substring matches survive (1.59.0 through current):

| Type | Dropdown |
|------|----------|
| `ape`  | `Grape` only |
| `aple` | *No results* |
| `rp`   | *No results* |

Root cause appears to be that the react-aria `ComboBox` applies its own built-in
`contains` text filter on top of Streamlit's already-fuzzy-filtered options, so
the visible list is the intersection (substring-only). Streamlit's own
`fuzzyFilterSelectOptions` util is still correct in isolation
(`ape → [Grape, Apple]`), so the fuzzy result is being re-filtered away by the
component. Consider disabling the component's built-in filter (e.g. a pass-through
`defaultFilter`) so Streamlit's fuzzy filter is authoritative.

(Screenshots attached: `EVIDENCE_v1_58_0_gap1_type_ape.png` shows `Grape, Apple`
on 1.58.0; `EVIDENCE_branch_gap1_type_ape.png` shows `Grape` only on 1.59.0+.)

### Is this a regression?
- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

Confirmed via bisect against official PyPI wheels: `ape` → `[Grape, Apple]` on
**1.58.0** (BaseWeb `Select`), `[Grape]` on **1.59.0** (react-aria `ComboBox`).
Identical in Chromium and WebKit. Introduced by #15438.

### Debug info
- Streamlit version: 1.59.0 (introduced); still present in current 1.59.x / dev builds
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: Linux (browser-independent)
- Browser: Chromium and WebKit (both affected)

### Additional Information

- Related migration PR: #15438 (Remove `BaseWeb` for `selectbox`).
- Discovered during QA of #15996 (which fixes the separate type-to-search
  append bug #15985). This filtering regression is independent of that fix.
- `filter_mode="fuzzy"` is the default and the mode affected; `prefix` / `contains`
  behave as documented.

title: Not handled DecodeError on the server side on file upload with double extension
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Hello streamlit team,

first of all thank you for the great work!
We have developed an application using streamlit, deployed our application as a container using Azure App services and in order to tackle the security concerns we have been performing penetration tests.

A minor finding was related to improper error handling, as both on client side and the server side, a traceback should not be displayed because this can pose security risks.

We can't solve it on the application side as the error gets displayed from the streamlit scripts.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
try:
    with st.form("file-upload-form", clear_on_submit=True):
        uploaded_file = st.file_uploader(label='Please select a file.', accept_multiple_files=False, type="xlsx")
        submitted = st.form_submit_button("Upload")
except Exception as e:
    msg = "The file could not be uploaded."
    logger.error(msg)
    st.write(msg)
    raise ValueError(msg)
```


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Download BurpSuite https://portswigger.net/burp/communitydownload 
2. Onboard yourself with:
          - https://portswigger.net/burp/documentation/desktop/getting-started/intercepting-http-traffic 
          - https://portswigger.net/burp/documentation/desktop/getting-started/modifying-http-requests
3. Access the application from the browser from BurpSuite
4. Upload a file with double extension: e.g. test_file.php.xlsx

title: TypeError: `_run_with_thread_state() takes 0 positional arguments but 1 was given` on websocket connect with `@st.fragment(run_every=...)` in 1.58.0
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the existing issues for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

After Streamlit Cloud auto-installed **1.58.0** (released 2026-05-28), every websocket connect to a deployed app raises:

```
TypeError: add_script_run_ctx.<locals>._run_with_thread_state()
  takes 0 positional arguments but 1 was given
```

The error is raised inside the threading wrapper installed by `add_script_run_ctx` in `lib/streamlit/runtime/scriptrunner_utils/script_run_context.py`. The wrapper is defined as:

```python
def _run_with_thread_state() -> None:    # ← 0 positional args
    fields = getattr(thread, _FRAGMENT_THREAD_STATE_FIELDS_ATTR, None)
    if fields is not None:
        ThreadState.initialize(**fields)
    original_run()
thread.run = _run_with_thread_state
```

Something in the new threading path calls `_run_with_thread_state(arg)` with one positional argument, which the wrapper can't accept.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

@st.fragment(run_every="5s")
def live_chart():
    st.write("tick")

live_chart()
```

Deploy to Streamlit Cloud (or run locally with Streamlit 1.58.0 on Python 3.13). The Sentry trace shows the error firing on every websocket connect even when no user-facing breakage is visible — the wrapped thread retries cleanly, so users don't crash, but Sentry floods.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Deploy a Streamlit app with a `@st.fragment(run_every="5s")` (or any positive interval) somewhere in the render path.
2. Open the app in a browser.
3. Observe `TypeError: _run_with_thread_state() takes 0 positional arguments but 1 was given` on every websocket connect.

### Expected Behavior

The fragment thread runs without raising; the auto-refresh works as it did in 1.57.0.

### Current Behavior

`TypeError` fires on every websocket connect. 51 events in 4 hours on our production deploy (5-user friends-alpha) before we pinned to 1.57.0.

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

Last known good: **1.57.0** (released 2026-04-28). Pinning to `streamlit==1.57.0` eliminates the error completely.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.58.0
- Python version: 3.13.13 (CPython)
- Operating System: Streamlit Cloud (Linux container) + reproduced on macOS 15.5
- Browser: Chrome 148 (also Firefox, Safari)

### Additional Information

Sentry trace excerpt:

```
TypeError: add_script_run_ctx.<locals>._run_with_thread_state()
  takes 0 positional arguments but 1 was given
mechanism: threading
transaction: ws://[app].streamlit.app/_stcore/stream
```

Workaround: pin `streamlit==1.57.0` until a fix lands.

Happy to add more detail or test a candidate fix.

body:

There maybe a specific need for the error handler to check the provider in the session, I am not sure, but I wonder if it should be checking for the provider in the `secrest.toml` config instead.

Here the function I am referring to: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/lib/streamlit/web/server/oauth_authlib_routes.py#L164 

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import logging
import os
import time

import streamlit as st
import yaml

from auth import Auth

# For a local run using .env file
if os.environ.get("ENV_SHORT", "LOCAL") == "LOCAL":
    from dotenv import load_dotenv
    load_dotenv()

logging.basicConfig(level='INFO')
logger = logging.getLogger('app.py')


def sso_login():
    """Re-direct the user to Microsoft SSO."""
    if st.session_state["env_short"].lower() == "uat":
        st.title('Streamlit Forms - Testing')
        st.warning("This is a **Testing** environment!  \nUse this link for live environment: https://...")
    else:
        st.title('Streamlit Forms')

    if st.button("Log in with Microsoft"):
        st.login("microsoft")
    st.stop()

def logout():
    """Clear the cookies and session state vars."""
    st.session_state.groups = []
    st.logout()
    st.info("User logged out.")

def forms_pages(groups):

    logoutPage = st.Page(
            logout,
            title="Log out",
            icon=":material/logout:",
        )
    noAccess = st.Page(
            no_access,
            title="Home",
            icon=":material/home:",
        )

    try:
        with open('forms/config.yml') as file:
            forms_config = yaml.safe_load(file)

        forms_config = forms_config['forms']

        formsPages = []

        # Check if the the user is part of the azure groups included in the Forms config.yml file.
        group_set = set(groups)
        for form, values in forms_config.items():
            groups_ids = [group['id'] for group in values['groups']]
            groups_match = group_set.intersection(set(groups_ids))

            # Create the Form page for each match between the config.yml and azure groups the user is member of.
            if len(groups_match) != 0: 
                formsPages.append(
                    st.Page(
                        f"forms/{form}.py",
                        title=values['title'],
                    )
                )
        # If there is no match, point the user to the No Access and Log Out pages to request the access
        if len(formsPages) > 0:
            pg = st.navigation(
            {"Home":formsPages} | {"Account":[logoutPage]}
            )
            pg.run()
        else:
            pg = st.navigation(
            {"Account":[noAccess, logoutPage]}
            )
            pg.run()


    except Exception as error:
        logger.error(f"Something went wrong during the creation of the Forms pages: {error}")
        


# Set up variable for session expiry in 8 hours.
current_time = int(time.time())
hours_in_session = 8 * 60 * 60


# Set up environement:
if "env_short" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state["env_short"] = os.environ["ENV_SHORT"]

if "groups" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state["groups"] = []


# Access checks
try:
    if "error" in st.user:
        st.error("Something went wrong, please **Try Again** or **Raise a Ticket** if the error persists.")
        logger.info(f"Something went wrong during logging attempt via SSO: {st.user.to_dict()}")
        log_again = st.button("Try Again",type="primary")
        if log_again:
            st.logout()
        raise_a_ticket = st.button("Raise a Ticket",type="secondary")
        if raise_a_ticket:
            logger.error(f"Something went wrong during logging via SSO: {st.user.to_dict()}")


    elif not st.user["is_logged_in"]:
        if st.session_state["env_short"].lower() == "uat":
            page_title = 'Streamlit Forms - Testing'
        else:
            page_title = 'Streamlit Forms'

        pg = st.navigation(
            {"Home":[
                    st.Page(
                    sso_login,
                    title=page_title,
                    icon=":material/login:"
                    )
                ]
            }
        )
        pg.run()

    # Delete `st.user` cookies if stayed logged over two days.
    elif current_time > (st.user.exp + hours_in_session):
        logger.info(f"Current time is greater than the exp date. Unicode time: {st.user.exp}. Logging out.")
        st.logout()

    # Render corresponding Forms pages if groups already stored in the state.
    elif len(st.session_state["groups"]) > 0:
        logger.info(f"Groups stored in session state. Number of groups:{len(st.session_state.groups)}")
        forms_pages(st.session_state["groups"])

    # Get list of groups. 
    elif len(st.session_state["groups"]) == 0:
        logger.info("Large group list, calling the API to get all the groups...")
         
        client_id = st.secrets["auth"]["microsoft"]["client_id"]
        client_secret = st.secrets["auth"]["microsoft"]["client_secret"]
        tenant = st.secrets["auth"]["microsoft"]["tenant"]
        auth = Auth(client_id=client_id,client_secret=client_secret,tenant=tenant)

        st.session_state["groups"] = auth.get_groups(st.user["oid"])
        logger.info(f"Fetched the large group list. API response object type: {type(st.session_state['groups'])}.")
        forms_pages(st.session_state["groups"])

except Exception as error:
    st.error(
        "Something went wrong, please **Try Again** "
        "or **Raise a Ticket** if the error persists."
    )

    log_again = st.button("Try Again",type="primary")
    if log_again:
        st.logout()
    raise_a_ticket = st.button("Raise a Ticket",type="secondary")
    if raise_a_ticket:
        logger.error(f"Something went wrong during the Access Check: {error}")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Log in
2. Refresh browser
3. Logout

### Expected Behavior

Since the provider is available in the `secrets.toml` there should not be an error log when a session is reset. 

### Current Behavior

```
Error, missing provider for oauth callback
```

title: Native authentication support for Streamlit
body:
### Summary

We are investigating approaches to add native authentication support for Streamlit, as it is one of the top most requested community features. This is a rough proposal for how it might work, which is shared for your feedback.

### Goals

**Goal 1:** Provide the building blocks for integrating more robust auth solutions including:
- documented support for reading headers (replace the undocumented but heavily used `_get_websocket_headers()`
- native support for reading and writing cookies ( #861 )
- native redirect ( #7123 )
- hooks to add identity information in `st.user`
- _[longer term]_ Support custom http endpoints ( #439 ) - this will be a bigger effort but know we probably need to get there eventually to have a really robust support
- ??? What else ???

**Goal 2:** Provide an out-of-the-box native integration which covers the most common use cases, especially for developers getting started. To that end, we propose **standardizing on OAuth2 & OpenID Connect as the natively supported protocols in Streamlit**.
- This would be an opinionated and minimal implementation, geared towards integrating with standardized OIDC providers.
- Goal would be, with a few lines of config / secrets, you can be set up with `login()` / `logout()` methods and the users verified email, OAuth2 token, and potentially other claims from a JWT readily available through a standard API (likely attributes on `st.user`).
- Ideally, include an easy integration with cookies support so it's trivial to maintain the user auth session across tabs for some time. However, we still need to investigate whether this is feasible or has other major implications.

**Why OpenID Connect (OIDC)?**
- From our perspective, OIDC seems like the most modern, standardized authentication protocol we can use which enables a standard format of user identity claims (including roles / groups) and minimal custom code across providers.
- We also see a wide range of adoption across identity providers both in the consumer space (Google, Apple, etc) and enterprise space (Auth0, AWS Cognito, MSFT Entra ID, etc).
- For most app developers who aren't working in a more sophisticated existing platform, it seems to cover the typical use case for "single sign on" for relatively low fuss and configuration required in the provider side.

**Non-goal: Replace the use of reverse proxy in higher security environments**

We know this practice of running Streamlit behind an auth proxy and forwarding authenticated requests to the app is fairly common among Streamlit usage in bigger companies or those with higher security requirements. We want to build library features that make that easier to run (such as documented headers support) but not replace it or build extremely hardened security into Streamlit, since it isn't our expertise.

But, we think this proposal can still unblock many developers operating in somewhat lower stakes environments who experience a lot of friction today.

### VERY ROUGH API sketch

Here's a very rough first idea of how the API might work for the built-in OIDC.

```toml
# .streamlit/secrets.toml or similar

[auth] # reserved group for defining auth, could also support multiple like [auth.google]
type = "oidc"
provider = "google" # or api_base_url="accounts.google.com"
client_id = "SOME ID"
client_secret = "SOME SECRET"
default_ttl = "7d" # if we have some easy cookie support

```

Once this is configured, you can call some standard methods in the app which will redirect to the appropriate OIDC flow. Streamlit will automatically expose an OAuth2 callback endpoint which handles the response from the identity provider.

In the case below, calling `login()` will simply redirect to the OAuth2 flow. When the user returns from the flow, their identity values will be available in `st.user`. Calling `logout()` will clear the values from `st.user` in that session along with any browser cookies.

```python
# streamlit_app.py

if st.user.logged_in(): # verify log in, including cookie from an earlier session
    st.write(f"Welcome, {st.user.name}!")
    st.sidebar.button("Logout", on_click=st.user.logout)
else:
    st.sidebar.button("Login", on_click=st.user.login)
```

### Other authentication protocols

We know other protocols are used today, such as looking up a username / password in a database (e.g. [Streamlit-Authenticator](https://github.com/mkhorasani/Streamlit-Authenticator)), or more complex delegated authentication schemes like SAML / LDAP. In some cases, the existing plugins / components for these can work pretty well. We'd like to provide some hooks to make them more consistent with the native support (maybe similar to `st.connection`), but it may not be in the initial launch.

### What do you think?

If this proposal and approach sounds good and meets your use case, please give a 👍 . Also, we'd love to hear any comments about what you like, don't like, or would change, or any use case you have which would not be supported. Thanks!!

title: FIPS friendliness
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Streamlit should support [FIPS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Information_Processing_Standards)  friendliness.

When a library or package is not FIPS friendly, it significantly limits your ability to use it commercially since you cant sell that software to the US gov or anyone that works with them.

### Why?

Streamlit is not officially [FIPS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Information_Processing_Standards) compliant. Any current FIPS friendliness seems to be [maintained by the community](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Astreamlit%2Fstreamlit+fips&type=issues). This means that sometimes new Streamlit features are developed that break FIPS requirements. 

The FIPS regressions seem to have been trivial, so it would be nice if they could be caught before release.

### How?

1. Streamlit should run it's pre-release CI suite on a FIPS compliant image and check for crashes. The suite should set up a FIPS environment (like the python-fips chainguard container) and executes a test script to see if unapproved paths are blocked. 
2. Streamlit should run a linter so that we pass `usedforsecurity=False` flag on non-cryptographic internal hashes; like cache key generation, file watchers, session IDs, or anything else we would use MD5 for.
