title: Change handling of non-browser user agents for public apps to avoid infinite redirect loop
body: ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests. - [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue. ### Summary When I try to submit the URL of my public Streamlit app to [OER Commons](https://oercommons.org/), I get an error because their non-browser user agent hits an infinite redirect loop, and so their add resource tool tells me that it's being redirected to an extremely long URL (which is my address plus `/-/login?payload=` plus a long session token. The Snowflake Support team suggested that I open a feature request to change how Streamlit Community Cloud handles session management for non-browser HTTP clients for public apps. ### Why? I’m trying to submit my app to [OER Commons](https://oercommons.org/), and when I submit the URL, it’s telling me that the URL redirects to the same URL with a *very* long login payload param appended, which OER Commons can't process. [According to the Streamlit Community Discussion Board's AgentStreamy AI](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/silent-redirect-with-long-payload-query-param-when-accessing-app/121581), this should only happen with private/invite-only sites, which mine is not (it's always been public). However, according to the Snowflake Support Team, it's actually the result of how Streamlit Community Cloud handles session management for non-browser HTTP clients. Here's the information from their response to my support case: **Root Cause**: We have confirmed that when a non-browser client (such as OER Commons' URL validator) accesses your app, it encounters an infinite redirect loop between three URLs: 1. https://latin-morph.streamlit.app/ 2. https://share.streamlit.io/-/auth/app?redirect_uri=... 3. https://latin-morph.streamlit.app/-/login?payload= This cycle repeats indefinitely because the client cannot execute JavaScript or maintain browser session cookies, which are required for Streamlit Community Cloud's session establishment to complete. Standard web browsers handle this transparently — the session is set via cookies and the app loads normally. Your app is public and works correctly in any standard web browser. This is not a problem with your app's privacy settings or code. This is a platform-level behavior in how Streamlit Community Cloud handles session management for non-browser HTTP clients. Why OER Commons fails: When OER Commons validates your URL, it follows the redirects like a non-browser client, encounters the loop, and reports the error you're seeing (redirect to a problematic URL). ### How? Snowflake Support's suggested solution is to ask the Streamlit Community Cloud team to consider handling non-browser user agents differently for public apps (e.g., serving a simple HTML page to non-browser clients instead of entering the redirect loop), so that's what I'm doing. ### Additional Context Linked above, but [here's my Streamlit Discussion Board post](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/silent-redirect-with-long-payload-query-param-when-accessing-app/121581). title: st.pydeck_chart selection events (on_select="rerun") are never delivered when the chart is inside @st.fragment
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the existing issues for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

`st.pydeck_chart(..., on_select="rerun", key=...)` never delivers the selection event to the server when the chart is rendered **inside a `@st.fragment`**. Clicking a pickable object does nothing: no fragment rerun, no app rerun, no selection state, no console error. Hover picking (auto_highlight + tooltip) works normally, so WebGL picking itself is alive — only the selection event pipeline is dead.

The exact same chart **outside** a fragment works perfectly.

Reproduced on **1.56.0 and 1.59.1** (Windows 11, Python 3.14, pydeck 0.9.x, Chromium via Playwright and real Chrome).

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import pydeck as pdk
import streamlit as st

hexes = ["87a8100d9ffffff", "87a8100dbffffff", "87a8100c1ffffff"]  # neighbors, São Paulo

def chart(key):
    layer = pdk.Layer(
        "H3HexagonLayer",
        data=[{"hex_id": h} for h in hexes],
        id="hexes",
        get_hexagon="hex_id",
        get_fill_color=[0, 150, 255, 160],
        pickable=True,
        auto_highlight=True,
    )
    deck = pdk.Deck(
        layers=[layer],
        initial_view_state=pdk.ViewState(latitude=-23.55, longitude=-46.64, zoom=9),
        map_style=None,
    )
    ev = st.pydeck_chart(deck, on_select="rerun", key=key, height=400)
    objs = getattr(getattr(ev, "selection", None), "objects", {}) or {}
    st.write(key, "->", "SELECTED_OK" if objs else "NO_SELECTION")

st.subheader("Outside fragment — clicking a hexagon WORKS")
chart("outside_fragment")

@st.fragment
def frag():
    st.subheader("Inside @st.fragment — clicking a hexagon does NOTHING")
    chart("inside_fragment")

frag()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. `streamlit run app.py`
2. Click a blue hexagon in the **first** (outside-fragment) chart → `SELECTED_OK` appears.
3. Click a blue hexagon in the **second** (inside-fragment) chart → nothing happens. No rerun (the running indicator never appears), no selection, no browser console error, no server log.

### Expected Behavior

Clicking a pickable object inside a fragment should trigger the fragment rerun and populate `event.selection.objects`, like it does outside a fragment (and like other selection-enabled elements, e.g. `st.plotly_chart`, do inside fragments).

### Current Behavior

The selection event is silently dropped. Hover highlight and tooltips keep working, which makes this quite hard to debug in a real app — the map looks alive but clicks go nowhere.

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version (our production app, whose pydeck chart has lived inside a fragment since May 2026, had working clicks on older Streamlit builds; after rebuilding with a current version the clicks died with no code change).

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.56.0 and 1.59.1 (both reproduce)
- Python version: 3.14 (also 3.11)
- Operating System: Windows 11 / Debian 13 (Docker)
- Browser: Chrome / Chromium

### Additional Information

Found while debugging a production dashboard where the pydeck chart + click handler live inside `@st.fragment` for rerun-cost reasons. Removing the decorator (chart inline in the page) immediately restores click delivery — that is our current workaround.

### Summary

Currently, Streamlit requires rerunning the entire script to refresh visual elements such as charts or plots.
This feature request suggests adding native support for incremental or real-time updates to chart components, allowing smoother dashboards for live data without script reruns.

### Why?

I often build dashboards with data that changes every few seconds (e.g. IoT sensors, live logs, financial data).
The current rerun mechanism makes the app flicker and consume excessive CPU, as every update forces Streamlit to re-execute all widgets and scripts.
A lighter update mechanism would make Streamlit much more efficient for real-time applications.

### How?

Introduce a new method, for example:

chart = st.line_chart(initial_data)
chart.update(new_data)


or a context manager such as:

with st.chart("my_chart") as chart:
    chart.update(data)


This would allow partial UI updates for selected components instead of full script reruns, leading to faster refresh rates and better performance.

### Additional Context

This feature would be highly valuable for real-time dashboards and data streaming use cases.
Similar functionality exists in libraries like Plotly Dash (dcc.Interval) or Bokeh Server.
Discussion inspiration: Streamlit Community Forum – Real-time dashboard performance

title: Callback called with old widget values if script is rerun without finishing
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

The user expects the values they entered to be used for the callback. However, if a user enters a new value for a widget which does not immediately trigger a rerun and then click a button with a callback, then two rerun requests will be sent quickly one after another. If the script then takes time to run and does not reach the line setting the callback before it is rerun, then when the second rerun request is handled, the old callback is called using old callback args.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
import time

if 'foo' in st.session_state:
    st.write(st.session_state['foo'])

text = st.text_input('Text', value='A')

# Wait so that the script may be stopped early for a rerun
time.sleep(1)

def handle_click(value):
    st.session_state['foo'] = value

st.button('Submit', on_click=handle_click, args=[text])
```


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Replace the text input value with "B" and do not press enter or click away
2. Click the "Submit" button

### Expected Behavior

The `handle_click` callback is called with the value "B", and the "B" is written to the screen

### Current Behavior

The `handle_click` callback is called with the value "A", and the "A" is written to the screen.


https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/5288285/c363f130-cac3-42f4-9eca-829cfe78cffe

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.32.2
- Python version: 3.11.5
- Operating System: macOS 13.5.2
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

Disabling `runner.fastReruns` does not fix the issue because the script runner still stops the script early for rerun requests.

This issue begins to appear intermittently later in development as the script takes longer to run because of more widgets or functionality getting added, making it hard to develop reliable apps. For example, with a larger script, clicking the button quickly triggers the issue, but clicking the button slowly allows for the first rerun to complete avoiding the issue.

Using forms instead of callbacks may be a workaround in some cases, but the widgets in a form cannot be used to dynamically display additional information or other widgets.

Adding a caveat to https://docs.streamlit.io/library/api-reference/session-state#caveats-and-limitations which states that widget values should not be passed with `args` and `kwargs` and updating Streamlit docs examples could be good if this is expected behavior.

Example found:
https://docs.streamlit.io/library/advanced-features/session-state#example-3-use-args-and-kwargs-in-callbacks
```Python
increment_value = st.number_input('Enter a value', value=0, step=1)

def increment_counter(increment_value):
    st.session_state.count += increment_value

increment = st.button('Increment', on_click=increment_counter,
    args=(increment_value, ))
```
Other example:
https://towardsdatascience.com/advanced-streamlit-session-state-and-callbacks-for-data-labelling-tool-1e4d9ad32a3f#498e
```Python
def submit_delete_project(project_name: str):
    """ Callback function during deleting an existing project. """
    st.session_state.projects.remove(project_name)
to_delete = st.selectbox('Project to be deleted:',
                         st.session_state.projects)
st.button('Delete project', key='button_delete_project',
          on_click=submit_delete_project, args=(to_delete, ))
```

title: st.context.theme.type does not trigger a rerun when the theme changes
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

According to [this comment](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/5009#issuecomment-2946544937), accessing `st.context.theme.type` in a script should cause the app to automatically rerun when the user changes the theme. This does not happen, the value only updates after a manual rerun.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

st.write(f"Current theme: `{st.context.theme.type}`")
st.write("Change the theme in Settings — this text should update automatically.")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the script above with `streamlit run app.py`
2. Note the theme value shown
3. Open the Settings menu (☰ → Settings) and switch between Light and Dark theme
4. Observe that the displayed theme value does NOT change
5. Manually click the Rerun button. The value now updates correctly

### Expected Behavior

The app reruns automatically when the theme changes, and `st.context.theme.type `reflects the new value without requiring a manual rerun.


### Current Behavior

No automatic rerun occurs. `st.context.theme.type` keeps returning the old value until the user manually triggers a rerun.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

title: Auth cookies set by st.login() are session-scoped in 1.57.0 — Max-Age / Expires not emitted (regression from 1.56)
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

After upgrading from Streamlit 1.56.0 to 1.57.0, the cookies set by `st.login()` (`_streamlit_user`, `_streamlit_user_tokens`) are emitted with neither `Max-Age` nor `Expires`. Per RFC 6265 §5.3, browsers therefore treat them as non-persistent (session) cookies and discard them when the browser is closed. The [`st.login` docs](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/user/st.login) state the identity cookie should persist for 30 days, which was the behaviour in 1.56.0.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
# app.py
import streamlit as st

if not st.user.is_logged_in:
    if st.button("Log in"):
        st.login(provider="auth0")
    st.stop()

st.success(f"Logged in as {st.user.email}")
st.button("Log out", on_click=st.logout)
```

`.streamlit/secrets.toml`:

```toml
[auth]
redirect_uri  = "http://localhost:8501/oauth2callback"
cookie_secret = "<a-random-32-byte-string>"

[auth.auth0]
client_id            = "YOUR_AUTH0_CLIENT_ID"
client_secret        = "YOUR_AUTH0_CLIENT_SECRET"
server_metadata_url  = "https://YOUR-TENANT.us.auth0.com/.well-known/openid-configuration"
```

Install with `pip install 'streamlit[auth]==1.57.0' httpx authlib`, run with `streamlit run app.py`.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app above against any Auth0 (or other OIDC) tenant.
2. Click **Log in**, complete the OAuth flow, land back on the app logged in.
3. Open DevTools → **Application** → **Cookies** → `http://localhost:8501`.
4. Look at the **Expires / Max-Age** column for `_streamlit_user` and `_streamlit_user_tokens`. On 1.57.0 the value is **`Session`**.
5. Close the browser entirely, reopen it, return to the app URL — you are logged out.

For a network-level trace, inspect the `Set-Cookie` response headers from `GET /oauth2callback`:

```
set-cookie: _streamlit_user=...;        HttpOnly; Path=/; SameSite=lax
            _streamlit_user_tokens=...; HttpOnly; Path=/; SameSite=lax
```

Compare to 1.56.0 on the same app — both cookies have `Expires=<~30 days out>`.

### Expected Behavior

`_streamlit_user` and `_streamlit_user_tokens` are emitted with a `Max-Age` (or `Expires`) of ~30 days, matching both the documented `st.login` behaviour and 1.56.0's behaviour. Closing the browser and reopening it should not log the user out.

### Current Behavior

Both cookies are emitted with no `Max-Age` and no `Expires`. Browsers treat them as session cookies; closing the browser logs the user out. The signed-payload server-side validation TTL of 31 days in `decode_signed_value(..., max_age_days=31)` is unchanged, suggesting the intent of the Starlette migration was to preserve ~30-day persistence and that the missing `max_age` argument is an oversight.

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

The regression appears to originate in [PR #14553 "Make Starlette the default server and remove Tornado"](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/14553). The pre-1.57 code path went through Tornado's `set_signed_cookie(...)` / `set_secure_cookie(...)`, which defaults `expires_days=30` when the kwarg is omitted. The new path emits the cookie via Starlette's `Response.set_cookie(...)`, which has no implicit `max_age` default — so the attribute is simply absent unless passed explicitly.

Relevant code in `lib/streamlit/web/server/starlette/starlette_auth_routes.py`:

```python
def _set_single_cookie(
    response: Response, cookie_name: str, serialized_value: str
) -> None:
    cookie_secret = get_cookie_secret()
    signed_value = create_signed_value(cookie_secret, cookie_name, serialized_value)
    cookie_payload = signed_value.decode("utf-8")
    response.set_cookie(
        cookie_name,
        cookie_payload,
        httponly=True,
        samesite="lax",
        path=_get_cookie_path(),
        # max_age=... is missing here
    )
```

A community report of the same problem is open on the Streamlit forum: <https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/auth-cookie-persistence-broken-in-1-57-0-starlette-migration/121410>.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.57.0
- Python version: 3.13
- Operating System: Ubuntu 24.04 (WSL2)
- Browser: Chrome 141
- OS-level: Tornado removed; Starlette 1.0.0 / Uvicorn 0.47.0 / websockets 16.0 from the `streamlit[auth]==1.57.0` extra plus Authlib 1.7.2 and httpx 0.28.1.

I am happy to follow up with a PR adding `max_age` to `_set_single_cookie` (and a regression test asserting the `Set-Cookie` attributes), restoring the documented 30-day default, if that approach is acceptable.

title: st.tabs: widget rerun inside a tab renders all tabs' content stacked below the page (regression in 1.59.0)
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

**Regression in 1.59.0** (1.58.0 is fine): when a widget inside an `st.tabs` tab triggers a rerun, the tab bar disappears and the content of **all** tabs renders stacked vertically down the page, as if the tabs container no longer exists. A browser reload restores the tabs until the next widget interaction.

Possibly related to the tabs DOM rework in 1.59.0: in 1.58.0 each tab renders a `[data-baseweb="tab-panel"]` element (4 tabs → 4 panels, 1 visible); in 1.59.0 those elements are gone entirely.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import altair as alt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st

st.title("Tabs regression repro")

rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
df = pd.DataFrame({"x": range(20), "y": rng.rand(20)})


def tab_content(name: str) -> None:
    st.metric("Metric", name)
    st.dataframe(df.head(3))
    st.altair_chart(alt.Chart(df).mark_bar().encode(x="x:O", y="y:Q"), use_container_width=True)
    st.altair_chart(alt.Chart(df).mark_line().encode(x="x:O", y="y:Q"), use_container_width=True)
    st.subheader("Leaderboard")
    choice = st.selectbox("Date range", ["A", "B", "C"], key=f"{name}_sel")
    n = {"A": 5, "B": 10, "C": 15}[choice]
    st.altair_chart(alt.Chart(df.head(n)).mark_bar().encode(x="y:Q", y="x:O"), use_container_width=True)


names = ["All", "Indy", "Clarksville", "Fort Wayne"]
for tab, name in zip(st.tabs(names), names):
    with tab:
        tab_content(name)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. `pip install streamlit==1.59.0 altair` and run the app above.
2. Stay on the first tab ("All").
3. Change the "Date range" selectbox from "A" to "B".

### Expected Behavior

The rerun re-renders the first tab's content in place; the other three tabs stay hidden behind the tab bar (this is the 1.58.0 behavior).

### Current Behavior

After the rerun the tab bar vanishes and the content of all four tabs is appended down the page in sequence. Measured headlessly (Playwright, counting `[data-testid="stVegaLiteChart"]` elements with a non-null `offsetParent`): 3 charts visible before the selectbox change, all 12 visible after. The same script against 1.58.0 shows 3 before / 3 after.

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version (1.58.0).

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.59.0 (broken), 1.58.0 (works)
- Python version: 3.11
- Operating System: reproduced on both macOS 15 and Raspberry Pi OS (Linux/arm64)
- Browser: Chrome, and headless Chromium via Playwright

title: Fragments are awesome but must to be more: Selective Rerun and Execution Control
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

### Feature Request: Selective Rerun and Execution Control for `st.fragment`

Hi Streamlit team 👋

First of all, great job with the `st.fragment` feature — it’s super useful for improving interactivity and modularizing Streamlit apps.

I’d like to suggest two improvements for `st.fragment` that would make it even more powerful in terms of performance and control.

1. [also covered in #10603] The first is the ability to explicitly trigger the rerun of specific fragments from anywhere in the app, instead of being limited to interactions within that fragment. This would allow for more coordinated updates between fragments without requiring a full app rerun.

2. The second idea is to let developers prevent certain fragments from re-executing during a full rerun, keeping their state and UI output intact unless their input parameters change or they are explicitly refreshed. This would improve performance and user experience by avoiding unnecessary recomputation and visual flickering.

Overall, these additions would give developers finer control over fragment behavior and app performance.

Thanks for considering this! 🙏

### Why?

#### Why this would be useful

These two ideas would allow for finer-grained control over how fragments behave during reruns, enabling developers to:

* Improve performance in apps with multiple heavy components.
* Avoid unnecessary recomputation and UI flicker.
* Trigger coordinated updates between fragments dynamically.

Internally, I imagine Streamlit already tracks the execution scope and state for each fragment, so this might be feasible with some form of dependency or caching mechanism.

Thanks a lot for considering this! 🙏
I’d be happy to help clarify or provide examples if needed.

### How?

#### 1. Selective rerun of specific fragments

Right now, when something inside a fragment is interacted with, Streamlit reruns that fragment only, which is great.
However, it would be even better if we could *trigger reruns of specific fragments programmatically* — for example, from another fragment or from the main app.

Imagine something like:

```python
st.fragment(key="fragment_a")
def my_fragmen_a(param1, param2):
    ...

st.fragment(key="fragment_b")
def my_fragmen_b(param1, param2):
    ...

# Somewhere else:
st.rerun(scope=["fragment_a", "fragment_b"])
```

So if you define a fragment with a key, you could explicitly trigger its rerun (with or without passing new parameters).
This would make it possible to coordinate updates between fragments in a controlled way, without forcing a full rerun of the app.

---

#### 2. Ability to skip rerun for some fragments on full app rerun

Another idea: when the app performs a full rerun, it would be great to have a way to mark certain fragments so they *don’t* re-execute — keeping their current state and UI output as-is.

For example, you might have a heavy fragment (long computation, visualization, etc.) that you don’t want to rerun unless its input parameters have actually changed.

Something like:

```python
@st.fragment(key="heavy_plot", rerun="explicit")
def heavy_plot(data):
    ...
```

If the fragment’s inputs haven’t changed and no internal interaction happened, Streamlit could just reuse the previous rendered output instead of re-running the code.
This would not only improve performance but also help avoid UI flickering (the “greyed out” state that appears during reruns).

### Additional Context

_No response_

```Python
import streamlit as st
```

title: "Download to CSV" export from `st.dataframe` excludes hierarchical column headers
body:
### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary The "Download to CSV" button built into the `st.dataframe` UI does not properly export dataframes that use hierarchical / multi-index column headers. When exporting a dataframe that uses multi-index columns, only the lowest level of the column headers will be included in the resulting CSV file. ### Reproducible Code Example ```Python import pandas as pd import streamlit as st first_level = ["2022", "2023"] second_level = ["Q1", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4"] multi_columns = pd.MultiIndex.from_product([first_level, second_level]) df = pd.DataFrame( [[23, 33, 22, 44, 45, 66, 31, 18], [11, 16, 47, 53, 78, 82, 9, 14]], index=["Sales", "Marketing"], columns=multi_columns, ) st.dataframe(df) ``` ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Run the app. 2. Hover your cursor over the table to display the dataframe toolbar. 3. Click the "Download to CSV" button in the toolbar. 4. Open the downloaded CSV file and compare it to the original table. ### Expected Behavior The downloaded CSV file should contain the following data, with both levels of the hierarchical column headers included.
2022 2022 2022 2022 2023 2023 2023 2023
Q1 Q2 Q3 Q4 Q1 Q2 Q3 Q4
Sales 23 33 22 44 45 66 31 18
Marketing 11 16 47 53 78 82 9 14
### Current Behavior The downloaded CSV file contains this data, only including the second level of the column header.
Q1 Q2 Q3 Q4 Q1 Q2 Q3 Q4
Sales 23 33 22 44 45 66 31 18
Marketing 11 16 47 53 78 82 9 14
### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. ### Debug info - Streamlit version: 1.59.0 - Python version: 3.14.6 - Operating System: macOS Tahoe 26.5.1 - Browser: Safari 26.5 ### Additional Information `pandas.DataFrame.to_csv` correctly includes all levels of the column headers, so the following `st.download_button` may be used as a workaround if necessary. ``` exported_df = df.to_csv() st.download_button( "Download Table Data", exported_df, mime="text/csv", ) ```

title: OAuth MismatchingStateError regression in 1.57.0 (works in 1.56.0)
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

# Streamlit OAuth Authentication Issue on Cloud Run

## Problem

Two issues with Streamlit native auth (`st.login`) on Cloud Run staging deployment:

1. First-login error: clicking "Log in with Google" → picking account → server error. Reloading the tab made it work.
2. Session persistence: re-authentication required on every interaction.

## Root Cause

Regression in Streamlit 1.57.0 affecting OAuth state/cookie handling.

Error from Cloud Run logs:

authlib.integrations.base_client.errors.MismatchingStateError:
mismatching_state: CSRF Warning! State not equal in request and response.

This occurred in the `/oauth2callback` endpoint when Authlib tried to validate the OAuth `state` parameter against the session cookie. They didn't match, indicating the cookie was lost or overwritten during the OAuth roundtrip.

## Investigation Path

| Step | What we checked | Outcome |
|------|-----------------|---------|
| 1 | Cloud Run instances (min/max) | Already pinned to 1, not the cause |
| 2 | `cookie_secret` stability | Stable across deploys, not the cause |
| 3 | Cloud Run logs (full traceback) | Found `MismatchingStateError` in Authlib |
| 4 | Streamlit version drift | Local: 1.56.0, Cloud Run: 1.57.0 |
| 5 | Pinned to 1.56.0 | Fixed |

## Solution

Pin Streamlit to 1.56.0 in `requirements.txt`:

title: `st.selectbox` with many options (~16k) freezes on open in 1.59.0 — forced reflow in StreamlitMarkdown (regression from 1.58.0)
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

An `st.selectbox` populated with a large number of options (~16,000) becomes effectively unusable in **1.59.0**: clicking to open the dropdown freezes the main thread for ~25 seconds. During the freeze the widget is greyed out (stale/running state) and neither clicking nor scrolling works. The same code on **1.58.0** opens the dropdown in ~0.5 s and is fully responsive.

A Chrome DevTools performance trace of the open interaction shows the time is dominated by a **forced reflow / layout thrashing**, with the top contributing call frame inside **`StreamlitMarkdown`** (plus `useFloatingOverlay` from the dropdown). On 1.58.0 the "Forced reflow" insight does not appear at all for the same interaction.

This looks like a rendering regression in how selectbox options are rendered in 1.59.0 (each option appears to go through the Markdown renderer). The 1.59 changelog includes a "fix selectbox format_func object-identity" change (#15618) which touches this code path.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

# ~16k options, with a trivial format_func (mirrors a real destination-search selectbox)
options = [f"{40000 + i} - LOCATION NAME {i}" for i in range(16000)]

choice = st.selectbox(
    "Search destination",
    options=options,
    index=None,
    format_func=lambda o: o,
)
st.write(choice)
```

### Steps To Reproduce


1. Run the app above with **streamlit==1.59.0**.
2. Click the selectbox to open the dropdown.
3. Observe the widget greys out and the tab freezes for ~25 s (no click / no scroll).
4. Downgrade to **streamlit==1.58.0**, rerun, repeat: the dropdown opens in ~0.5 s and is responsive.

### Expected Behavior


Opening a selectbox with a large option list should stay responsive (as it does in 1.58.0 — ~0.5 s to open), without freezing the main thread.

### Current Behavior

On 1.59.0 the open interaction blocks the main thread ~25 s. Measured with Chrome DevTools (Performance):

- 1.58.0: interaction (INP) ~495 ms, no "Forced reflow" insight, widget stays interactive (white).
- 1.59.0: ~26 s of blocked main thread, "Forced reflow" insight ~4.4 s, top frame inside `StreamlitMarkdown` (+ `useFloatingOverlay`); widget greyed out / not clickable.

Reproduced with the minimal snippet above **in isolation** (no other app code): on 1.59.0 the selectbox never becomes interactive on open (stays greyed ~25 s); on 1.58.0 it opens immediately.

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version:- Streamlit version: 1.59.0 (vs 1.58.0 OK)
- Python version: 3.13
- Operating System: Windows 11
- Browser: Chrome
- Python version:
- Operating System:
- Browser:


### Additional Information

The forced reflow is dominated by `StreamlitMarkdown` — each of the ~16k options appears to be rendered through the Markdown renderer, and combined with the dropdown's `useFloatingOverlay` (which reads layout geometry) this triggers heavy synchronous layout on open. Suspected related change: #15618 ("fix selectbox format_func object-identity"), which modified the selectbox option render path in 1.59.

title: Regression in v1.49.0 when showing layered altair chart in dialog - tooltips not showing when a facet option is specified
body: ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary I have encountered a regression in how layered altair charts are displayed in dialogs in 1.49.0 vs how they worked in 1.48.0. If you specify a facet (`color`, `strokeWidth`, ...) in the chart encoding, tooltips only show up for the last layer in the chart and the other layers no longer show a tooltip. This only happens for dialogs and not for showing the chart in the page regularly. If you remove the facet encoding (`color` for example), it works correctly, but this means that we would need to have as many chart layers as we have variables, which is quite inconvenient and breaks how altair usually expects data to be fed to it. ### Reproducible Code Example [![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-12390) ```Python import streamlit as st import pandas as pd import altair as alt def _create_chart(): """ Same chart code for both page and dialog """ df = pd.DataFrame( { "x": [1, 2, 3], "y": [4, 5, 6], "y2": [1, 2, 3], # in this case, having a facet encoding doesn't make sense, but usually we'd have multiple kpis here "kpi": ["kpi1", "kpi1", "kpi1"], } ) chart1 = ( alt.Chart(df) .mark_line(point=alt.OverlayMarkDef(size=80)) .encode(x="x", y="y", color="kpi", tooltip=["x", "y"]) .interactive() ) chart2 = ( alt.Chart(df) .mark_area() .encode(x="x", y="y2", color="kpi", tooltip=["x", "y2"]) ) chart = alt.layer(chart1, chart2) return chart @st.dialog("Dialog with Chart", width="large") def show_dialog(): # show the chart in the dialog chart = _create_chart() st.altair_chart(chart) # show the chart in the page chart = _create_chart() st.altair_chart(chart) show_dialog_btn = st.button("Show Dialog") if show_dialog_btn: show_dialog() ``` ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Hover over both layers in the page chart, make sure both are showing up 2. Click on the "Show Dialog" button 3. Hover over both layers in the dialog, only the area chart tooltip shows up ### Expected Behavior Tooltips should show up for all layers for both page and dialog ### Current Behavior Only the tooltip for the last layer in the layered chart in the dialog is shown ### Is this a regression? - [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. ### Debug info - Streamlit version: 1.49.0, 1.49.1 - Python version: 3.12 - Operating System: MacOS - Browser: Safari, Chrome, Firefox ### Additional Information _No response_

title: Programmatically closed popovers reopen when interacting with another stateful popover
body: ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary [![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-14943) The widget state for stateful (with user set key, and on_change="rerun") st.popover objects is being overridden or handled incorrectly when there are multiple stateful popovers on the page. This results in a bug where opening a second popover after a popover is closed programmatically results in the first popover re-opening alongside the second. This only happens when the first popover is closed programmatically by setting the session state key value to False. Closing the popover by clicking outside the container or clicking the expander icon does not lead to this issue. The minimal example below works fine in streamlit v1.55.0 but results in the described behaviour in 1.56.0. Presumably this bug was introduced somewhere in commit 5feecf4 ### Reproducible Code Example ```Python import streamlit as st def close_first_popover(): st.session_state.first_popover = False def close_second_popover(): st.session_state.second_popover = False with st.popover("A popover", key="first_popover", on_change="rerun"): st.button("Close First", on_click=close_first_popover) with st.popover("Another popover", key="second_popover", on_change="rerun"): st.button("Close Second", on_click=close_second_popover) ``` ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Run the code example 2. Open a popover 3. Close the popover by clicking the button inside 4. Open the other popover 5. Both popovers open together ### Expected Behavior _No response_ ### Current Behavior ### Is this a regression? - [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. ### Debug info - Streamlit version: 1.56.0 - Python version: 3.13.7 - Operating System: OpenSuse - Browser: Firefox/Chrome ### Additional Information _No response_

title: Multiselect Visual State vs Returned Value Mismatch
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

After `st.rerun()` following cache clear, sidebar multiselect shows one selection visually but returns different values to the code.

### Reproducible Code Example

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-12305)

```Python
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

# Cached data function that returns test data
@st.cache_data
def load_test_data():
    return pd.DataFrame({
        'id': ['item_1', 'item_2', 'item_3'],
        'type': ['TypeA', 'TypeB', 'TypeC'],
        'value': [100, 200, 300]
    })

st.title("Multiselect Bug Reproducer")

# Sidebar with reload button (matching original pattern)
with st.sidebar:
    st.header("Data Management")
    if st.button("🔄 Reload Data", help="Clear cache and reload"):
        load_test_data.clear()
        st.success("Cache cleared! Data will be reloaded.")
        st.rerun()

# Load data
df = load_test_data()

# Extract unique types (matching original pattern)
all_types = sorted(df['type'].dropna().unique())

# Sidebar filters (matching original pattern)
st.sidebar.header("Filters") 

# Create multiselect in sidebar with all types as default
selected_types = st.sidebar.multiselect(
    "Select Types",
    all_types,
    default=all_types,  # All selected by default
)

# Filter data based on selection
filtered_df = df.copy()
if selected_types:
    filtered_df = filtered_df[filtered_df['type'].isin(selected_types)]

# Show debug info that reveals the bug
st.write("### Debug Information:")
st.write(f"**Multiselect shows selected**: {selected_types}")
st.write(f"**Filtered data rows**: {len(filtered_df)}")
st.write(f"**Item IDs in filtered data**: {sorted(filtered_df['id'].tolist())}")

st.write("---")
st.write("### Steps to reproduce bug:")
st.write("1. Initially all types are selected → shows 3 rows")
st.write("2. **In sidebar, deselect 'TypeA'** → should show 2 rows")
st.write("3. **Click 'Reload Data' button in sidebar**")
st.write("4. **BUG**: Sidebar shows 'TypeB, TypeC' but filtered data includes all 3 rows")

st.write("### Show actual data:")
st.dataframe(filtered_df)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Put the above in `reproducer.py` and run
2. Deselect "TypeA" in sidebar (UI shows "TypeB, TypeC" selected)
3. Click "🔄 Reload Data" button in sidebar
4. **BUG**: UI still shows "TypeB, TypeC" but code receives `['TypeA', 'TypeB', 'TypeC']`


### Expected Behavior

Multiselect returns what it shows visually.

### Current Behavior

- Visual: Shows "TypeB, TypeC" ✅
- Returned: `['TypeA', 'TypeB', 'TypeC']` ❌


### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.45.1
- Python version: 3.12.1
- Operating System: macOS
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

I originally discussed this [here]( https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/clearing-cache-on-a-single-method-screws-up-multiselect-selected-items/119093) and it looks like [this discussion](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/multipage-with-multiselect-default-and-session-state/52619) may also be relevant. 

  Related GitHub Issues:
  - Issue #6079: "session_state not actually changed until second page reload" - Documents that session_state doesn't update immediately after widget interaction, requiring double reloads
  - Issue #4223: "Issue in multiselect - default and current value overlap" - Reports similar problems where default parameters conflict with current selections in multiselect widgets
  - Issue #4695: "multiselect reset to defaults behavior is inconsistent" - Documents inconsistent behavior when multiselect widgets reset to defaults during reruns

### Summary

I would like to see a parameter on the `st.multiselect` widget to enable or disable the "Select all" option.
The suggested parameter `select_all` can be True by default to sustain the current behavier.

### Why?

Currently, I've an application where users can choose a single or multiple options to plot each option a line object on a Plotly chart. However, for this use case, the number of options exceeds over a 1000.

If the user selects the first "Select all" option, the application will create 1000+ Plotly line objects and create a cluttered and very resource heavy plot that doesn't serve any practical use case.

There is of course the `max_selections` parameter to limit the number of selected options, but there are use cases that all options don't per se relate to each other. This workaround also creates confusion to the end-users since the "Select all" option doesn't select all available options due to the `max_selections` limitation.

### How?

Include the following parameter: `select_all_opt`:

```python
def multiselect (**other_existing_params, select_all_opt:bool = True)
"""
[Current description of multiselect]

Parameters
----------
[Other current parameters]

select_all_opt: bool, default = True
   Option to enable or disable the "Select all" option on this widget. If `True`, the user can select all available options in one click. If `max_selections` is provided, the widget will only select the first n of available options
"""
- 
```

### Additional Context

title: Health check endpoint seems to break when deployed in certain cloud environments
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Hi,
I really enjoy using streamlit to deploy all sorts of applications, but I consistently run into an issue that I have started to be able to reproduce, but is very difficult to understand. I have seen people discuss this issue before, but I haven't been able to find a version of streamlit that fixes the issue. Essentially, the application seems to refresh on me after a certain period of time. Here is one example.

https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/i-get-kicked-out-of-my-app-at-random-times/28316

### Reproducible Code Example

N/A

### Steps To Reproduce

Deploy a long running application to a non streamlit cloud environment using docker.

### Expected Behavior

I expect the _stcore/health to not throw an exception, seemingly causing my application to refresh.

### Current Behavior

Essentially, the gist of the issue is that when I deploy this using Docker to a cloud environment (AWS/Azure), I find the call made to the /_stcore/health endpoint **fails to parse on the frontend**. The endpoint produces a response with the text "ok", but further into the code, it seems the axios library tries to parse this response as json using JSON.parse(). However, this results in an error, which seems to refresh the page. I don't know how often the health endpoint is called, but it seems like it happens approximately every 5 minutes, so for long running processes, these don't end up finishing.

I tried to trace the bug through the streamlit codebase and found that perhaps you are returning the text "ok" on line 519 in the function labeled "is_ready_for_browser_connection". This seems to get returned to the UI, likely through in the "HealthHandler" class on line 148 in the get function. I suspect self.write() will converts dictionaries to json and text is just returned as text through the API. However, perhaps returning the dictionary {"status": "ok"} might fix the issue. 

From the code and stacktrace, it seems there is a websocket that attempts to close, and before closing, it pings the server (the health check), however, the health check indicates it is "ok" and should keep the websocket open. However, an exception occurs during the parsing of the health check, so the connection is closed and perhaps that is when the page refreshes.

Importantly, this does not seem to happen for me in the Streamlit Cloud nor locally, likely because neither seem to call the health check endpoint. The streamlit cloud seems to call the app/status endpoint and locally, no health checks are performed.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.24.0
- Python version: 3.8.16
- Operating System: Windows
- Browser: Chrome/Edge


### Additional Information

**Preview of the endpoint (base url removed)**
![image](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/107218510/11e28e3d-def1-4e67-8698-57671851981f)

**Preview of the response**
![image](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/107218510/0bc3fa7b-32f8-4e9b-8eb1-6b935deca53c)

title: Enhance menu button with download payload capability
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

The new `st.menu_button` is a welcome addition. It would be more useful if it could be combined with download behavior: the user picks an export format from a menu (for example Markdown, plain text, or PDF), and Streamlit serves the matching file without requiring a separate `st.download_button` or fragile conditional wiring for each format.
The idea is a single control—similar to an **Export** menu in desktop apps—where each menu option is tied to download metadata (`data`, `file_name`, `mime`) so “choose format → file downloads” is a first-class pattern.


### Why?

Today, `st.menu_button` only communicates **which option was selected** on the rerun where the user picks something; **sending bytes to the browser still requires `st.download_button`** (or other workarounds). In practice that causes:
- **Awkward UX**: pick a format from the menu, then click again to download—or rely on `st.session_state` because the menu’s return value resets on later reruns.
- **Repeated boilerplate**: every app reimplements mapping from “format label” → `data` / `file_name` / `mime`.
- **Cost vs. laziness**: precomputing every variant (e.g. large PDFs or zips) wastes CPU and memory; deferring generation until after a choice fights Streamlit’s rerun model unless authors invent their own patterns.
A combined primitive would match common product UI, reduce custom session-state hacks, and make multi-format export easier to build and maintain.

### How?

Ship either a **new widget** (for example `st.download_menu_button`) or an **extension** of `st.menu_button` / `st.download_button` so one control can:
1. Show a dropdown of export labels.
2. On selection, trigger a download using the **payload mapped to that label**.
**Options API (sketch for discussion)**
Accept a structured mapping instead of plain string labels only, for example:
- A **list of tuples or small dicts**, e.g. `(label, file_name, mime, data)`; or  
- A **dict** keyed by label with values like `{ "data": ..., "file_name": ..., "mime": ... }`.
**Lazy payloads**
Allow `data` (or the equivalent field) to be a **callable** that Streamlit invokes **only when that option is chosen**, so expensive exports are not built on every rerun. Document when the callable runs, error handling, and any constraints (e.g. serialization, size limits).

title: Updating selectbox selection that is saved in st.session_state needs to be clicked twice
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Hello everyone. 

In my use case, I have a multipage application, with an st.selectbox on top of every subpage. The default value of those selectboxes is taken from st.session_state. The bug I have encountered now is that when I want to update the selectbox value I need to select the new value twice. An example

Selected option: 1
I select option 2.
Selected option: 1
I select option 2 again.
Selected option: 2

From then on the value is updated and working as expected. This behavior is 100% reproducible for me but only happening after I updated the selected option once i.e. directly after the start of the application it works fine and expected once. Afterward I need to double select the options.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
app.py:
import streamlit as st

def main():
    pg = st.navigation([st.Page("page1.py")])
    pg.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()





page1.py:
import streamlit as st


def page():
    if "selectedIndex" not in st.session_state:
        st.session_state["selectedIndex"] = 0
    
    selectedIndex = st.selectbox(
        label="Select something:", 
        options=range(0, 5),
        index=st.session_state["selectedIndex"]
    )
    
    st.session_state["selectedIndex"] = selectedIndex
    
    st.write(f"You selected {selectedIndex}.")
    st.write(f"Session state {st.session_state["selectedIndex"]}.")


page()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Start the application `streamlit run app.py`
2. Update the select box value to 3.
4. Select option 1.
6. Select option 1 again.

You can repeat steps 4-7 as often as you want; it will happen every time.

### Expected Behavior

1. Start the application `streamlit run app.py`
2. Update the select box value to 3.
3. The value is now correctly set as 3.
4. Select option 1.6. 
5. The value is now correctly set as 1.

### Current Behavior

No error messages.

1. Start the application `streamlit run app.py`
2. Update the select box value to 3.
3. The value is now correctly set as 3.
4. Select option 1.
5. The selected value will jump back to 3. The return value and session state value also don't update.
6. Select option 1 again.
7. The value is now correctly set as 1.
You can repeat steps 4-7 as often as you want; it will happen every time.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.56
- Python version: 3.12.7
- Operating System: Windows 11
- Browser: Firefox 149.0.2

### Summary

I'm using Langgraph with `st.write_stream`. I've observed the following:
Case 1: Using  `@st.cache_resource` to cache the model connection and `.stream`. Chatbot works well with no error.

```
_chat_msg.write_stream(stream_output())
```

Case 2: Without `@st.cache_resource`  and `.astream` i.e. async version. Chatbot works well with no error.

```
_chat_msg.write_stream(stream_output())
```

Case 3: Using  `@st.cache_resource` to cache the model connection and `.astream` i.e. async version. Chatbot gives `RuntimeError: Event loop is closed` error after the first turn of the conversation.

```
@st.cache_resource
def get_LLM(llm_name:str = "mistral-small3.2:24b"):
    from langchain_ollama import ChatOllama
    model = ChatOllama(model=llm_name, temperature=0)
    return model
```
and

```
_chat_msg.write_stream(stream_output())
```

It will run in 3rd turn of the conversation without any error in case 3 as well.


### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
from langgraph.graph.message import MessagesState
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, START, END
from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, AIMessage, SystemMessage, ToolMessage
from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import MemorySaver

if 'history' not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state['history'] = MemorySaver()
    st.session_state['config'] = {'configurable': {'thread_id' : 'abc123'} }

@st.cache_resource
def get_LLM(llm_name:str = "mistral-small3.2:24b"):
    from langchain_ollama import ChatOllama
    model = ChatOllama(model=llm_name, temperature=0)
    return model

@st.cache_resource
def get_graph():
    graph = StateGraph(MessagesState)
    graph.add_node(node='chat_node', action=chat_node)
    graph.add_edge(start_key=START, end_key='chat_node')
    graph.add_edge(start_key='chat_node', end_key=END)
    return graph

async def chat_node(state: MessagesState) -> MessagesState:
    """A simple chat node that uses the model to respond to the last human message."""
    messages = state['messages']
    from langchain_ollama import ChatOllama
    model = get_LLM('mistral-small3.2:24b') ## any other LLM such as OpenAI
    response = await model.ainvoke(messages)
    return {'messages': [response]}

messages = st.session_state['history'].get(config=st.session_state['config'])
if messages is not None:
    for message in messages['channel_values']['messages']:
        if isinstance(message, HumanMessage):
            _chat_msg = st.chat_message(name='human')
            _chat_msg.markdown(message.content, unsafe_allow_html=True)
        elif isinstance(message, AIMessage):
            _chat_msg = st.chat_message(name='ai', avatar=':material/support_agent:')
            _chat_msg.markdown(message.content, unsafe_allow_html=True)

if chat_input := st.chat_input('What can I help with?'):
    _chat_msg = st.chat_message(name='human')
    _chat_msg.markdown(chat_input, unsafe_allow_html=True)
    _chat_msg = st.chat_message(name='ai', avatar=':material/support_agent:')

    graph = get_graph()
    chatbot = graph.compile(checkpointer=st.session_state['history'])  # Compile the graph with the checkpointing mechanism

    result = chatbot.astream({'messages': [HumanMessage(content=chat_input)]},
        stream_mode='messages',
        config=st.session_state['config']
    )
    async def stream_output():
        async for chunk, meta_data in result:
            yield chunk.content

    _chat_msg.write_stream(stream_output())
```

title: Selectbox dropdown renders behind st.dialog (options hidden, mouse clicks don't register)
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When an `st.selectbox` is placed inside an `st.dialog`, opening its dropdown renders the option list **behind** the dialog. The options are visually hidden and mouse clicks fall through to the widgets stacked on top, so the selection never changes. Keyboard selection (↓ + Enter) still works, which is the giveaway that the options exist but are not reachable by mouse.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

@st.dialog("Dialog with selectboxes")
def show_dialog():
    a = st.selectbox("First", ["one", "two", "three", "four", "five"], key="a")
    b = st.selectbox("Second", ["alpha", "beta", "gamma"], key="b")
    c = st.selectbox("Third", ["red", "green", "blue"], key="c")
    st.write({"First": a, "Second": b, "Third": c})

if st.button("Open dialog"):
    show_dialog()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app and click **Open dialog**.
2. Click the **First** selectbox to open its dropdown.
3. Try to pick an option with the mouse.

### Expected Behavior

The dropdown option list appears on top of the dialog, and clicking an option selects it (as it does for a selectbox outside a dialog).

### Current Behavior

The dropdown is painted **behind** the dialog, so the options are hidden, and mouse clicks land on the dialog's other widgets instead of the options. The selection does not change. Selecting with the keyboard (Arrow keys + Enter) does work.

Root cause is a stacking-order/z-index mismatch:

- The dropdown `[data-testid="stSelectboxVirtualDropdown"]` is portaled to `<body>` with `z-index: 100000`.
- `st.dialog` (`[data-testid="stDialog"]`) renders at `z-index: 1000060`.

Because the dialog's z-index is higher, it (and its child widgets) paint over the dropdown. Confirmed via `document.elementFromPoint()` over an open option's center — it returns the `stSelectbox` element above it, not the option, so the option never receives the click.

Workaround (lifts the dropdown above the dialog):

```python
st.markdown(
    "<style>[data-testid='stSelectboxVirtualDropdown']{z-index:1000070!important}</style>",
    unsafe_allow_html=True,
)
```

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

Appears tied to the migration away from BaseWeb for `st.selectbox` (#15438), which introduced `stSelectboxVirtualDropdown`. The previous BaseWeb popover layered correctly inside dialogs.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.58.1.dev20260610
- Python version: 3.11.11
- Operating System: macOS 26.5
- Browser: Chrome

### Additional Information

- Affects every `st.selectbox` inside an `st.dialog` (the more fields below the selectbox, the more obviously the options are covered).
- Likely related component change: #15438 ("Remove `BaseWeb` for `selectbox`").
- Possibly related dialog/popover layering reports: #13633, #13859.

title: server side rendering
body:
### Problem

I'm always frustrated when streamlit takes 2 minutes to just load static content on a page.

### Solution

**MVP:** What's the smallest possible solution that would get 80% of the problem out of the way?

Do an initial static render of the HTML on the server side, and send that to browser. Then Load javascript & connect via websocket lazily.


### Additional context

I built https://gooey.ai/explore completely using streamlit. I love that streamlit allows us to iterate fast, but also at the same time seeing a lot of frustrated users when the initial page load times are slow. Plus, the google SEO stuff also gets hurt because everything has to be loaded via a websocket.

I also don't mind taking a shot at the MVP if someone can throw ideas at me around how this can be done
